name: Roof
description: The top building enclosure that provides weather protection and thermal insulation, typically sloped or flat and supported by the roof structure.

name: Wall
description: Vertical building enclosure element that divides spaces, provides structural support, and offers thermal/acoustic insulation and weather resistance.

name: Foundation
description: The lowest load-bearing part of a building that transfers structural loads to the ground, including footings, piles, and raft slabs.

name: Beam
description: A horizontal structural member that primarily resists bending and shear forces, transferring loads from slabs and walls to columns or walls.

name: Column
description: A vertical structural member that primarily carries compressive loads from beams and slabs down to the foundation.

name: Slab
description: A flat horizontal structural element that forms floors and ceilings, transferring live and dead loads to beams and columns.

name: Window
description: A glazed opening in the building envelope that admits natural light and ventilation while providing thermal and acoustic insulation.

name: Door
description: A movable barrier in an opening that provides access between spaces while offering security, fire resistance, and acoustic separation.

name: Curtain Wall
description: A non-structural external wall system of lightweight framed glazing that clads the building face and resists wind loads.

name: Stair
description: A series of steps and landings providing vertical circulation between floors, including treads, risers, stringers, and handrails.

name: Ramp
description: An inclined surface providing wheelchair-accessible vertical circulation between different floor levels.

name: Ceiling
description: The overhead interior surface that conceals services, provides acoustic treatment, and supports light fixtures.

name: Partition
description: A non-load-bearing interior wall that subdivides floor space into rooms or zones.

name: HVAC System
description: Heating, ventilation, and air conditioning system that maintains indoor thermal comfort and air quality through ductwork, diffusers, chillers, boilers, and air handling units.

name: Plumbing System
description: The network of pipes, fixtures, and fittings that supplies potable water and removes wastewater, including hot water heaters and traps.

name: Electrical System
description: The distribution network for electrical power including switchboards, cables, conduits, outlets, switches, and light fixtures.

name: Fire Suppression System
description: Active fire protection system including sprinkler heads, piping, pumps, alarms, and control valves that detects and extinguishes fires.

name: Lift/Elevator System
description: Vertical transportation system consisting of a car, counterweights, guide rails, cables, and machine room equipment for moving between floors.

name: Escalator
description: A powered moving stairway that transports people continuously between building levels.

name: Lighting System
description: The building-integrated artificial lighting network including luminaires, emergency exit signs, controls, and dimming systems.

name: Fire Detection and Alarm System
description: Life safety system comprising smoke detectors, heat detectors, manual call points, alarm bells, and a central control panel.

name: Security System
description: Building access control and surveillance system including CCTV cameras, card readers, intercoms, and alarm monitoring equipment.

name: Building Management System (BMS)
description: A centralized computerized control system that monitors and manages building services including HVAC, lighting, and energy consumption.

name: Structural Framing System
description: The primary load-bearing skeleton of the building composed of beams, columns, bracing, and connections.

name: Corridor
description: A long narrow passageway that provides horizontal circulation and access to adjacent rooms and spaces.

name: Stairwell
description: A fire-rated vertical enclosure containing a stair, providing protected means of egress between floors.

name: Plant Room
description: A dedicated mechanical space housing building services equipment such as boilers, chillers, pumps, and air handling units.

name: Car Park
description: A parking area within or attached to the building for vehicle storage, typically with ramps and marked bays.

name: Office
description: A room or area designed for administrative or professional work, typically furnished with desks and workstations.

name: Toilet/Restroom
description: A sanitary space equipped with water closets, urinals, washbasins, and associated plumbing fixtures.

name: Lobby
description: A transitional entrance space that provides access to the building's interior, often with reception and waiting areas.

name: Atrium
description: A large multi-storey open space within a building, often topped by a skylight, providing light and visual connection.

name: Auditorium
description: A large room designed for audience seating and performances, with tiered or fixed seating and acoustic treatment.

name: Reception Area
description: The formal entrance and greeting zone in a building, often featuring a built-in reception desk and visitor seating.

name: Break Room/Kitchenette
description: A staff amenity space with built-in counters, sink, cabinets, and sometimes a microwave or refrigerator.

name: Meeting/Conference Room
description: A room equipped with tables and built-in AV systems for group discussions and presentations.

name: Server/IT Room
description: A climate-controlled secure room housing building-integrated computer servers, network equipment, and rack systems.

name: Concrete
description: A composite construction material of cement, aggregates, and water that hardens to form strong structural elements.

name: Timber
description: Wood used as a structural or finish material in the form of dimensional lumber, glulam, or cross-laminated timber.

name: Structural Steel
description: Rolled steel sections (I-beams, channels, angles) used for beams, columns, and bracing in the structural frame.

name: Glass
description: A transparent or translucent material used in windows, curtain walls, and glazed partitions, available as annealed, tempered, or laminated sheets.

name: Insulation
description: Thermal and/or acoustic material such as fiberglass, mineral wool, or foam board installed within walls, roofs, and floors.

name: Waterproof Membrane
description: A sheet or liquid-applied barrier that prevents water penetration through roofs, foundations, basements, and wet areas.

name: Brick
description: A fired clay masonry unit laid with mortar to form walls, veneers, and paving.

name: Concrete Block/CMU
description: A preformed concrete masonry unit used for load-bearing and partition walls.

name: Rebar (Reinforcing Steel)
description: Steel bars embedded in concrete to resist tensile stresses and provide structural reinforcement.

name: Gypsum Board/Drywall
description: A factory-made panel of gypsum plaster sandwiched between paper facers, used for interior walls and ceilings.

name: Mortar
description: A workable paste of cement, lime, sand, and water used to bond masonry units and seal joints.

name: Adhesive/Sealant
description: A bonding or sealing compound applied at joints and interfaces to ensure watertightness and structural adhesion.

name: Roofing Membrane
description: A weatherproof sheet material (e.g., PVC, TPO, modified bitumen) applied as the top layer of a flat or low-slope roof.

name: Acoustic Panel
description: A sound-absorbing panel installed on walls or ceilings to reduce reverberation and control noise.

name: Floor Finish
description: The visible walking surface material such as tile, carpet, vinyl, terrazzo, or hardwood adhered to the structural slab.

name: Waterproofing
description: The on-site application of waterproof membranes or coatings to roofs, basements, and wet areas to prevent water ingress.

name: Formwork Installation
description: The on-site assembly of temporary molds (timber or metal) to shape and support wet concrete until it hardens.

name: Formwork Removal/Striking
description: The on-site dismantling and removal of formwork after the concrete has achieved sufficient strength.

name: Concrete Pouring
description: The on-site placement of fresh concrete into prepared formwork, including transport via pump or bucket and compaction by vibration.

name: Curing
description: The on-site maintenance of adequate moisture and temperature in freshly placed concrete to ensure proper hydration and strength gain.

name: Finishing (Concrete)
description: The on-site smoothing, levelling, and texturing of fresh concrete surfaces using trowels and floats to achieve the specified floor finish.

name: Glazing
description: The on-site installation of glass panes into window frames, curtain wall systems, or partition framing.

name: Painting
description: The on-site application of primer and paint coatings to interior and exterior surfaces for decoration and protection.

name: Testing and Commissioning
description: The on-site verification, adjustment, and performance testing of building systems (HVAC, electrical, fire, plumbing) to ensure they operate as designed.

name: Rebar Fixing/Reinforcement Installation
description: The on-site cutting, bending, tying, and placing of reinforcing steel bars within formwork prior to concrete pouring.

name: Masonry/Bricklaying
description: The on-site laying of bricks or blocks with mortar to construct walls, partitions, and veneers.

name: Plastering
description: The on-site application of plaster coats to walls and ceilings to create a smooth finish ready for painting or tiling.

name: Tile Installation
description: The on-site fixing of ceramic, stone, or porcelain tiles to floors and walls using adhesive and grout.

name: Ductwork Installation
description: The on-site assembly and mounting of sheet metal ducts and fittings for air distribution in the HVAC system.

name: Pipework Installation
description: The on-site cutting, joining, and fixing of pipes for plumbing, heating, and fire suppression systems.

name: Electrical Cabling and Wiring
description: The on-site pulling, routing, and termination of electrical cables through conduits and cable trays.

name: Fire Sprinkler Installation
description: The on-site mounting of sprinkler heads, piping, and control valves within ceilings and walls.

name: Drywall Installation
description: The on-site fixing of gypsum boards to metal or timber studs to form interior wall and ceiling linings.

name: Taping and Jointing
description: The on-site application of joint compound and tape over drywall joints to create a seamless surface ready for painting.

name: Insulation Installation
description: The on-site placement of thermal or acoustic insulation material within wall cavities, roof spaces, and floor assemblies.

name: Floor Screeding
description: The on-site application of a levelling layer of sand-cement mortar over the structural slab to receive floor finishes.

name: Roofing Installation
description: The on-site laying of roofing membranes, tiles, or sheets over the roof deck to provide weatherproofing.

name: Window and Door Installation
description: The on-site fixing, sealing, and adjusting of window and door frames and sashes into prepared openings.

name: Lift Installation
description: The on-site assembly and installation of lift cars, guide rails, doors, and machinery within the lift shaft.

name: Fixed Seating Installation
description: The on-site mounting and securing of auditorium or stadium seating to the structural floor.

name: Built-in Millwork/Cabinetry Installation
description: The on-site fitting and fixing of custom-built cabinets, reception desks, and built-in benches.

name: Earthwork/Excavation
description: The on-site excavation and removal of soil to required depths for foundations, basements, and utility trenches.

name: Backfilling and Compaction
description: The on-site placement and compaction of soil or granular material around foundations and below slabs.

name: Scaffolding Erection
description: The on-site assembly of temporary scaffold structures to provide access for workers at height during construction.

name: Scaffolding Dismantling
description: The on-site systematic removal of scaffolding after all trades have completed their work at height.

name: Landscaping (Building-Integrated)
description: The on-site planting and installation of green roof systems, planters, and building-integrated vegetation.

Roof Structure
description: The primary load-bearing framework of the roof, including rafters, trusses, purlins, and beams that transfer loads to walls or columns.

name: Roof Decking
description: The rigid surface layer laid over the roof structure to provide a base for insulation and waterproofing, typically plywood, OSB, or metal deck.

name: Roof Covering
description: The outermost weatherproof layer of the roof that sheds water and protects the building, including tiles, shingles, metal sheets, or membrane.

name: Roof Insulation
description: Thermal insulation material placed within or above the roof assembly to reduce heat transfer through the roof.

name: Roof Underlayment
description: A water-resistant or waterproof barrier installed between the roof deck and the roof covering to provide secondary moisture protection.

name: Roof Flashing
description: Thin metal or waterproof strips installed at roof junctions, valleys, vents, and penetrations to prevent water ingress.

name: Roof Drainage System
description: The network of gutters, downpipes, scuppers, and internal drains that collect and convey rainwater from the roof surface.

name: Roof Edge Trim & Fascia
description: The finished board or metal trim along the roof perimeter that encloses the roof edge and supports the gutter system.

name: Roof Ventilation
description: Passive or mechanical vents, ridge vents, soffit vents, and turbines that allow airflow within the roof assembly to control moisture and temperature.

name: Rooflight / Skylight
description: A glazed aperture set into the roof plane to admit natural daylight into the space below.

name: Roof Curbs & Supports
description: Raised framework on the roof deck used to mount rooftop equipment such as HVAC units, skylights, or exhaust fans.

name: Roof Parapet
description: A low protective wall extending above the roof plane at the building edge, often serving as a fire barrier or architectural feature.

name: Roof Access Hatch
description: A hinged or sliding opening in the roof deck providing access to the roof surface for maintenance and inspection.

name: Green Roof System
description: A layered roof assembly designed to support vegetation, including a waterproof membrane, drainage layer, growing medium, and plantings.

name: Roof Snow Guard / Snow Fence
description: Devices installed on sloped roofs to prevent accumulated snow or ice from sliding off in large sheets.

name: Roof Installation Activity
description: On-site construction activities including framing the roof structure, installing decking, laying underlayment, applying covering, and integrating flashings.

name: Roof Waterproofing Activity
description: On-site application of liquid or sheet waterproofing membranes, torch-on felt, or sealants to achieve a watertight roof assembly.

name: Roof Insulation Installation
description: On-site placement and securing of thermal insulation boards, batts, or spray foam within the roof assembly.

name: Gutter & Downpipe Installation
description: On-site fixing of gutter channels, downpipes, and fittings to the roof edge to establish the rainwater drainage system.

name: Skylight / Rooflight Installation
description: On-site fitting, glazing, and sealing of skylight or rooflight units into prepared roof openings.

name: Eaves & Soffit Installation
description: On-site assembly and fixing of eaves components, soffit boards, and ventilation strips at the roof overhang.

name: Load-Bearing Wall
description: A structural wall that supports vertical loads from floors, roofs, or other building elements above.

name: Non-Load-Bearing Wall
description: A partition wall that does not carry structural loads and serves only to divide interior space.

name: Retaining Wall
description: A wall designed to resist lateral pressure of soil, water, or other materials on the building perimeter.

name: Cavity Wall
description: A wall consisting of two leaves (wythes) with a gap between them, often filled with insulation.

name: Shear Wall
description: A rigid vertical wall designed to resist lateral forces such as wind and seismic loads.

name: Party Wall
description: A shared wall that separates two adjoining buildings or units, often with fire-resistance requirements.

name: Firewall
description: A fire-rated wall that subdivides a building to resist the spread of fire between compartments.

name: Veneer Wall
description: A non-structural outer layer of brick, stone, or other material attached to a backing wall for aesthetic or weather protection.

name: Bearing Wall
description: Synonym for load-bearing wall, emphasizing its role in transmitting gravity loads to the foundation.

name: Wall Finishes
description: Surface treatments applied to walls such as paint, plaster, wallpaper, tile, or paneling for protection and appearance.

name: Wall Insulation
description: Thermal or acoustic insulation material placed within or on wall assemblies to control heat flow and sound transmission.

name: Wall Framing
description: The structural skeleton of a wall, typically wood or metal studs, tracks, plates, and bracing.

name: Wall Cladding
description: External weather-resistant skin material applied to wall surfaces such as metal panels, wood siding, or fiber cement.

name: Wall Damp-Proofing
description: Waterproof membranes or coatings applied to walls to prevent moisture penetration from ground or rain.

name: Wall Opening/Window
description: An aperture in a wall that accommodates a window, door, or other fenestration element.

name: Wall Lintel
description: A horizontal structural member spanning an opening in a wall to support the load above.

name: Wall Tie
description: A metal connector joining two leaves of a cavity wall to ensure they act as a composite unit.

name: Wall Footer/Foundation Wall
description: The below-grade portion of a wall that transfers loads to the ground or a spread footing.

name: Wall Construction
description: On-site erection, alignment, bracing, and securing of wall framing, sheathing, and finishes.

name: Wall Waterproofing Installation
description: Application of liquid or sheet waterproofing membranes to below-grade or exposed walls.

name: Wall Insulation Installation
description: Placement of batt, rigid board, spray foam, or blown-in insulation within wall cavities.

name: Wall Cladding Installation
description: Attachment of exterior wall cladding materials including metal panels, brick veneer, or siding.

name: Wall Finishing Application
description: On-site application of paint, plaster, skim coat, or wallcovering to completed wall surfaces.

name: Wall Thermal Break Installation
description: Installation of thermal break materials at wall penetrations or junctions to reduce thermal bridging.

name: Strip Footing
description: A continuous linear footing that supports load-bearing walls and distributes their load to the soil.

name: Isolated Pad Footing
description: A square or rectangular footing supporting a single column and spreading its concentrated load to the ground.

name: Combined Footing
description: A footing supporting two or more columns, used when individual pad footings would overlap or be eccentrically loaded.

name: Raft Foundation / Mat Foundation
description: A large continuous concrete slab that supports the entire building and distributes loads over a wide area on soft soils.

name: Pile Foundation
description: Deep foundation system of long slender columns (piles) transferring building loads through weak soil to stronger strata below.

name: Pile Cap
description: A reinforced concrete block cast on top of a group of piles to distribute column or wall loads evenly to the piles.

name: Grade Beam
description: A reinforced concrete beam at grade level that connects pile caps or footings and distributes loads from the superstructure.

name: Foundation Wall
description: A load-bearing wall below grade that transfers loads from the superstructure to the footing and resists lateral earth pressure.

name: Slab-on-Grade
description: A concrete slab placed directly on the ground at the lowest floor level, serving as both foundation and floor surface.

name: Crawlspace Foundation
description: A shallow foundation system that elevates the building slightly above grade with a partial-height accessible void beneath the floor.

name: Basement Foundation
description: A deep foundation system with full-height below-grade walls and a slab floor creating habitable or service space underground.

name: Pier Foundation
description: A vertical structural member (drilled shaft or caisson) that transfers deep foundation loads through soil to a bearing stratum.

name: Foundation Drainage System
description: A perimeter drainage assembly of perforated pipes, gravel, and filter fabric installed at the base of foundations to divert groundwater.

name: Waterproofing Membrane
description: A liquid-applied or sheet-applied barrier coating on foundation walls and slabs to prevent moisture intrusion from the surrounding soil.

name: Dampproofing Coating
description: A bituminous or cementitious coating applied to below-grade walls to resist capillary moisture migration without stopping hydrostatic pressure.

name: Subgrade Base Course
description: A compacted layer of granular fill placed beneath a slab-on-grade or footing to provide uniform support and drainage.

name: Foundation Excavation
description: The on-site earthwork of digging trenches or pits to the required depth and width for foundation installation.

name: Reinforcement Placement
description: The on-site positioning, tying, and securing of steel reinforcing bars within foundation formwork before concrete is poured.

name: Concrete Pouring & Curing
description: The on-site placement, consolidation, finishing, and curing of concrete in foundation elements to achieve design strength.

name: Waterproofing Application
description: The on-site installation of waterproofing membranes or coatings to foundations walls and slabs before backfilling.

name: Drainage System Installation
description: The on-site placement of perforated drain pipes, gravel, and geotextile fabric around the foundation perimeter.

name: Backfilling & Compaction
description: The on-site placement and mechanical compaction of soil against completed foundation walls to restore grade and provide lateral support.

name: Helical Pier
description: A steel deep foundation element with helical plates welded to a central shaft that is screwed into the ground for light structures.

name: Steel Beam
description: A horizontal structural member made of structural steel, typically I-shaped (universal beam) or H-shaped, used for load-bearing spanning in steel-framed construction.

name: Reinforced Concrete Beam
description: A cast-in-place or precast concrete beam with embedded steel reinforcement, used for spanning openings and transferring loads to columns or walls.

name: Timber Beam
description: A horizontal load-bearing member fabricated from solid sawn lumber or engineered wood (such as LVL or glulam), used in timber-framed structures.

name: Composite Beam
description: A beam that combines steel and concrete (typically via shear studs on a steel section with a concrete slab) to act as a single structural unit for greater load capacity.

name: Precast Prestressed Beam
description: A factory-manufactured concrete beam with tensioned steel tendons, used in bridges and large-span building structures for reduced deflection and cracking.

name: Lintel Beam
description: A short beam spanning above door, window, or other openings in masonry walls to support the wall above the opening.

name: Tie Beam
description: A horizontal beam connecting two columns or walls, primarily acting in tension to hold structural elements together and resist lateral forces.

name: Ring Beam / Plinth Beam
description: A continuous beam at foundation or floor level that distributes loads from walls to the foundation and provides lateral stability.

name: Spandrel Beam
description: A beam along the exterior perimeter of a building at each floor level, supporting the facade and floor slab edge while transferring gravity loads.

name: Transfer Beam
description: A deep beam that transfers loads from upper-level columns or walls to lower-level columns or foundations where the structural grid changes below.

name: Cantilever Beam
description: A beam that projects horizontally beyond its last support point, fixed at one end and free at the other, used for balconies, canopies, and overhangs.

name: Edge Beam
description: A perimeter beam at the edge of a floor slab that stiffens the slab edge, supports cladding, and helps distribute edge loads.

name: Beam Formwork Installation
description: On-site assembly and erection of shuttering, molds, and falsework to shape and support wet concrete during beam casting.

name: Beam Reinforcement Placement
description: On-site cutting, bending, tying, and positioning of steel rebar cages within beam formwork prior to concrete pouring.

name: Beam Concrete Pouring
description: On-site placement, consolidation, and finishing of concrete into beam formwork, followed by controlled curing to achieve design strength.

name: Steel Beam Erection
description: On-site hoisting, alignment, temporary bracing, and bolting or welding of steel beams onto columns or other supports.

name: Beam-to-Column Connection Installation
description: On-site bolting, welding, or grouting of connections between beams and columns, including shear tabs, end plates, and moment connections.

name: Beam Fireproofing Application
description: On-site spray-applied fire-resistive material, intumescent coating, or encasement board installation to provide the required fire rating to beams.

name: Beam Cambering
description: On-site pre-stressing or fabrication-introduced upward curvature in a steel or precast beam to counteract expected deflection under load.

name: Beam Embed Plate Installation
description: On-site setting of steel embed plates and anchors into beam surfaces for attachment of suspended ceilings, mechanical systems, or facade elements.

name: Structural Column
description: A vertical load-bearing member that transfers compressive forces from beams, slabs, or roof structures down to the foundation.

name: Decorative Column
description: A non-structural column used for aesthetic purposes, architectural expression, or to visually define interior or exterior spaces.

name: Steel Column
description: A column fabricated from structural steel shapes such as H-sections, I-sections, or hollow sections, common in steel-framed buildings.

name: Reinforced Concrete Column
description: A column cast from concrete with embedded steel reinforcement bars to resist both compressive and tensile forces.

name: Timber Column
description: A column made from solid sawn timber, glue-laminated timber (glulam), or engineered wood products.

name: Composite Column
description: A column combining steel and concrete (e.g., concrete-filled steel tube or steel-encased concrete) to optimize structural performance.

name: Masonry Column
description: A column built from bricks, concrete blocks, or stone units bonded with mortar.

name: Column Base Plate
description: A steel plate at the bottom of a column that distributes the column load to the foundation or supporting structure.

name: Column Capital
description: The widened top portion of a column that distributes and transfers loads from beams or slabs above into the column shaft.

name: Column Fireproofing
description: Applied fire-resistive material, such as spray-applied fire-resistive material (SFRM) or intumescent coating, protecting the column from fire.

name: Column Formwork
description: Temporary molds or shuttering used to shape and support wet concrete during the casting of a concrete column.

name: Column Reinforcement Cage
description: The assembled framework of longitudinal rebars and transverse ties or spirals placed inside column formwork before concrete pour.

name: Column Splice
description: A connection detail used to join two column segments end-to-end, typically in multi-story steel or precast concrete construction.

name: Column Erection Activity
description: On-site hoisting, positioning, plumbing, and temporary bracing of a column into its final location within the building frame.

name: Column Concrete Pour Activity
description: On-site placement and vibration of concrete into column formwork, followed by curing.

name: Column Fireproofing Application Activity
description: On-site spray or trowel application of fire-resistive materials to exposed steel or concrete columns.

name: Column Inspection Activity
description: On-site quality control inspection of column alignment, plumbness, connection integrity, and material condition after installation.

name: Column Cladding Installation Activity
description: On-site installation of architectural column covers, wraps, or cladding panels around a structural column core.

name: Floor Slab
description: The primary horizontal structural member forming the floor level, typically cast-in-place concrete, precast concrete, or composite steel deck.

name: Roof Slab
description: A horizontal or slightly sloped structural slab at the top of the building that supports roof coverings and provides weather protection.

name: Ground/Foundation Slab
description: A slab cast directly on the ground (on-grade) or supported by piles/foundations, serving as the lowest floor of the building.

name: Slab Edge / Spandrel Slab
description: The perimeter edge zone of a floor or roof slab, often thickened or insulated for structural continuity and thermal bridging reduction.

name: Suspended Slab
description: A slab supported by beams, walls, or columns above grade, transferring loads to vertical structural elements below.

name: Precast Hollow-Core Slab
description: A prefabricated prestressed concrete slab unit with longitudinal voids to reduce weight while maintaining structural capacity.

name: Composite Steel Deck Slab
description: A slab system formed by a profiled steel deck with a concrete topping acting compositely for floor spans.

name: Post-Tensioned Slab
description: A concrete slab reinforced with tensioned steel tendons after concrete curing to reduce cracking and allow longer spans.

name: Slab Reinforcement
description: Steel reinforcing bars or mesh embedded in the slab to resist tensile and shear forces.

name: Slab Formwork
description: Temporary moulds and supports used to shape and support wet concrete until it gains sufficient strength.

name: Slab Edge Insulation
description: Perimeter thermal insulation applied to slab edges to reduce heat loss and prevent condensation at the building envelope junction.

name: Slab Vapour Barrier
description: A polyethylene or similar membrane placed beneath a slab-on-grade to prevent moisture migration from the ground.

name: Slab Underside Fireproofing
description: Spray-applied fire-resistive material or intumescent coating on the soffit of a slab to maintain fire-rating integrity.

name: Slab Waterproofing
description: Liquid-applied or sheet membrane systems on exposed slab surfaces to prevent water ingress in wet areas or planters.

name: Slab Pouring / Concreting
description: The on-site placement and consolidation of fresh concrete into slab formwork to create a monolithic structural element.

name: Slab Curing
description: On-site moisture-retention or covering process undertaken after concrete placement to ensure proper hydration and strength development.

name: Slab Striking / Formwork Removal
description: The on-site dismantling and removal of slab formwork and shoring after the concrete has reached required strength.

name: Slab Reinforcement Installation
description: On-site placement, tying, and positioning of rebar or mesh within slab formwork prior to concrete pouring.

name: Slab Post-Tensioning
description: On-site tensioning of steel tendons within the slab after concrete cures to induce compressive stress and control deflection.

name: Slab Cutting / Coring
description: On-site diamond saw cutting or core drilling of existing slabs for openings, penetrations, or demolition.

name: Slab Surface Finishing
description: On-site trowelling, power floating, brooming, or grinding of the slab surface to achieve the specified finish and tolerance.

name: Window Frame
description: The perimeter structure that surrounds and supports the glazing, typically made of wood, aluminum, vinyl, or steel.

name: Window Sash
description: The movable or fixed assembly within the frame that holds the glass panes in place.

name: Window Glazing
description: The glass or transparent panel assembly within the sash, which may be single, double, or triple paned.

name: Window Sill
description: The horizontal ledge at the bottom of the window frame that supports the frame and sheds water.

name: Window Head
description: The top horizontal member of the window frame that transfers loads to the surrounding wall.

name: Window Jamb
description: The vertical side members of the window frame that guide the sash and provide weather sealing.

name: Weatherstripping
description: A sealing material applied between the sash and frame to prevent air and water infiltration.

name: Window Hardware
description: Operable components such as hinges, handles, locks, cranks, and friction stays that enable window operation and security.

name: Window Insect Screen
description: A mesh panel mounted on the frame to exclude insects while allowing ventilation when the window is open.

name: Window Grille/Mullion
description: Decorative or structural vertical/horizontal dividers within the window frame that separate individual glass panels.

name: Casement Window
description: A window variant with side-hinged sashes that swing outward or inward for ventilation.

name: Double-Hung Window
description: A window variant with two vertically sliding sashes that move past each other within the frame.

name: Sliding Window
description: A window variant with one or more sashes that slide horizontally along tracks within the frame.

name: Awning Window
description: A window variant with top-hinged sashes that project outward, allowing ventilation even during rain.

name: Fixed Window
description: A non-operable window variant that provides light and view but does not open.

name: Skylight
description: A window installed on a roof or ceiling plane to admit natural light from above.

name: Bay Window
description: A multi-panel window assembly projecting outward from the building face, consisting of a center fixed unit and angled side casements.

name: Window Installation
description: The on-site process of setting, leveling, anchoring, and sealing window units into prepared rough openings.

name: Window Glazing Installation
description: The activity of setting glass panels into the sash, applying glazing tape or compound, and installing stops.

name: Window Weatherproofing
description: The application of flashing, sealants, and membranes around the window perimeter to prevent water intrusion.

name: Window Hardware Commissioning
description: The adjustment, lubrication, and testing of window operating mechanisms and locking hardware for proper function.

name: Door Leaf
description: The movable panel or panels of the door assembly that swing, slide, or fold to open and close the doorway.

name: Door Frame
description: The stationary structural perimeter surrounding the door opening that supports the door leaf and transfers loads to the surrounding wall.

name: Door Hardware
description: The collective set of mechanical components attached to the door leaf and frame including hinges, handles, locks, latches, and closers.

name: Door Threshold
description: The strip or plate at the bottom of the door opening that seals the gap between the door leaf and the finished floor.

name: Door Sill
description: The horizontal structural member at the base of a door frame that provides a finished transition and often incorporates a threshold.

name: Transom Panel
description: A fixed or operable panel located directly above the door leaf within the same frame assembly, often glazed for borrowed light.

name: Door Glazing
description: The glass panel or panels fitted into an opening within the door leaf, including any integral lites or vision panels.

name: Door Stop
description: The projecting strip or molding attached to the frame or floor that prevents the door leaf from swinging past its intended closed position.

name: Swinging Door
description: A door type where the leaf rotates about vertical hinges, commonly used as the primary operable door in most building entries and interior passages.

name: Sliding Door
description: A door type where the leaf moves horizontally along tracks, used where swing clearance is limited or for wide openings.

name: Folding Door
description: A door type consisting of multiple hinged leaves that fold together when opened, commonly used for closet or room-divider applications.

name: Revolving Door
description: A door system with multiple leaves radiating from a central axis within a cylindrical enclosure, providing continuous passage with minimal air exchange.

name: Automatic Door Operator
description: The electromechanical assembly that powers the opening and closing of a door, including actuators, sensors, and control logic.

name: Fire Door Assembly
description: A rated door-and-frame combination engineered to resist fire and smoke passage for a specified duration as required by building codes.

name: Door Closer
description: A mechanical or hydraulic device mounted to the door leaf and frame that automatically closes the door after it has been opened.

name: Door Lockset
description: The complete locking mechanism installed in the door leaf and strike plate, including the latch, deadbolt, key cylinder, and trim.

name: Door Hinge
description: The pivot hardware connecting the door leaf to the frame that allows rotational movement along the hinge stile.

name: Kickplate
description: A protective metal or plastic plate applied to the lower portion of the door leaf to resist scuffs, impacts, and abrasion.

name: Door Frame Anchors
description: Metal ties or brackets embedded in the surrounding wall construction that secure the door frame to the masonry, stud, or concrete structure.

name: Door Installation
description: The on-site process of setting, plumbing, and fastening the door frame into the rough opening and hanging the door leaf or leaves.

name: Door Hardware Installation
description: The on-site fitting and adjustment of all door hardware including hinges, locks, closers, pulls, and accessories to the door assembly.

name: Door Weatherproofing
description: The on-site application of weatherstripping, thresholds, perimeter sealants, and gaskets to ensure air and water tightness.

name: Door Commissioning
description: The on-site testing, adjustment, and verification of door operation, automatic operators, latching, and fire-rating integrity.

name: Curtain Wall Frame
description: The primary structural grid of mullions and transoms that supports the curtain wall panels and transfers loads to the building structure.

name: Curtain Wall Glazing Panel
description: The infill panel (glass or other transparent/translucent material) set within the curtain wall frame, providing vision and daylight.

name: Curtain Wall Spandrel Panel
description: An opaque or back-painted infill panel located at floor slab levels to conceal structure and building services.

name: Curtain Wall Gaskets & Glazing Beads
description: The continuous sealing profiles and pressure beads that secure and weatherproof the panels within the frame.

name: Curtain Wall Thermal Break
description: A low-conductivity material inserted in the frame to reduce thermal bridging and improve energy performance.

name: Curtain Wall Anchors & Brackets
description: The metal connections that fix the curtain wall frame to the building's edge slab or structure, allowing for tolerance adjustment.

name: Stick-Built Curtain Wall
description: A curtain wall assembled piece by piece on site from individual mullions, transoms, and infill panels.

name: Unitized Curtain Wall
description: A curtain wall system composed of prefabricated panel units that are lifted and fixed to the building as complete modules.

name: Structural Glazing Curtain Wall
description: A curtain wall where glass panels are bonded to the frame with structural silicone sealant, minimizing visible framing externally.

name: Point-Supported (Spiderman) Curtain Wall
description: A curtain wall in which glass panels are hung from point-fixing bolted connections with minimal framing, creating a fully transparent appearance.

name: Cable-Net Curtain Wall
description: A curtain wall where glass panels are supported by a tensioned stainless steel cable net, often used for large atria.

name: Curtain Wall Installation
description: The on-site process of erecting and fixing the curtain wall frame, installing panels, and sealing joints to the building structure.

name: Curtain Wall Glazing Installation
description: The on-site placement and setting of glass or panel infills into the curtain wall frame with gaskets and pressure beads.

name: Curtain Wall Sealing & Weatherproofing
description: The application of sealants, backer rods, and weather barriers at all joints and penetrations to ensure air and water tightness.

name: Curtain Wall Air Leakage Testing
description: On-site field testing of the installed curtain wall assembly for air infiltration and water penetration performance.

name: Curtain Wall Gasket
description: The elastomeric profile used between frame and panel to provide compression sealing and accommodate movement.

name: Curtain Wall Structural Silicone Sealant
description: A high-strength silicone adhesive used to structurally bond glass to the frame in structural glazing systems.

name: Stair Flight
description: The inclined series of steps between two landings or floors, including the stringers, treads, and risers that form the primary structural and walking surface of the stair.

name: Stair Landing
description: A horizontal platform between flights of stairs providing a resting point, change of direction, or access to floors.

name: Stair Tread
description: The horizontal top surface of each step that is walked upon, typically finished with slip-resistant material.

name: Stair Riser
description: The vertical face between two consecutive treads that closes the step opening and contributes to the stair's structural and fire-safety performance.

name: Stair Stringer
description: The inclined structural member on one or both sides of a stair flight that supports the treads and risers.

name: Stair Nosing
description: The protruding front edge of a stair tread, often reinforced or fitted with a contrasting slip-resistant strip for safety and visibility.

name: Handrail
description: A railing grasped by hand for support and balance, mounted on one or both sides of a stair flight or along a landing.

name: Guardrail / Balustrade
description: A protective barrier system consisting of balusters, newel posts, and a top rail installed along the open sides of stairs and landings to prevent falls.

name: Newel Post
description: The principal vertical post at the start, end, or turn of a stair that anchors the handrail and balustrade.

name: Baluster
description: The vertical spindles or pickets between the handrail and stair stringer or floor that fill the guardrail opening.

name: Stair Underlayment
description: A sound-dampening or leveling layer installed beneath stair finishes such as carpet, tile, or wood on treads and landings.

name: Stair Finish Flooring
description: The applied walking surface on treads and landings, which may be carpet, stone, tile, wood, terrazzo, or resilient sheet/plank.

name: Spiral Stair
description: A stair type that ascends in a helical curve around a central pole or open center, used where space is constrained.

name: Monolithic / Precast Concrete Stair
description: A stair unit cast as a single piece of reinforced concrete either precast off-site or poured in situ, forming integrated treads, risers, and stringers.

name: Metal Pan Stair
description: A stair system fabricated from formed metal pans filled with concrete or other fill material to create the tread surface.

name: Fire Escape Stair
description: An exterior or enclosed stair dedicated to emergency egress, typically constructed of steel with self-closing fire-rated doors at each landing.

name: Stairwell Enclosure
description: The fire-rated vertical shaft or enclosure that contains the stair system, providing smoke protection and structural fire separation between floors.

name: Stair Pressurization System
description: A mechanical smoke-control system that maintains positive air pressure within the stairwell to prevent smoke entry during a fire emergency.

name: Stair Installation
description: On-site assembly, erection, and fastening of prefabricated stair components or cast-in-place concrete stair construction within the building structure.

name: Stair Finish Application
description: Installation of tread and landing finishes, nosing strips, and underlayment on the completed stair structure.

name: Handrail and Guardrail Installation
description: On-site mounting, anchoring, and alignment of handrails, balusters, newel posts, and guardrails to the stair structure and adjacent walls.

name: Stairwell Fire Caulking
description: Application of fire-rated sealants and penetration seals at joints, gaps, and service penetrations within the stairwell enclosure to maintain fire-resistance ratings.

name: Straight Ramp
description: A ramp with a linear, uninterrupted slope, typically the simplest configuration for accessible egress or circulation.

name: Curved Ramp
description: A ramp that follows a curved or arc path, often used in architectural feature stair/ramp combinations or at vehicular roundabouts.

name: Switchback Ramp
description: A ramp with one or more 180-degree turns via intermediate landings, used where a single straight run exceeds maximum slope length.

name: Helical Ramp
description: A ramp that spirals continuously around a central core, common in parking structures and iconic building entries.

name: Folded / Dogleg Ramp
description: A ramp that changes direction at a mid-point landing without a full switchback, forming a Z-shaped or folded plan.

name: Ramp Landing
description: A level platform at the top, bottom, or intermediate point of a ramp providing resting space and direction change.

name: Ramp Handrail
description: A graspable rail or guard mounted beside a ramp run to provide support and fall prevention for users.

name: Ramp Edge Guard / Curb
description: A raised vertical element along the open side(s) of a ramp to prevent wheels from running off the edge.

name: Ramp Slope Transition
description: A carefully graded change in slope at the top and bottom of a ramp run to prevent abrupt grade breaks and tripping.

name: Ramp Surface Finish / Tread
description: The applied walking surface material on a ramp, which may include slip-resistant coatings, textured strips, or tactile warning surfaces.

name: Ramp Drainage Trench
description: A linear drain or gully installed along or across a ramp to collect and convey surface water away from the sloped surface.

name: Vehicle Ramp
description: A ramp designed for vehicular traffic, typically with a steeper slope tolerance and heavier structural capacity than pedestrian ramps.

name: Pedestrian Ramp
description: A ramp designed for foot traffic, complying with accessibility codes for slope, width, handrails, and landings.

name: Loading Dock Ramp / Dock Leveler
description: An adjustable or fixed ramp bridging a loading dock edge and a truck bed to allow equipment and goods transfer.

name: Wheelchair Ramp
description: A ramp specifically configured to meet wheelchair accessibility requirements, including gentle slope, wide clear width, and edge protection.

name: Ramp Reinforcement / Structure
description: The structural framing, slab thickening, or foundation supporting a ramp, ensuring it carries design loads.

name: Ramp Expansion Joint
description: A gap or joint within a ramp structure to accommodate thermal movement and prevent cracking in long or exposed ramp runs.

name: Ramp Lighting
description: Fixed luminaires mounted along or above a ramp to provide safe illumination for nighttime or interior use.

name: Ramp Foundation / Abutment
description: The substructure element at the base of a ramp transferring loads to the ground, often including a retaining wall if cut into grade.

name: Ramp Installation
description: On-site construction activity of forming, placing, and finishing a ramp structure including its reinforcement and surface.

name: Ramp Handrail Installation
description: On-site installation of handrails and guardrails along ramp edges with required brackets, anchors, and joints.

name: Ramp Surface Finishing
description: On-site application of slip-resistant coatings, sealants, or tactile warning strips to the ramp walking surface.

name: Ramp Slope Grading
description: On-site earthwork or concrete screeding activity to achieve the precise design slope ratio of a ramp run.

name: Ramp-to-Stair Combination
description: An integrated circulation system where a ramp and stair run adjacent to or share landings and handrails.

name: Accessible Egress System
description: The network of ramps, level landings, and refuge areas that together form an accessible means of egress from a building.

name: Suspended Ceiling
description: A ceiling hung from the structural floor above using a grid system, typically supporting lightweight tiles or panels.

name: Ceiling Tile
description: Individual modular panels (mineral fibre, metal, wood, or gypsum) laid into or clipped onto a suspended ceiling grid.

name: Ceiling Grid / T-Bar System
description: The metal framing grid of main tees and cross tees that supports and aligns ceiling tiles in a suspended ceiling assembly.

name: Gypsum Board Ceiling
description: A continuous ceiling surface formed by fixing gypsum plasterboard sheets to joists or furring channels and finishing with joint compound.

name: Plaster Ceiling
description: A traditional monolithic ceiling surface created by applying wet plaster onto lath or a masonry substrate.

name: Stretch Ceiling
description: A PVC or fabric membrane clamped into perimeter tracks and tensioned to form a seamless, flat or curved ceiling surface.

name: Metal Ceiling Panel
description: Pre-finished aluminium or steel panels (flat, perforated, or linear) installed on a concealed or exposed grid for acoustic or aesthetic ceilings.

name: Wood Ceiling Panel
description: Solid wood or wood-veneer boards or planks fixed to a subframe to create a warm, textured ceiling finish.

name: Acoustic Ceiling System
description: A ceiling assembly incorporating sound-absorbing panels, baffles, or clouds to reduce reverberation and improve room acoustics.

name: Ceiling Soffit
description: The underside of a structural slab, beam, or stair flight that is finished as a ceiling, often in exposed-concrete or painted form.

name: Coffered Ceiling
description: A decorative ceiling composed of recessed square or rectangular panels (coffers) framed by beams or mouldings.

name: Tray Ceiling
description: A ceiling with a central recessed area stepped up from the surrounding perimeter, creating a layered, architectural effect.

name: Vaulted Ceiling
description: A ceiling following the slope of a roof or formed as an arched shape, often open to the structural rafters or finished with boarding.

name: Cove / Cornice Moulding
description: A decorative plaster, timber, or polymer profile fitted at the junction of wall and ceiling to conceal the transition.

name: Ceiling Access Panel
description: A hinged or removable door set flush into the ceiling finish to allow maintenance access to services above.

name: Ceiling-Mounted Light Fixture
description: A lighting unit attached directly to the ceiling surface or recessed into it, including downlights, pendants, and troffers.

name: Ceiling Diffuser / Grille
description: An air distribution device mounted in or on a ceiling for supply or return of conditioned air from HVAC ductwork.

name: Ceiling Insulation
description: Thermal or acoustic insulation material (batts, boards, or loose-fill) placed above the ceiling membrane within the ceiling plenum.

name: Cable Tray / Conduit (in Ceiling Plenum)
description: Support systems for electrical, data, or control cabling routed through the concealed space between ceiling and structural slab.

name: Fire Damper / Smoke Damper (Ceiling)
description: A fire-rated closure device installed where ductwork penetrates a ceiling fire-resistance rating assembly.

name: Ceiling Cloud / Baffle
description: An independent acoustic panel or array suspended below the main ceiling plane, not forming a full ceiling surface.

name: Metal Linear Ceiling
description: A ceiling system using long, interlocking metal planks or strips in a continuous run, often with concealed clips.

name: Open-Grid / Egg-Crate Ceiling
description: A ceiling formed by a deep grid of interlocking louvers or cells, providing visual screening while allowing air and sprinkler passage.

name: Radiant Ceiling Panel
description: A ceiling-mounted panel containing embedded hydronic tubing or electric elements for heating or cooling by radiation.

name: Ceiling Suspension Hanger / Wire
description: Galvanised steel wire or rod used to hang the ceiling grid from the structural deck above.

name: Furring Channel / Hat Channel
description: A cold-formed steel channel fixed perpendicular to joists or walls to create a level subframe for ceiling board attachment.

name: Ceiling Install (Activity)
description: On-site installation of ceiling framing, board/tile fixing, joint finishing, and integration of lighting and grilles.

name: Ceiling Grid Layout and Assembly (Activity)
description: Setting out, cutting, and assembling the suspended ceiling grid including main tees, cross tees, and wall angles.

name: Ceiling Plenum Inspection and Rough-In (Activity)
description: Coordination and installation of MEP services (ductwork, pipes, cables) in the ceiling void prior to ceiling finish closure.

name: Exposed Ceiling (System)
description: An intentional design where the structural slab, beams, and services are left visible and finished as the ceiling, often painted.

name: Ceiling Plenum
description: The concealed void between the ceiling membrane and the structural floor above, used for routing building services.

name: Solid Partition
description: A rigid, non-load-bearing vertical divider constructed from materials such as brick, block, or concrete masonry units (CMUs), often used for fire separation or acoustic privacy.

name: Stud Partition
description: A framed partition consisting of vertical studs (metal or timber) with board facings, forming a lightweight demountable or permanent internal wall.

name: Demountable Partition
description: A movable or reconfigurable partition system designed for office or commercial interiors, typically with panels and integrated framing.

name: Glazed Partition
description: A partition incorporating glass panels (framed or frameless) to provide visual transparency while dividing interior space.

name: Folding Partition
description: A collapsible partition system consisting of hinged or sliding panels that fold away to open up a large space on demand.

name: Sliding Partition
description: A partition made of sliding door-like panels that move along tracks to subdivide or open a room.

name: Fire-rated Partition
description: A partition assembly specifically designed and tested to resist the passage of fire and maintain compartmentation for a rated duration.

name: Acoustic Partition
description: A partition with enhanced sound insulation properties, often incorporating dense cores, resilient channels, or acoustic sealants.

name: Toilet Cubicle Partition
description: A compact, floor- or ceiling-mounted partition system that creates individual enclosed toilet or changing compartments.

name: Operable Partition
description: A large-scale movable partition system, typically motorized or manually operated, used to subdivide ballrooms, auditoria, or conference halls.

name: Partition Framing
description: The structural skeleton of studs, tracks, noggins, and bracing that supports partition facings.

name: Partition Board
description: Sheet material (e.g., plasterboard, gypsum board, cement board) used to face partition framing.

name: Partition Insulation
description: Thermal or acoustic insulation material installed within the cavity of a stud partition.

name: Partition Furring
description: A system of horizontal or vertical strapping applied to a solid substrate to create a level cavity for partition board installation.

name: Partition Base/Skirting
description: The trim or baseboard installed at the junction between partition face and floor finish.

name: Partition Head Detail
description: The top connection between a partition and the structural soffit or ceiling, including deflection heads and acoustic seals.

name: Partition Installation
description: On-site erection, alignment, fixing, and finishing of partition framing, boards, and associated linings.

name: Partition Fire Stopping Installation
description: Installation of fire-resistant seals, intumescent collars, or firestop pillows at penetrations and partition perimeters.

name: Partition Acoustic Sealing
description: Application of acoustic caulks, gaskets, and resilient seals at partition joints, base, and penetrations.

name: Air Handling Unit (AHU)
description: A factory-made assembly that conditions and circulates air, typically containing a fan, heating/cooling coils, filters, and dampers.

name: Fan Coil Unit (FCU)
description: A terminal unit with a fan and heat exchanger that heats or cools the air in a local zone.

name: Variable Air Volume (VAV) Box
description: A terminal device that regulates the volume of conditioned air delivered to a zone in response to temperature demands.

name: Chiller
description: A refrigeration machine that removes heat from a liquid coolant for use in cooling coils or fan coil units.

name: Boiler
description: A pressurized vessel that heats water or generates steam for hydronic heating systems.

name: Heat Pump
description: A reversible refrigeration device that transfers heat between indoor and outdoor air or ground for both heating and cooling.

name: Ductwork
description: A network of metal, fiberglass, or flexible conduits that distributes conditioned air throughout the building.

name: Diffuser / Grille / Register
description: Air distribution outlets and inlets mounted in ceilings, walls, or floors that direct airflow into or out of spaces.

name: Thermostat / Zone Controller
description: A sensing and control device that maintains setpoint temperature by signaling HVAC equipment to operate or modulate.

name: Building Management System (BMS) Controller
description: A digital controller that monitors and orchestrates HVAC equipment operation, scheduling, and alarms across the facility.

name: Expansion Tank
description: A vessel that absorbs pressure fluctuations in a closed hydronic loop caused by thermal expansion of water.

name: Pump (Hydronic)
description: A mechanical device that circulates hot or chilled water through piping loops to terminal units.

name: Condenser Coil
description: An outdoor heat exchanger that rejects heat from refrigerant to ambient air or a cooling tower loop.

name: Cooling Tower
description: A heat rejection device that dissipates waste heat from a chiller by evaporating a portion of recirculated water.

name: Air Filter
description: A replaceable media device that removes particulates from the airstream to protect equipment and indoor air quality.

name: Damper (Fire / Smoke / Volume)
description: A movable blade assembly within ductwork that regulates airflow or closes automatically in fire or smoke conditions.

name: Humidifier / Dehumidifier
description: A device that adds or removes moisture from the airstream to maintain target relative humidity levels.

name: Ventilation Air Intake / Exhaust Louver
description: A weather-protected opening in the building envelope through which outdoor air enters or indoor air is expelled.

name: Energy Recovery Wheel (ERV/HRV)
description: A rotary heat exchanger that transfers sensible and latent energy between exhaust and supply airstreams to improve efficiency.

name: Refrigerant Piping
description: Copper or steel tubing that carries refrigerant between the compressor, condenser, and evaporator sections.

name: Variable Refrigerant Flow (VRF) System
description: A multi-split heat pump system that varies refrigerant flow to multiple indoor fan coil units for simultaneous heating and cooling in different zones.

name: Dedicated Outdoor Air System (DOAS)
description: A separate ventilation system that conditions 100% outdoor air and delivers it independently of the zone-level heating/cooling units.

name: Packaged Rooftop Unit (RTU)
description: A self-contained heating and cooling unit mounted on the roof that contains all components in a single weatherproof enclosure.

name: Underfloor Air Distribution (UFAD) Plenum
description: A pressurized cavity beneath a raised access floor that supplies conditioned air through floor diffusers directly to the occupied zone.

name: Mechanical Room / Plant Room
description: A dedicated building space housing major HVAC equipment such as chillers, boilers, pumps, and air handlers.

name: Install & Commission Ductwork
description: The on-site assembly, sealing, support, and testing of supply, return, and exhaust duct sections.

name: Install Air Handling Unit
description: The rigging, placement, leveling, and connection of the AHU to ductwork, piping, electrical, and controls.

name: Install Terminal Units (FCU/VAV/VRF Indoor)
description: Mounting, piping, ducting, and wiring fan coil units, VAV boxes, or VRF indoor units in ceilings or zones.

name: Install Chiller & Cooling Tower
description: Setting the chiller and cooling tower on foundations, piping refrigerant and water loops, and connecting power.

name: Install Boiler & Hydronic Piping
description: Placing the boiler, connecting flue, fuel supply, water piping, expansion tanks, pumps, and safety valves.

name: Install Controls & BMS Wiring
description: Running low-voltage control cables, mounting sensors and thermostats, and programming the building management system controllers.

name: Air Balancing & System Commissioning
description: Measuring and adjusting airflow, water flow, and control sequences to verify that all HVAC zones meet design performance specifications.

name: Install Duct Insulation
description: Applying thermal and acoustic insulation wrap to ductwork to reduce heat loss and condensation.

name: Water Supply System
description: Pressurized piping network that delivers potable cold and hot water from the main supply to fixtures and equipment throughout the building.

name: Drainage and Vent System
description: Gravity-driven waste and vent piping network that removes used water and sewage from fixtures while maintaining proper air pressure in the drainage stack.

name: Stormwater Drainage System
description: Piping and components that collect and convey rainwater from roof drains, scuppers, and area drains to the building's stormwater disposal system.

name: Plumbing Fixtures
description: Water-using devices such as water closets, urinals, lavatories, sinks, bathtubs, showers, and service sinks that are permanently connected to the water supply and drainage systems.

name: Water Heaters
description: Tank-type or tankless heating devices that supply domestic hot water to fixtures and appliances through the hot water distribution piping.

name: Pumps
description: Mechanical devices including booster pumps, circulation pumps, sump pumps, and sewage ejector pumps that move water or waste within the plumbing system.

name: Valves
description: Flow-control devices such as gate valves, globe valves, check valves, pressure-reducing valves, and balancing valves installed on piping for isolation, regulation, and backflow prevention.

name: Piping and Fittings
description: Pipe segments made of copper, PVC, PEX, cast iron, or steel along with elbows, tees, couplings, and adapters that form the water supply and drainage conveyance network.

name: Backflow Prevention Devices
description: Assemblies such as reduced-pressure zone backflow preventers, double-check valves, and vacuum breakers that protect the potable water supply from contamination.

name: Natural Gas Piping System
description: Black steel or CSST piping network that delivers natural gas from the utility meter to gas-fired appliances and equipment within the building.

name: Compressed Air System
description: Piping, compressors, receivers, and dryers that supply compressed air for building mechanical controls, lab equipment, or industrial processes.

name: Medical Gas System
description: Dedicated piping network supplying oxygen, nitrous oxide, medical air, and vacuum to outlets in healthcare facility headwalls and patient care areas.

name: Fire Standpipe System
description: Vertical piping with hose connections at each floor that provides firefighting water supply for manual fire suppression by building occupants or firefighters.

name: Plumbing Rough-In Installation
description: On-site installation of concealed water supply and drainage piping within walls, floors, and ceilings before wall finishes are applied.

name: Plumbing Trim-Out Installation
description: On-site installation of exposed plumbing fixtures, faucets, trim plates, flush valves, and trap assemblies after wall finishes are complete.

name: Water Heater Installation
description: On-site placement, connection, and commissioning of gas or electric water heaters including temperature and pressure relief valves and vent connections.

name: Plumbing Pressure Testing
description: On-site hydrostatic or air pressure testing of installed water supply and drainage piping to verify leak-free joints before concealing pipes in building assemblies.

name: Conductor & Cable System
description: The assembly of insulated copper/aluminum conductors, cables, and wiring that distribute electrical power throughout the building.

name: Conduit & Raceway System
description: The protective tubing, pipes, and channels that enclose and route electrical wiring through the building fabric.

name: Cable Tray & Ladder System
description: Structural support assemblies used to carry cables and wiring above ceilings, in risers, or in service corridors.

name: Distribution Board (Panelboard)
description: Enclosed panel containing circuit breakers or fuses that distributes incoming power to branch circuits throughout the building.

name: Main Switchboard
description: The primary electrical panel receiving utility power and housing main protective devices, metering, and busbars for building distribution.

name: Sub-Distribution Board
description: Secondary distribution panel that serves a specific zone, floor, or wing of the building.

name: Circuit Breaker & Fuse Assembly
description: Overcurrent protection devices mounted within distribution boards or standalone enclosures that safeguard circuits from faults.

name: Metering & Monitoring Equipment
description: Utility meters, sub-meters, and energy monitoring devices that measure power consumption within the building.

name: Earthing & Grounding System
description: The network of ground rods, grounding conductors, and bonding connections that safely dissipates fault currents to earth.

name: Lightning Protection System
description: Air terminals, down conductors, and earth electrodes that intercept and safely conduct lightning strikes to ground.

name: Switch & Socket Outlet
description: Wall-mounted or floor-mounted devices providing user-accessible power points and lighting control switches.

name: Cable Tray Installation
description: On-site assembly, mounting, and securing of cable tray runs along structural supports, ceilings, and walls.

name: Conduit Installation
description: Cutting, threading, bending, and fixing of conduit runs within wall chases, slabs, and ceiling voids.

name: Cable Pulling & Termination
description: On-site pulling of cables through conduits or trays and terminating them at panels, outlets, and equipment.

name: Distribution Board Installation & Commissioning
description: Mounting, wiring, and testing of panelboards including breaker installation, busbar connection, and circuit verification.

name: Earthing System Installation
description: Driving ground rods, laying grounding conductors, and bonding all metallic services and structural steel to the earth electrode.

name: Hypothetical: Fire Alarm System
description: Electrically powered detection and notification system that is closely related but typically modeled as a separate discipline system.

name: Hypothetical: Emergency Lighting System
description: Battery-backed or generator-backed lighting that activates upon mains failure, closely related but tracked as a separate life-safety system.

name: Hypothetical: Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) System
description: Battery-based backup power system providing conditioned, uninterrupted power to critical building loads.

name: Hypothetical: Standby Generator System
description: Engine-driven generator and associated transfer switch providing emergency/standby power to the building.

name: HVAC Power Connection
description: Dedicated electrical supply wiring, disconnects, and controls serving HVAC equipment such as chillers, AHUs, and pumps.

name: Power Busway & Bus Duct
description: Prefabricated grounded metal-enclosed busbar system used for high-current distribution in risers or data centers.

name: Transformers (Step-down)
description: Dry-type or oil-filled transformers that reduce utility voltage to building utilization voltage levels.

name: Electrical Room / Closet
description: Dedicated enclosed space housing switchboards, panelboards, metering, and other electrical equipment within the building.

name: Cable Management Accessories
description: Cable ties, saddles, cleats, grommets, firestop sleeves, and identification tags used to organize and protect wiring.

name: Conduit Bending & Fabrication (on-site)
description: On-site bending, cutting, and threading of conduit to fit building geometry before installation.

name: Switch & Socket Installation
description: Mounting wiring devices into back boxes, connecting conductors, and fixing faceplates at final fit-out stage.

name: Lighting Fixture Connection
description: On-site wiring, suspension, or recess-mounting of luminaires including emergency test and commissioning.

name: System Testing & Commissioning
description: Insulation resistance testing, continuity checks, polarity verification, and loop impedance measurements of the complete installation.

name: Fire Suppression Control Panel
description: The central control unit that monitors fire detection inputs and activates suppression system components.

name: Fire Suppression Piping Network
description: The distribution piping that conveys fire suppressant agent from the storage to discharge points throughout the building.

name: Sprinkler Head
description: A thermally-activated discharge device that releases water or other suppressant when a preset temperature is reached.

name: Fire Suppression Agent Storage Tank
description: A pressurized vessel that stores water, foam, or chemical suppressant for release into the piping network.

name: Dry Pipe Valve
description: A valve that holds back water in a dry-pipe sprinkler system until a sprinkler head opens and releases air pressure.

name: Flow Switch
description: A device that detects water flow in the suppression piping and sends a signal to the control panel.

name: Tamper Switch
description: A monitoring device attached to a control valve that alerts when the valve is partially or fully closed.

name: Fire Suppression Zone Valve
description: A sectional control valve that isolates a specific zone of the suppression system for maintenance or testing.

name: Clean Agent Suppression System
description: A gaseous fire suppression system using chemical agents such as FM-200 or Novec 1230 for protecting sensitive equipment spaces.

name: Water Mist Suppression System
description: A suppression system that discharges fine water droplets to extinguish fires with minimal water damage.

name: Foam Suppression System
description: A fire suppression system that discharges foam concentrate mixed with water to smother flammable liquid fires.

name: Kitchen Hood Suppression System
description: A dedicated wet-chemical suppression system installed over commercial cooking equipment to extinguish grease fires.

name: Fire Suppression System Commissioning
description: On-site testing and verification of all suppression system components to ensure proper operation and code compliance.

name: Suppression Piping Installation
description: On-site installation and routing of suppression system feed and branch piping through the building structure.

name: Sprinkler Head Installation
description: On-site mounting and connection of sprinkler heads to branch piping at designated spacing and coverage locations.

name: Fire Suppression Control Wiring
description: On-site installation of electrical and signal cabling connecting detection devices, valves, and the control panel.

name: Fire Suppression Agent Charging
description: On-site filling and pressurization of suppression agent storage tanks with water, chemical, or gaseous agent.

name: Suppression System Valve Assembly
description: On-site assembly and installation of control valves, check valves, and trim piping at the system riser room.

name: Standpipe System
description: A vertical pipe network providing hose connections at each floor for manual firefighting by building occupants or fire department.

name: Fire Hydrant Connection
description: A building exterior connection point that allows fire department apparatus to supply water to the standpipe or sprinkler system.

name: Fire Pump
description: A pump that boosts water pressure to the suppression system when municipal supply pressure is insufficient.

name: Fire Suppression Riser Room
description: A dedicated enclosed space housing the main riser, valves, pumps, and control equipment for the building's fire suppression system.

name: Elevator Car
description: The enclosed passenger or freight cabin that travels vertically within the hoistway, transporting occupants and goods between building floors.

name: Hoistway/Shaft
description: The vertical enclosed shaft within the building structure that guides and contains the elevator car and counterweight during travel.

name: Guide Rails
description: Vertical steel rails mounted in the hoistway that guide the elevator car and counterweight to ensure smooth and precise vertical movement.

name: Elevator Machine/Roomless Controller
description: The motor, drive system, and control panel that powers and regulates the movement, speed, and floor-leveling of the elevator car.

name: Traction/ Hydraulic System
description: The mechanical system using either steel ropes and sheaves (traction) or a hydraulic piston (hydraulic) to raise and lower the elevator car.

name: Counterweight Assembly
description: A weighted frame traveling opposite the car on its own guide rails to balance the car's weight and reduce motor load.

name: Elevator Landing Doors
description: The sliding or swing doors installed at each floor opening that provide security and fire separation when the car is not present.

name: Car Doors
description: The sliding or swing doors mounted on the elevator car that open and close in synchronization with landing doors at each floor.

name: Safety Brake/Governor
description: A mechanical overspeed governor and braking system that stops and holds the elevator car in the event of free fall or excessive speed.

name: Buffers
description: Spring or oil-filled shock absorbers located at the bottom of the hoistway to cushion the car or counterweight in case of over-travel.

name: Traveling Cable
description: A flexible electrical cable that connects the stationary building power supply to the moving elevator car for lighting, controls, and communications.

name: Hall Call Fixtures
description: Push-button panels located at each floor landing to summon the elevator car to that floor.

name: Car Operating Panel
description: The control panel inside the elevator car containing floor selection buttons, door open/close controls, alarm, and emergency communication.

name: Position Indicator
description: A display within the car or at landings showing the current floor number and direction of travel.

name: Machine Room (if separate)
description: A dedicated room, typically above the hoistway, housing the elevator drive machinery, controller, and power supply equipment.

name: Pit
description: The recessed area at the bottom of the hoistway that contains buffers and provides clearance for maintenance access below the car.

name: Elevator Install/Commissioning
description: On-site assembly, installation, wiring, testing, and commissioning of elevator components within the hoistway and machine room.

name: Hoistway Construction
description: On-site building of the vertical shaft enclosure, including structural walls, fire-rated lining, and sill installation at each landing.

name: Platform Lift/Wheelchair Lift
description: A smaller vertical lifting platform for accessibility, typically serving limited heights and installed where full elevator shafts are not feasible.

name: Truss/Balustrade Assembly
description: The structural framework and glass/metal barrier panels that enclose the escalator stairway and protect passengers.

name: Step Chain and Pallet System
description: The continuous chain-driven loop of individual steps or pallets that form the moving stair tread surface.

name: Handrail (Moving)
description: The moving rubber or polymer belt that travels in synchrony with the steps to provide passenger support.

name: Handrail Drive Mechanism
description: The pulleys, tensioners, and motor drive that power the moving handrail belt.

name: Drive Motor and Gearbox
description: The electric motor and reduction gearbox that provides torque to the step chain drive system.

name: Drive Shaft and Sprockets
description: The rotating shaft and toothed wheels that engage the step chain and transmit power from the motor.

name: Step Guide Rails/Track
description: The fixed steel rail system that guides the step wheels through the inclined and flat sections of the escalator path.

name: Newel (Handrail Base)
description: The fixed structural post at the entry/exit points that houses the handrail return mechanism and direction change.
