name: Landing Platform (Upper/Lower)
description: The flat fixed floor plates at each end where passengers step on and off the moving stairway.

name: Comb Plate
description: The toothed metal plate at the landing that meshes with the step cleats to allow smooth passenger transition.

name: Skirt Panel
description: The vertical side panel adjacent to the steps that prevents objects from contacting the internal machinery.

name: Truss Stringer (Side Beam)
description: The main longitudinal steel beam on each side of the escalator truss spanning between floor levels.

name: Controller/Panel
description: The electrical control cabinet housing the PLC, variable frequency drive, and safety relay logic for escalator operation.

name: Emergency Stop Switch
description: The manual push-button or key-switch installed at landings that immediately halts escalator motion.

name: Safety Sensors and Switches
description: The collection of missing-step sensors, handrail-entry sensors, and overspeed governors that detect unsafe conditions.

name: Step Demarcation Lighting
description: The LED strip lights embedded at the step periphery to improve passenger visibility and safety.

name: Machine Room (Integrated)
description: The enclosed compartment within the truss or adjacent pit housing the drive motor, controller, and hydraulic brake components.

name: Escalator Pit
description: The recessed concrete or steel pit below the lower landing that accommodates the return loop of the step chain and tensioning device.

name: Escalator Truss
description: The primary structural steel frame spanning between floors that supports all escalator components and transfers loads to the building.

name: Railing (Fixed) Adjacent to Escalator
description: The fixed guardrail or handrail attached to the balustrade on the building side for additional passenger safety.

name: Escalator Installation
description: The on-site process of lifting, positioning, and connecting the prefabricated escalator truss assembly into the prepared structural opening.

name: Escalator Commissioning
description: The on-site testing, load testing, safety-function verification, and adjustment of drive parameters before handover.

name: Travelator/Moving Walk
description: A flat or gently inclined moving walkway variant of the escalator that transports passengers horizontally or on a shallow slope without steps.

name: Spiral Escalator
description: A curved-path escalator variant that follows a helical trajectory through a building atrium or circular opening.

name: Heavy-Duty/Metro Escalator
description: A reinforced escalator variant with increased step width, higher motor power, and more robust components for high-traffic public transit environments.

name: Inclined Elevator (Funicular-style Escalator)
description: A hybrid system variant combining an escalator-like inclined track with elevator cabs for passengers with wheeled mobility devices.

name: Lighting Fixture
description: The actual luminaire or light-producing device installed in the building, including decorative and functional types.

name: Lamp / Light Source
description: The replaceable light-emitting element within a fixture, such as LED module, fluorescent tube, or incandescent bulb.

name: Ballast / Driver
description: Electrical device that regulates current and voltage to the lamp, including LED drivers and fluorescent ballasts.

name: Lighting Control System
description: Networked or standalone system managing the switching, dimming, and scheduling of lighting fixtures.

name: Lighting Switch
description: Manual wall-mounted device for turning lights on/off, including toggle, dimmer, and smart switches.

name: Occupancy Sensor
description: Device that detects presence of people in a space to automatically control lighting.

name: Daylight Sensor / Photocell
description: Device that measures ambient light levels and adjusts electric lighting output accordingly.

name: Lighting Control Panel
description: Centralized electrical enclosure containing relays, dimmers, and controllers for multiple lighting circuits.

name: Emergency Lighting System
description: Battery-backed lighting that activates upon power loss to provide illumination for safe egress.

name: Exit Sign
description: Internally illuminated sign indicating an emergency exit path, typically with battery backup.

name: Lighting Conductor / Track
description: Linear metal channel or busway that supports and supplies power to track-mounted lighting fixtures.

name: Lighting Diffuser / Lens
description: Transparent or translucent cover that spreads and softens light output from a fixture.

name: Reflector / Baffle / Louver
description: Optical component that directs, shields, or controls the distribution of light from a fixture.

name: Mounting Bracket / Hanger
description: Hardware used to attach lighting fixtures to ceilings, walls, poles, or other building surfaces.

name: Electrical Junction Box (Lighting)
description: Enclosure housing electrical connections for lighting circuits, serving as a mounting point for fixtures.

name: Lighting Circuit / Feeder
description: Branch electrical wiring and conduit dedicated to supplying power to lighting loads.

name: Install Lighting Fixtures
description: On-site mounting, wiring, and securing of luminaires to building surfaces or supports.

name: Install Lighting Controls
description: On-site installation of switches, sensors, dimmers, and control panels with associated wiring.

name: Install Emergency Lighting
description: On-site mounting and connection of emergency lights, exit signs, and associated battery systems.

name: Commission Lighting System
description: On-site testing, calibration, and programming of all lighting components to meet design specifications.

name: Daylighting Integration
description: Coordinated design and control of electric lighting with natural daylight from windows, skylights, or light shelves.

name: Task Lighting
description: Focused, localized lighting provided at workstations or task areas, often integrated into furniture or ceiling grids.

name: Accent / Display Lighting
description: Directional lighting used to highlight architectural features, artwork, or retail merchandise.

name: Recessed Downlight / Can Light
description: Fixture installed flush into a ceiling cavity, providing downward-directed ambient or accent light.

name: Surface-Mount Luminaire
description: Fixture mounted directly onto a ceiling or wall surface without recessing.

name: Pendant Luminaire
description: Suspended fixture hanging from the ceiling by a rod, cable, or chain.

name: Wall Sconce
description: Fixture mounted on a wall that directs light upward, downward, or outward.

name: Strip Light / Linear Fixture
description: Long, narrow fixture typically using fluorescent or LED strip lamps, common in commercial and industrial spaces.

name: High-Bay / Low-Bay Luminaire
description: High-intensity fixture designed for ceilings above 15 ft (high-bay) or 10-15 ft (low-bay), used in warehouses and gymnasiums.

name: Landscape / Exterior Lighting
description: Weatherproof fixtures mounted on building exterior, poles, or ground for illuminating paths, facades, and parking areas.

name: Lighting Control Bus / Communication Cable
description: Low-voltage cabling linking sensors, switches, and controllers for digital lighting control protocols like DALI or DMX.

name: Control Panel / Fire Alarm Control Unit (FACU)
description: The central processing hub that monitors inputs from detectors and initiation devices, processes signals, and activates notification and suppression systems.

name: Smoke Detector
description: A device that senses smoke particles in the air, typically using ionization, photoelectric, or aspiration sensing technologies.

name: Heat Detector
description: A device that responds to a rise in temperature above a fixed threshold or a rapid rate-of-rise in temperature.

name: Manual Pull Station (Manual Call Point)
description: A manually operated wall-mounted device that occupants use to initiate a fire alarm signal.

name: Notification Appliance
description: A device that emits audible and/or visible alerts, such as horns, strobes, sirens, speakers, and combined horn/strobe units.

name: Fire Alarm Bell / Sounder
description: An electromechanical or electronic audible signaling device typically mounted in corridors and public areas.

name: Visual Alarm / Strobe Light
description: A flashing light-based notification device required for areas where occupants are hearing-impaired or where ambient noise is high.

name: Voice Evacuation System
description: An integrated public-address system that broadcasts pre-recorded or live emergency voice instructions to building occupants.

name: Addressable Device Module / Loop Interface
description: An electronic interface that connects addressable field devices to the signaling line circuit (SLC) for individual device identification.

name: Conventional Detector Zone Module
description: A component that interfaces conventional (non-addressable) detector zones with an addressable control panel.

name: Fire Alarm Control Panel Enclosure
description: A lockable metal cabinet housing the FACU electronics, batteries, and wiring terminations.

name: Backup Battery / Power Supply
description: A secondary power source, typically sealed lead-acid or lithium batteries, that ensures system operation during main power failure.

name: Annunciator Panel (Remote Annunciator)
description: A remote display panel, often located at a building entrance or security desk, that indicates alarm zone status and device locations.

name: Fire Alarm Wiring / Cabling
description: Specialized fire-resistant or shielded cables (e.g., FPL, FPLR, or MC cable) that interconnect all fire alarm system components.

name: Conduit / Raceway for Fire Alarm Cables
description: Electrical metallic tubing (EMT) or rigid conduit that provides mechanical protection and pathway for fire alarm wiring.

name: Detector Base
description: A mounting base fixed to the ceiling or wall that mechanically and electrically connects a plug-in detector head.

name: Duct Smoke Detector
description: A smoke detector specifically designed for installation in HVAC ductwork to sense smoke in air-handling systems and trigger fan shutdown.

name: Beam Detector (Projected Beam Smoke Detector)
description: A line-of-sight optical smoke detector that projects a light beam across large open spaces such as atriums and warehouses.

name: Aspiration / Air-Sampling Smoke Detector (ASD)
description: An extremely sensitive detection system that draws air samples through a network of pipes to a central laser-based detection chamber.

name: Flame Detector
description: An optical sensor that detects infrared (IR) or ultraviolet (UV) radiation emitted by flames, used in high-hazard areas.

name: Gas Detector (CO / Combustible Gas)
description: A device that monitors for carbon monoxide, natural gas, or other hazardous gas concentrations and triggers alarms.

name: Interface Relay / Control Module
description: A device that allows the fire alarm system to control external building systems such as door releases, elevator recall, and HVAC shutdown.

name: Door Holder / Magnetic Door Release
description: An electromagnetic device that holds fire-rated doors open under normal conditions and releases them upon alarm signal to close.

name: Fire Alarm System Ground Fault / Surge Protector
description: A protective device installed on fire alarm circuits to mitigate electrical surges and detect ground faults in the wiring.

name: Testing / Commissioning of Fire Alarm System
description: On-site verification and functional testing of all detection, notification, and control devices to ensure system operates per design specifications and code.

name: Installation of Fire Alarm Devices and Cabling
description: On-site mounting, wiring, and termination of all fire alarm field devices, panels, and interconnecting cables within the building.

name: Cable Pulling and Conduit Installation for Fire Alarm
description: On-site installation of conduit raceways and pulling of fire-rated cabling through walls, ceilings, and cable trays.

name: Intrusion Detection System
description: Electronic system that detects unauthorized entry into a building through sensors, alarms, and control panels.

name: Access Control System
description: System that manages and restricts entry to building areas using credentials such as keycards, biometrics, or PIN codes.

name: CCTV / Video Surveillance System
description: Network of cameras, recorders, and monitors used to visually monitor interior and exterior building areas.

name: Security Control Panel / Annunciator
description: Central interface unit where security personnel monitor alarms, view system status, and manage responses.

name: Door Contact Sensor
description: Magnetic switch mounted on doors and windows that triggers an alarm when the circuit is broken by opening.

name: Motion Detector / PIR Sensor
description: Passive infrared sensor that detects movement within a protected zone and signals the alarm system.

name: Glass Break Detector
description: Acoustic or vibration sensor that detects the sound or shock of breaking glass and triggers an alarm.

name: Electronic Lock / Magnetic Lock
description: Electrically controlled locking device on doors that releases upon valid credential presentation or fire alarm.

name: Card Reader / Keypad Reader
description: Wall-mounted device that reads credentials (smart card, proximity card, or PIN) to authorize door entry.

name: Biometric Scanner
description: Credential reader using fingerprint, iris, or facial recognition to verify identity for access control.

name: Emergency Exit / Request-to-Exit Device
description: Push bar or motion sensor that allows egress from a secured door while triggering the access control system.

name: Security Camera (Fixed, PTZ, Dome)
description: Video capture device mounted in or on the building that records or streams footage to the surveillance system.

name: Digital Video Recorder (DVR) / Network Video Recorder (NVR)
description: Dedicated recording appliance that stores and manages video feeds from security cameras.

name: Intercom / Video Intercom System
description: Two-way communication system at building entries allowing visitors to announce themselves and be granted access remotely.

name: Security Lighting
description: Purpose-built exterior or interior lighting fixtures that illuminate vulnerable areas for surveillance and deterrence.

name: Perimeter Fence / Gate with Sensor
description: Physical barriers around the building property line integrated with contact sensors or vibration detection.

name: Panic / Duress Alarm Button
description: Manually activated wall switch or pendant that sends a silent alarm signal in emergency situations.

name: Security System Cabling and Wiring
description: Low-voltage cabling (CAT6, shielded cable, power wiring) that interconnects all security devices and control panels.

name: Install Intrusion Detection Wiring and Sensors
description: On-site installation of alarm cables, door/window contacts, motion detectors, and glass break sensors throughout the building.

name: Install Access Control Hardware and Cabling
description: On-site mounting and connection of card readers, electronic locks, biometric scanners, and intercoms at controlled doors.

name: Install CCTV Cameras and Recording Equipment
description: On-site mounting of security cameras and rack-mounting of DVR/NVR units with cable termination and power connection.

name: Commission and Program Security System
description: On-site configuration, zone programming, credential assignment, and end-to-end testing of all security subsystems.

name: BMS Controller / Head-End Server
description: The central processing unit and server hardware that aggregates data from all connected building subsystems and provides the user interface for monitoring and control.

name: Field Controllers / PLCs
description: Distributed programmable logic controllers or direct digital control (DDC) panels installed in plant rooms that execute local control logic for HVAC, lighting, or other subsystems.

name: Sensors (Temperature, Humidity, CO2, Pressure)
description: Field devices that measure environmental parameters such as air temperature, relative humidity, carbon dioxide concentration, and differential pressure for feedback control.

name: Actuators (Valve, Damper, Relay)
description: Electromechanical devices that receive control signals from controllers to modulate valves, dampers, or electrical relays serving HVAC and lighting systems.

name: BACnet / LonWorks / Modbus Gateway
description: Communication protocol interface hardware that translates between the BMS backbone and different building subsystem networks to enable interoperability.

name: BMS Control Network Cabling & Bus
description: The physical twisted-pair, RS-485, or Ethernet backbone cabling that interconnects controllers, sensors, and the head-end server throughout the building.

name: Operator Workstation & BMS Software
description: The dedicated desktop or mobile computer running supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) software that displays dashboards, alarms, and trends to facility managers.

name: Building Energy Metering Hardware
description: Submeters, pulse counters, and current transformers connected to the BMS for real-time tracking of electrical, gas, water, or thermal energy consumption.

name: Alarm Annunciation Panel
description: A local or remote indicator panel, often with audible and visual alerts, that notifies building operators of critical system faults or emergency conditions.

name: BMS Installation & Commissioning
description: On-site mounting of controllers, routing and termination of control cabling, sensor calibration, and end-to-end system integration testing to verify proper BMS operation.

name: Integrated Fire Alarm / Life Safety Interface
description: A dedicated relay or gateway module that connects the fire alarm system to the BMS for coordinated smoke control, fan shutdown, and emergency status reporting.

name: Integrated Lighting Control Interface
description: A networked interface panel that links the building's lighting control system to the BMS for centralized scheduling, demand response, and occupancy-based dimming.

name: Primary Structural Frame
description: The main load-bearing assembly of columns, beams, and girders that transfers gravity and lateral loads to the foundation.

name: Secondary Structural Framing
description: Subsidiary framing members such as purlins, girts, joists, and bridging that support cladding, decking, and roof panels.

name: Bracing System
description: Lateral stability elements including cross-bracing, portal frames, shear walls, and moment-resisting connections that resist wind and seismic forces.

name: Floor Framing System
description: The assembly of floor beams, girders, and decking that supports floor loads and transfers them to the primary frame.

name: Roof Framing System
description: The assembly of roof beams, trusses, purlins, and decking that supports roof loads and transfers them to the primary frame.

name: Foundation Connections
description: Steel base plates, anchor rods, grouted pockets, and connection details that transfer frame forces into the foundation system.

name: Structural Steel Connections
description: Bolted, welded, or pinned joints and connection plates that join framing members together at intersections.

name: Composite Decking
description: Profiled steel deck panels with shear studs that act compositely with concrete topping to form floor slabs.

name: Trusses and Space Frames
description: Triangulated assemblies of members that span large distances efficiently for roofs, floors, or long-span structures.

name: Steel Erection Activity
description: On-site hoisting, aligning, and bolting or welding of structural steel members into their final position.

name: Connection Bolting and Torquing Activity
description: On-site installation and tensioning of high-strength bolts in structural connections to achieve design clamping force.

name: Welding and Inspection Activity
description: On-site field welding of steel framing connections followed by non-destructive testing for quality assurance.

name: Deck Installation and Shear Stud Welding Activity
description: On-site placement of metal deck panels and welding of shear studs through the deck to the supporting steel beams.

name: Fireproofing Application Activity
description: On-site spray-applied or board-applied fire-resistive material application to structural steel members.

name: Steel Frame Alignment and Plumb Checking Activity
description: On-site surveying and adjustment of erected steel members to ensure vertical plumbness and dimensional tolerances.

name: Wall Finish
description: The surface treatment applied to corridor walls, including paint, wallcovering, wainscoting, or impact-resistant panels.

name: Ceiling Finish
description: The overhead surface treatment in the corridor, typically suspended acoustic tile, gypsum board, or exposed structure with paint.

name: Corridor Lighting
description: Light fixtures installed in the corridor ceiling or walls to provide egress and general illumination.

name: Emergency Exit Sign
description: Illuminated signage mounted in the corridor indicating the path of egress to an exit.

name: Corridor Fire Door
description: A rated door assembly installed in the corridor wall to maintain fire compartmentation and provide passage.

name: Corridor Handrail
description: A continuous rail mounted on corridor walls to provide support and comply with accessibility codes.

name: Corridor Wall Base
description: A protective trim piece where the corridor wall meets the floor, typically rubber, vinyl, or wood.

name: Corridor Soffit
description: A dropped ceiling or horizontal projection in the corridor that conceals ductwork, piping, or wiring.

name: Corridor Floor Drain
description: A plumbing fixture set flush in the corridor floor for drainage in wet or service corridors.

name: Corridor Wall Protection
description: Impact-resistant corner guards, crash rails, or bumper strips mounted on corridor walls to prevent damage.

name: Corridor Signage System
description: Wayfinding and room-identification signs mounted on corridor walls or suspended from the ceiling.

name: Corridor Access Panel
description: A removable panel in the corridor wall or ceiling providing access to concealed mechanical, electrical, or plumbing services.

name: Corridor Smoke Barrier

description: Durable finished floor covering (tile, stone, carpet, or polished concrete) specific to the reception area.

name: Reception Ceiling
description: Suspended or feature ceiling treatment including acoustic panels and integrated lighting within the reception zone.

name: Entry Door Assembly
description: The main entrance doors and automatic sliding or revolving door system adjacent to the reception.

name: Lobby HVAC Diffuser
description: Supply and return air grilles or diffusers serving the reception area's heating and cooling.

name: Reception AV System
description: Fixed audio-visual equipment including monitor screens, speakers, and digital signage mounted in the lobby.

name: Reception Fire Safety Equipment
description: Fixed fire extinguisher cabinet, smoke detectors, and emergency signage located in the reception area.

name: Reception Data/Power Outlets
description: Floor boxes, wall sockets, and cable management provisions installed for reception equipment and visitor use.

name: Install Lobby Seating
description: On-site installation of fixed benches or seats in the waiting area of the reception.

name: Install Reception Lighting
description: Mounting and connection of all ceiling and wall luminaires dedicated to the reception zone.

name: Install Visitor Management Kiosk
description: On-site mounting, wiring, and network connection of the visitor check-in terminal.

name: Install Reception Signage
description: Mounting of fixed nameplates, logo walls, and directional signs in the reception area.

name: Countertop
description: The horizontal work surface in the kitchenette, typically laminate, solid surface, or tile.

name: Base Cabinets
description: Floor-mounted storage cabinets below the countertop providing enclosed storage and supporting the counter surface.

name: Wall Cabinets
description: Wall-mounted overhead storage cabinets for dishes, glassware, and dry goods above the counter.

name: Sink with Faucet
description: A basin with a mixing faucet for hand-washing and light food preparation, connected to building plumbing.

name: Built-in Microwave
description: A building-integrated microwave oven recessed into cabinetry or mounted above the counter.

name: Built-in Refrigerator/Under-counter Fridge
description: A building-integrated refrigeration unit fitted into cabinetry for chilled storage and ice making.

name: Dishwasher (Under-counter)
description: An under-counter appliance for washing and sanitizing dishes, connected to building plumbing and electrical.

name: Overhead Microwave/Exhaust Hood
description: A ventilation hood mounted above cooking appliances to capture steam, heat, and odors, ducted or recirculating.

name: Backsplash
description: The wall finish behind the countertop and sink area, typically tile or sheet material, protecting walls from moisture and stains.

name: Kitchenette Plumbing Rough-in
description: The hot and cold water supply lines, drain-waste-vent piping, and shut-off valves serving the sink and dishwasher.

name: Kitchenette Electrical Rough-in
description: The dedicated branch circuits, outlets, and switch wiring serving appliances, lighting, and GFCI-protected receptacles.

name: Undercabinet Lighting
description: Task lighting fixtures mounted beneath wall cabinets to illuminate the countertop work surface.

name: Ceiling Light Fixture
description: A general ambient light fitting centered in the break room/kitchenette area.

name: Floor Finish (Resilient/Tile)
description: The durable, water-resistant floor covering—typically vinyl composition tile, luxury vinyl plank, or ceramic tile—installed in the kitchenette zone.

name: Wall Finish (Paint/Tile)
description: The painted or tiled surface finish on the kitchenette walls, selected for cleanability and moisture resistance.

name: Break Room Seating Area
description: The adjacent seating zone within the break room furnished with tables and chairs for staff breaks.

name: Break Room Counter/Bar Seating
description: A built-in counter-height eating surface with bar stools or fixed seating attached to the kitchenette peninsula or island.

name: Coffee/ Beverage Station Niche
description: A dedicated alcove or counter section with a built-in coffee machine, hot water dispenser, and additional GFCI outlets.

name: Upper Shelf / Open Shelving
description: Wall-mounted open shelves above the counter for decorative or frequently accessed items, separate from closed cabinets.

name: Kickplate / Toe-kick
description: The recessed base panel at the bottom of base cabinets, often with an integrated vent for dishwasher airflow.

name: Garbage/ Recycling Pull-out
description: A slide-out bin drawer built into the base cabinetry for concealed waste and recycling receptacles.

name: Countertop Outlet Strip (Pop-up)
description: A retractable or flush-mounted electrical outlet strip set into the countertop for small appliance use.

name: Install Cabinetry and Countertop
description: On-site assembly, leveling, and fastening of base and wall cabinets followed by countertop installation and sealing.

name: Install Plumbing Fixtures
description: On-site connection of the sink, faucet, and dishwasher supply/drain lines to the rough-in plumbing.

name: Install Appliances
description: On-site placement and connection of built-in microwave, refrigerator, and dishwasher to services.

name: Install Floor Finish
description: On-site installation of resilient or tile flooring including underlayment, cutting, laying, and grouting.

name: Install Backsplash
description: On-site tiling or sheet installation of the backsplash wall finish including cutting, adhesion, and sealing.

name: Install Ceiling & Lighting
description: On-site mounting of ceiling fixtures, undercabinet lighting, and any ceiling finish work.

name: Final Trim & Hardware
description: On-site installation of cabinet hardware, shelving, kickplates, and outlet covers to complete the kitchenette.

name: Meeting Room Chair
description: Task or conference seating designed for comfort during meetings, typically on casters with armrests.

name: Presentation Display Screen
description: A wall-mounted or ceiling-mounted monitor, projector screen, or interactive whiteboard for presentations.

name: Audio Conferencing System
description: Integrated speakerphone, ceiling microphones, or soundbar system enabling remote meeting participation.

name: Video Conferencing Camera
description: Fixed camera unit, typically wall- or ceiling-mounted above the display, for video call capture.

name: Whiteboard / Marker Board
description: A wall-mounted dry-erase writing surface for brainstorming and note-taking during meetings.

name: Room Scheduling Panel
description: A wall-mounted touchscreen or display outside the door showing room availability and booking status.

name: Ceiling Mounted Projector
description: A permanently installed digital projector suspended from the ceiling for image projection onto a screen.

name: Projection Screen
description: A motorized or fixed retractable screen installed on the wall or ceiling for receiving projected images.

name: Built-in Credenza / Media Cabinet
description: A fixed storage unit along the wall for AV equipment, supplies, or presentation materials.

name: Cable Management System
description: Concealed raceways, floor boxes, or grommets routing power and data cables to the conference table.

name: Window Blinds / Motorized Shades
description: Adjustable light-blocking window coverings to control glare and ambient light during presentations.

name: Floor Box / Power Outlet
description: A flush-mounted floor access point providing power and data connectivity at the conference table.

name: Room Sound Masking System
description: An audio system emitting background white noise to enhance speech privacy within the meeting room.

name: HVAC Zone Damper / Thermostat
description: Dedicated temperature control device allowing individual HVAC adjustment for the meeting room zone.

name: Door with Privacy Lock
description: A solid-core door equipped with an electronic or keyed privacy lock for meeting confidentiality.

name: Installing Acoustic Treatment
description: On-site installation of acoustic panels, sound baffles, or ceiling clouds to improve room acoustics.

name: Installing AV Rack & Equipment
description: Mounting and cabling AV equipment including the display, speakers, microphones, and control processor.

name: Commissioning Room AV System
description: Testing and calibrating audio, video, and control subsystems to ensure proper operation for meetings.

name: Server Racks & Cabinets
description: Standardized metal frames (e.g., 19-inch racks) that mount and organize server hardware, switches, and patch panels within the IT room.

name: Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS)
description: Battery-backed power system that provides emergency backup power to servers and network equipment during mains power interruptions.

name: Power Distribution Unit (PDU)
description: Device that distributes electric power from the UPS or main supply to multiple server racks with metering and outlet-level control.

name: Precision/Computer Room Air Conditioning (CRAC/CRAH)
description: Dedicated cooling system designed to maintain strict temperature and humidity levels required by heat-generating IT equipment.

name: Overhead Cable Tray & Ladder Rack
description: Support structure fixed above or below the raised floor to organize and route network and power cabling between racks.

name: Fire Suppression System (Clean Agent)
description: Gas-based (e.g., FM-200, Novec 1230) fire extinguishing system that protects sensitive electronics without water damage.

name: Environmental Monitoring System
description: Networked sensors and controller that continuously monitor temperature, humidity, smoke, water leakage, and access in the server room.

name: Server Room Access Control System
description: Electronic lock and authentication system (card reader, biometric scanner) restricting physical entry to authorized personnel only.

name: Grounding & Bonding Busbar
description: Copper busbar and conductor network providing a dedicated low-impedance path to ground for all IT equipment racks and cable trays.

name: Patch Panel & Fiber Optic Termination Enclosure
description: Fixed panel where incoming data cabling terminates and is patched to server/switch ports, located inside or adjacent to server racks.

name: Subfloor Vibration Isolation Base
description: Structural isolation pad or spring mount placed under server racks to decouple sensitive equipment from building-floor vibrations.

name: Install Raised Access Flooring
description: Assembling and leveling modular floor panels on adjustable pedestals to create the raised platform and cable plenum.

name: Install CRAC/CRAH Unit and Ducting
description: Positioning, anchoring, and connecting precision cooling units to the building's chilled water or refrigerant loop.

name: Install UPS and Battery Bank
description: Mounting uninterruptible power supply cabinets and their battery strings, and connecting to the building's main electrical panel.

name: Install Server Racks and Cable Management
description: Anchoring server racks to the raised floor, mounting cable trays/ladder racks, and dressing all data and power cabling.

name: Install Clean-Agent Fire Suppression System
description: Mounting gas cylinders, piping, and discharge nozzles in the ceiling plenum and under the raised floor for fire protection.

name: Commission Environmental and Access Control Systems
description: Programming, testing, and calibrating temperature/humidity sensors, leak detectors, door locks, and monitoring software.

name: Reinforced Concrete
description: Concrete with embedded steel reinforcement bars or mesh to resist tensile forces.

name: Precast Concrete
description: Concrete elements cast and cured in a controlled factory environment before being transported and installed on site.

name: Prestressed Concrete
description: Concrete with internal stresses introduced by tensioned tendons to improve performance under load.

name: Lightweight Concrete
description: Concrete made with lightweight aggregates to reduce density while maintaining structural strength.

name: High-Performance Concrete
description: Concrete engineered with admixtures and optimized mix designs for enhanced durability, strength, or workability.

name: Fiber-Reinforced Concrete
description: Concrete containing dispersed fibers (steel, glass, synthetic) to improve crack resistance and toughness.

name: Concrete Formwork
description: Temporary or permanent molds that shape and support wet concrete until it cures and gains sufficient strength.

name: Concrete Reinforcement Bar (Rebar)
description: Steel bars or mesh placed within concrete to carry tensile and shear stresses.

name: Concrete Slab
description: A flat, horizontal concrete structural element forming floors, roofs, or ground-bearing slabs.

name: Concrete Beam
description: A horizontal or sloped concrete structural member that resists loads primarily by bending.

name: Concrete Column
description: A vertical concrete compression member that transfers loads from beams and slabs down to foundations.

name: Concrete Wall
description: A vertical concrete element used as a load-bearing or shear wall to support and stabilize a building.

name: Concrete Foundation
description: The lowest load-bearing concrete part of a building that transfers loads to the ground.

name: Concrete Stair
description: A precast or cast-in-place concrete staircase providing vertical circulation within a building.

name: Concrete Joint (Construction/Expansion/Contraction)
description: Engineered gaps and connections in concrete elements to control cracking from shrinkage, thermal movement, and structural loads.

name: Cast-in-Place Concrete Construction
description: On-site activity of placing, consolidating, finishing, and curing fresh concrete in prepared formwork.

name: Precast Concrete Installation
description: On-site activity of lifting, positioning, aligning, and connecting precast concrete elements into the building structure.

name: Concrete Curing
description: On-site process of maintaining moisture and temperature conditions in freshly placed concrete to ensure proper hydration and strength gain.

name: Concrete Surface Finishing
description: On-site activity of troweling, brooming, or applying surface treatments to achieve the desired texture, flatness, or appearance.

name: Concrete Grout
description: A fluid mixture of cement, water, and sometimes sand used to fill voids, bond reinforcement, or sheath tendons.

name: Concrete Anchor / Embedment
description: Steel plates, bolts, or headed studs cast into concrete to provide connection points for structural or non-structural elements.

name: Concrete Topping / Screed
description: A thin layer of concrete or cementitious mix applied over a structural slab to provide a flat level surface or wear layer.

name: Glulam (Glued Laminated Timber)
description: Engineered timber product made by layering and bonding dimensioned lumber with structural adhesives, used for beams, columns, and arches.

name: Cross-Laminated Timber (CLT)
description: Engineered wood panel made from cross-oriented layers of lumber glued together, used for walls, floors, and roofs.

name: Laminated Veneer Lumber (LVL)
description: Engineered timber product made from thin veneers bonded with adhesive under heat and pressure, typically used for beams, lintels, and structural headers.

name: Timber Frame (Heavy Timber / Post-and-Beam)
description: Structural framing system using large-section timber posts, beams, and braces as the primary load-bearing skeleton of a building.

name: Light Timber Framing (Stud Walls, Joists, Rafters)
description: Conventional dimensional lumber framing system consisting of studs, joists, rafters, and plates used in platform or balloon framing.

name: Timber Truss
description: Prefabricated or site-built triangulated timber assembly used to support roofs, floors, or long-span structures.

name: Timber Decking / Subflooring
description: Solid wood or engineered wood planks/panels applied as walking surfaces, structural floor platforms, or roof sheathing.

name: Timber Cladding / Siding
description: Wood boards, shingles, or panels applied as the exterior weather-resistant finish layer on building walls.

name: Timber Finishes (Interior Paneling, Trims, Moldings)
description: Wood-based interior architectural millwork including wall paneling, baseboards, crown moldings, and decorative trim.

name: Timber Doors and Window Frames
description: Solid wood or engineered-wood door leaves, door frames, and window sash/frames installed as building openings.

name: Timber Stairs and Railings
description: Wooden stair flights, landings, handrails, and balustrades providing vertical circulation within a building.

name: Heavy Timber Fireproofing / Encapsulation
description: Fire-resistance measures for timber elements including encapsulation layers, intumescent coatings, or char-layer design allowances.

name: Timber-Concrete Composite System
description: Hybrid floor or deck system where timber beams/panels are shear-connected to a concrete topping slab to act compositely.

name: Structural Timber Installation
description: On-site erection, alignment, and connection of timber structural framing elements including columns, beams, and trusses.

name: Timber Decking / Flooring Installation
description: On-site laying, fastening, and finishing of timber floorboards, deck planks, or subfloor panels.

name: Timber Cladding Installation
description: On-site fixing, lapping, and sealing of timber siding or shingles to building exterior walls.

name: Timber Joinery / Millwork Installation
description: On-site fitting and fixing of prefinished timber doors, window frames, stair assemblies, and interior trim.

name: Timber Treatment and Coating Application
description: On-site application of preservatives, fire retardants, stains, or clear coatings to protect and finish timber surfaces.

name: Timber Connection Hardware
description: Metal fasteners, brackets, bolts, screws, hold-downs, and shear plates used to join timber members in structural assemblies.

name: Structural Steel Columns
description: Vertical load-bearing steel members that transfer compressive forces from beams and slabs to the foundation.

name: Structural Steel Beams
description: Horizontal steel members that support floor and roof loads and transfer them to columns or walls.

name: Steel Trusses
description: Triangulated assemblies of steel members that efficiently span large distances for roofs, floors, or bridges.

name: Steel Girders
description: Large primary horizontal steel beams that support smaller beams and carry heavy concentrated loads.

name: Steel Bracing Systems
description: Diagonal or cross steel members that resist lateral forces such as wind and seismic loads on the building.

name: Steel Moment Frames
description: Rigid steel beam-to-column connections that resist lateral loads through bending rather than bracing.

name: Steel Base Plates
description: Thick steel plates at the bottom of columns that distribute loads to the foundation and anchor the column.

name: Steel Connections & Fasteners
description: Bolts, welds, gusset plates, and splice plates that join steel members together at joints.

name: Composite Steel Decking
description: Profiled steel sheets that serve as permanent formwork for concrete slabs and act compositely with the concrete.

name: Steel Shear Studs
description: Welded-headed steel connectors that transfer shear between steel beams and composite concrete slabs.

name: Structural Steel Erection
description: On-site hoisting, aligning, and bolting/welding of steel members into their final positions in the building frame.

name: Steel Welding & Bolting
description: On-site welding of steel connections and torque-controlled bolting of high-strength friction-grip connections.

name: Steel Column & Beam Installation
description: Setting, plumbing, and temporarily bracing columns and beams before permanent connections are completed.

name: Steel Fireproofing Application
description: Spray-applied fire-resistive material or intumescent coating applied to steel members for fire protection.

name: Steel Shop Drawing Review & Staging
description: On-site coordination and layout of delivered steel pieces prior to erection to ensure fit-up.

name: Light-Gauge Steel Framing
description: Cold-formed thin-gauge steel sections used for non-load-bearing partitions and secondary framing.

name: Steel Stairs & Railings
description: Fabricated steel stringers, treads, landings, and guardrails forming egress stairs and platforms.

name: Steel Canopies & Canopy Supports
description: Steel-framed roof overhangs and their supporting structure at building entrances or loading areas.

name: Steel Roof Trusses & Purlin Systems
description: Steel trusses and secondary roof purlins spanning between trusses to support roof cladding.

name: Embedded Steel Anchor Systems
description: Steel plates, bolts, and channels cast into concrete to receive structural steel connections.

name: Float Glass
description: Standard flat glass produced by floating molten glass on molten tin, used as base for windows and glazing.

name: Tempered Glass
description: Heat-treated safety glass that shatters into small granules upon impact, used in doors, facades, and shower enclosures.

name: Laminated Glass
description: Composite glass with interlayer for safety, security, and acoustic performance, used in skylights, balustrades, and windshields.

name: Insulated Glass Unit (IGU)
description: Multi-pane sealed glass assembly with air or gas cavity for thermal insulation in windows and curtain walls.

name: Low-E Coated Glass
description: Glass with microscopically thin metallic coating that reflects infrared radiation while transmitting visible light.

name: Reflective Glass
description: Glass with a metallic coating that reduces solar heat gain and provides mirror-like appearance on building facades.

name: Frosted Glass
description: Glass with etched or sandblasted surface for privacy while transmitting light, used in partitions and doors.

name: Wired Glass
description: Glass with embedded wire mesh for fire resistance and crack containment, used in fire-rated doors and windows.

name: Curtain Wall Glazing
description: Non-structural exterior cladding system where glass panels are attached to a metal frame, forming the building envelope.

name: Structural Glass
description: Thick, high-strength glass used in load-bearing applications such as glass fins, beams, and frameless assemblies.

name: Glass Balustrade
description: Glass barrier system used along staircases, balconies, and terraces for fall protection with visual transparency.

name: Glass Partition
description: Interior glass wall system dividing spaces while allowing light transmission, typically framed or frameless.

name: Glass Door
description: Full or partial glass door panel used for interior or exterior access, available in hinged, sliding, or revolving types.

name: Glass Canopy
description: Glass roof or awning structure at building entrances providing weather protection while admitting daylight.

name: Glass Floor Panel
description: Structural glass panel installed in floors or walkways for visual connection between levels.

name: Glass Skylight
description: Fixed or operable glass roof panel admitting natural light into interior spaces from above.

name: Glass Block
description: Hollow glass masonry unit used in walls and windows for light diffusion with privacy and insulation.

name: Spandrel Glass
description: Opaque or back-painted glass used in curtain walls to conceal structural elements, floors, and mechanical equipment.

name: Glass Installation
description: On-site placement, alignment, and fixing of glass panels into frames, curtain walls, or structural supports.

name: Glazing Sealant Application
description: Application of weather-resistant sealants around glass edges to ensure air and water tightness.

name: Glass Cutting & Preparation On-Site
description: On-site cutting, edge grinding, and drilling of glass panels to fit specific openings and hardware.

name: Glass Balustrade Assembly
description: Installation and securing of glass panels with clamps, shoes, or standoffs for stair and balcony safety barriers.

name: Glass Curtain Wall Installation
description: Erection and glazing of the curtain wall system including mullions, transoms, and glass infill panels.

name: Thermal Insulation
description: General-purpose insulation materials that reduce heat transfer through building assemblies such as walls, roofs, and floors.

name: Acoustic Insulation
description: Insulation materials specifically designed to absorb sound and reduce noise transmission between spaces.

name: Duct Insulation
description: Insulation applied to HVAC ductwork to reduce thermal losses and prevent surface condensation.

name: Cavity Wall Insulation
description: Insulation installed within the cavity between two leaves of a masonry wall to improve thermal performance.

name: Floor Insulation
description: Insulation placed beneath or within floor constructions, including ground floors and intermediate floors, to reduce heat loss and impact sound.

name: Spray Foam Insulation
description: Insulation applied as a liquid spray that expands into a rigid foam, providing both thermal insulation and air sealing.

name: Rigid Board Insulation
description: Pre-formed rigid insulation panels made from materials such as polyisocyanurate, XPS, EPS, or mineral wool, used in continuous insulation layers.

name: Batt Insulation
description: Flexible fiberglass, mineral wool, or natural fiber insulation supplied in pre-cut rolls or batts designed to fit between framing members.

name: Loose-Fill Insulation
description: Granular or fibrous insulation materials blown or poured into attics, wall cavities, or floor spaces.

name: Reflective Insulation
description: Insulation that uses reflective foil surfaces to reduce radiant heat transfer, typically installed in attics or roof assemblies.

name: Structural Insulated Panels (SIPs)
description: Composite building panels consisting of an insulation core sandwiched between two structural facings, used as load-bearing wall, roof, and floor elements.

name: Insulated Concrete Forms (ICFs)
description: Hollow foam blocks or panels that are stacked, reinforced with rebar, and filled with concrete to create insulated structural walls.

name: Air Sealing
description: Installation of air barriers, tapes, caulks, and gaskets to prevent uncontrolled air leakage through the building envelope.

name: Vapor Retarder
description: A material layer that resists diffusion of moisture vapor through building assemblies, often installed adjacent to insulation.

name: Thermal Break
description: A low-conductivity material interposed between conductive building elements to reduce thermal bridging.

name: Blown-In Insulation Equipment
description: On-site machinery used to pneumatically convey and install loose-fill insulation into building cavities.

name: Bituminous Membrane
description: A waterproof sheet membrane made from modified bitumen (APP or SBS), typically torch-applied or self-adhered for low-slope roofing and below-grade waterproofing.

name: EPDM Membrane
description: A synthetic rubber (ethylene propylene diene monomer) sheet membrane known for high flexibility, UV resistance, and single-ply roofing applications.

name: PVC/TPO Membrane
description: Thermoplastic single-ply sheet membranes (polyvinyl chloride or thermoplastic polyolefin) used for mechanically fastened or adhered roof waterproofing.

name: Liquid-Applied Membrane
description: A cold or hot fluid-applied coating that cures to form a seamless elastomeric waterproof barrier on roofs, decks, and below-grade walls.

name: Self-Adhered Sheet Membrane
description: A pre-formed rubberized asphalt sheet with a release liner that bonds directly to the substrate without torching or hot asphalt.

name: Bentonite Waterproofing Membrane
description: A sodium bentonite clay layer encased in geotextile or cardboard that expands upon hydration to seal below-grade concrete structures.

name: Drainage Composite / Protection Board
description: A dimpled plastic sheet or board installed against the waterproof membrane to protect it and provide a drainage/venting path.

name: Metal Flashing / Counter-flashing
description: Sheet metal (aluminum, copper, or galvanized steel) profiles installed at membrane terminations, penetrations, and transitions to shed water.

name: Membrane Lap Sealant / Primer
description: Solvent-based or butyl adhesives and sealants used to bond membrane overlaps and seal edges during installation.

name: Membrane Installation (Laying)
description: On-site placement, unrolling, positioning, and fitting of sheet or liquid waterproof membrane to the prepared substrate.

name: Torch-On Application (Bitumen)
description: On-site heat-fusing of APP-modified bitumen sheets using a propane torch to melt the underside and bond to the substrate.

name: Membrane Lap Joining / Seaming
description: On-site welding, adhesion, or sealing of overlapping membrane edges to create a continuous waterproof barrier.

name: Membrane Termination / Edge Detailing
description: On-site installation of metal flashings, drip edges, and sealant beads at membrane edges, penetrations, and transitions.

name: Below-Grade Waterproofing System
description: A combined assembly of membranes, drainage boards, and protection layers applied to basement walls and slabs against groundwater.

name: Roof Waterproofing System (Low-Slope)
description: A roof assembly incorporating waterproof membrane, insulation, vapor retarder, and drainage for flat or low-slope roofs.

name: Green / Vegetated Roof System
description: A roof assembly built atop a waterproof membrane with root barrier, drainage, filter fabric, and growing medium for plantings.

name: Clay Brick
description: Traditional fired clay masonry unit used for walls, facades, and structural elements in building construction.

name: Concrete Brick
description: Cement-based compressed masonry unit used for load-bearing and non-load-bearing walls.

name: Calcium Silicate Brick
description: Sand-lime brick manufactured by autoclaving, offering smooth finish and high compressive strength.

name: Engineering Brick
description: Dense, low-porosity fired brick with high compressive strength suitable for damp-proof courses and structural applications.

name: Perforated/Vertically Perforated Brick
description: Brick with vertical holes to reduce weight and improve thermal performance while maintaining structural capacity.

name: Glass Brick
description: Translucent hollow glass block used for non-load-bearing partitions and light-transmitting wall sections.

name: Reclaimed Brick
description: Salvaged brick from demolished structures reused in new construction for aesthetic or sustainability purposes.

name: Brick Mortar
description: Cement-lime-sand bedding material that bonds brick units together and accommodates movement in masonry assemblies.

name: Brick Wall Assembly
description: Vertical construction of brick units laid in bond patterns, forming a load-bearing or non-load-bearing building element.

name: Brick Veneer
description: Non-structural outer wythe of brick attached to a backup wall system, providing cladding and weather resistance.

name: Brick Arch
description: Curved masonry construction spanning openings such as windows, doors, or portals, transferring loads laterally.

name: Brick Pillar/Pier
description: Vertical isolated masonry element providing structural support or decorative emphasis in a building facade.

name: Brick Floor Paving
description: Brick units laid flat on a prepared base to form a durable, slip-resistant walking surface.

name: Brick Cavity Wall
description: Two parallel wythes of brick with an air space between them, improving thermal and moisture performance.

name: Brick Coping
description: Capping course of brick installed on top of a wall or parapet to shed water and protect the masonry below.

name: Brick Corbelling
description: Projecting courses of brick stepped outward from the wall face for decorative or structural support purposes.

name: Brick Lintel
description: Horizontal masonry or reinforced brick element spanning an opening to support the wall above.

name: Brickwork Installation
description: On-site process of laying bricks in mortar to construct walls, piers, arches, and other masonry elements.

name: Brick Joint Pointing
description: Finishing mortar joints between bricks for weather resistance, appearance, and durability after initial laying.

name: Brick Cleaning/Chemical Wash
description: Application of cleaning agents and pressure washing to remove mortar stains, efflorescence, and soiling from new brickwork.

name: Brick Wall Damp-Proofing
description: Installation of damp-proof courses and membranes within brick assemblies to prevent rising or penetrating dampness.

name: Brick Tying and Wall Starter Installation
description: Fixing metal wall ties, starter clips, and bed-joint reinforcement to integrate brick veneer with the backup structure.

name: Expansion Joint Installation in Brickwork
description: Incorporating vertical movement joints filled with compressible filler and sealant to accommodate thermal and moisture movement.

name: Brickwork Curing and Protection
description: Covering and damp-curing newly laid brickwork to ensure proper mortar hydration and prevent premature drying or frost damage.

name: Standard Hollow CMU
description: A typical concrete masonry unit with two or three cores (voids), used for load-bearing and non-load-bearing walls.

name: Solid CMU
description: A dense concrete block with no cores, used for special structural or fire-resistance applications.

name: Lightweight CMU
description: A concrete block made with lightweight aggregates (e.g., expanded clay, slag) for reduced dead load and improved thermal performance.

name: Split-Face CMU
description: A decorative concrete block with a textured, fractured face achieved by splitting two bonded blocks apart.

name: Ground-Face/Polished CMU
description: A concrete block with a ground and polished face exposing the aggregate for an architectural finish.

name: Glazed/Faced CMU
description: A concrete block with a factory-applied glazed or ceramic finish on one face for easy cleaning and durability.

name: Interlocking/Retaining Wall CMU
description: A concrete block with shaped flanges or lips designed for dry-stack retaining walls or segmental gravity walls.

name: Aerated Autoclaved Concrete (AAC) Block
description: A lightweight, precast foam concrete block cured in an autoclave, offering insulation and fire resistance.

name: CMU Bond Beam Block
description: A U-shaped or notched concrete block designed to receive horizontal reinforcement and grout for bond beams.

name: CMU Lintel Block
description: A deep, reinforced concrete block used as a lintel over openings in masonry walls.

name: CMU Corner Block
description: A specially shaped concrete block with one finished end used to form clean external or internal corners.

name: CMU Half Block / Stretcher Block
description: Half-length or standard stretcher concrete blocks used for running bond patterns and modular coordination.

name: CMU Grout (Fine/Grout Mix)
description: A flowable cementitious mix poured into CMU cores to bond reinforcement and increase structural capacity.

name: CMU Mortar (Type N/S/M)
description: A mixture of cement, lime, sand, and water used to bed and bond concrete masonry units together.

name: Horizontal Joint Reinforcement
description: Steel wire truss or ladder reinforcement embedded in mortar joints every 16" to control cracking in CMU walls.

name: Vertical Rebar in CMU
description: Deformed steel reinforcing bars placed vertically within grouted CMU cores for structural strength.

name: CMU Control Joint / Expansion Joint Material
description: Preformed gaskets, neoprene strips, or sealant placed in control joints to accommodate movement in CMU walls.

name: CMU Wall Ties / Anchors
description: Metal connectors used to tie CMU veneer to backup walls or to connect intersecting CMU walls.

name: CMU Washout Access / Cleanout
description: Removable block or plastic access unit at the base of grouted CMU walls to allow debris removal before grouting.

name: CMU Wall Assembly (grouted & reinforced)
description: A complete structural masonry wall system composed of CMU, reinforcement, and grout working together.

name: CMU Cavity Wall Assembly
description: A two-wythe CMU wall system with a continuous airspace for drainage, insulation, and moisture control.

name: CMU Veneer System (Anchored)
description: A non-load-bearing exterior CMU cladding system tied back to a structural backup wall.

name: CMU Retaining Wall System
description: A gravity or reinforced CMU wall system designed to resist lateral earth pressure.

name: CMU Laying / Masonry Installation
description: The on-site placement of concrete blocks in a running or stack bond pattern with mortar joints.

name: CMU Grouting / Core-Fill Operation
description: The on-site pumping or pouring of fluid grout into CMU cores after reinforcement has been placed.

name: CMU Rebar Placement & Tying
description: The on-site installation, splicing, and tying of vertical and horizontal reinforcing steel within CMU walls.

name: CMU Control Joint Cutting / Routing
description: The on-site cutting or forming of vertical control joints in a CMU wall to control cracking.

name: CMU Wall Waterproofing / Dampproofing Application
description: The on-site application of liquid or sheet waterproofing membrane to the exterior face of a CMU wall below grade.

name: CMU Scaffolding & Material Hoisting
description: The on-site erection of scaffolding and hoisting of CMU materials to the workface for mason access.

name: CMU Intersecting Wall Anchoring
description: The on-site installation of metal wall ties and anchors where CMU walls intersect or abut other structure.

name: Concrete Masonry Unit (CMU) — General
description: A precast concrete block used as a primary building unit for masonry walls, partitions, and foundations.

name: Rebar Cage (Reinforcement Cage)
description: Pre-assembled framework of tied reinforcing bars used as a single placement unit in columns, beams, or piles.

name: Rebar Splicing (Lap Splice / Mechanical Splice)
description: On-site activity of overlapping or mechanically connecting reinforcing bars to transfer stress across a joint.

name: Rebar Placing & Fixing
description: On-site activity of positioning, aligning, and tying reinforcing bars into formwork prior to concrete placement.

name: Reinforcing Mesh (Welded Wire Fabric)
description: Prefabricated grid of welded steel wires used as reinforcement in slabs, walls, and pavements.

name: Epoxy-Coated Rebar
description: Steel reinforcing bar with an epoxy coating for corrosion resistance in aggressive environments.

name: Galvanized Rebar
description: Zinc-coated steel reinforcing bar used where additional corrosion protection is needed.

name: Stainless Steel Rebar
description: Corrosion-resistant reinforcing bar manufactured from stainless steel alloys for high-durability applications.

name: GFRP Rebar (Glass-Fiber-Reinforced Polymer Rebar)
description: Non-metallic reinforcing bar made of glass fibers in a polymer resin, used where electromagnetic neutrality or non-corrosiveness is required.

name: Stirrups (Shear Reinforcement)
description: Closed-loop or U-shaped bars placed around longitudinal rebar to resist shear forces in beams and columns.

name: Ties (Column Ties / Beam Ties)
description: Small-diameter reinforcing bars wrapped around longitudinal bars to maintain alignment and prevent buckling.

name: Spiral Reinforcement (Helical Ties)
description: Continuously wound spiral bar used in circular columns or piles to confine concrete and improve ductility.

name: Dowels (Dowling Bars)
description: Short projecting reinforcing bars left protruding from a concrete pour to connect to a subsequent pour.

name: Rebar Bending & Cutting (On-Site)
description: On-site cutting and bending of reinforcing bars to required shapes and dimensions before placement.

name: Post-Installed Rebar Anchoring
description: On-site drilling and bonding of rebar into hardened concrete using adhesive or mechanical anchors.

name: Reinforcement Couplers (Mechanical Connectors)
description: Mechanical devices used to connect rebar ends end-to-end without lapping, providing full tension capacity.

name: Reinforcement Cover Blocks (Spacers)
description: Small precast concrete or plastic blocks placed under rebar to maintain the specified concrete cover depth.

name: Chair Reinforcement (Rebar Chairs)
description: Support devices used to hold upper layers of reinforcing mesh or bars at the correct elevation in slabs.

name: Tension Reinforcement (Main Longitudinal Bars)
description: Primary longitudinal reinforcing bars placed on the tension face of a structural member to resist bending.

name: Compression Reinforcement
description: Longitudinal reinforcing bars placed on the compression side of a member to increase strength and reduce creep.

name: Temperature & Shrinkage Reinforcement
description: Light reinforcement bars or mesh distributed in slabs to control cracking from thermal and shrinkage stresses.

name: Gypsum Board (Regular)
description: Standard gypsum wallboard used for interior walls and ceilings in dry areas.

name: Moisture-Resistant Gypsum Board
description: Green-board or treated gypsum board for use in bathrooms, kitchens, and other high-humidity areas.

name: Fire-Resistant Gypsum Board (Type X)
description: Gypsum board with glass fibers and additives to improve fire resistance, used in rated assemblies.

name: Impact-Resistant Gypsum Board
description: Reinforced gypsum board with a fiberglass or mesh backing for high-traffic or abuse-prone areas.

name: Mold-Resistant Gypsum Board
description: Gypsum board treated with anti-microbial agents and faced with mold-resistant paper or fiberglass mat.

name: Shaftliner Gypsum Board
description: Thin, dense gypsum board designed specifically for use in elevator shafts and stairwell enclosures.

name: Vapor-Retarder Gypsum Board
description: Gypsum board with a foil or treated paper backing that reduces moisture vapor transmission.

name: Flexible/Curved Gypsum Board
description: Thinner, scored gypsum board that can be bent to form curved wall and ceiling surfaces.

name: Gypsum Board Wall Partition
description: A non-load-bearing interior wall assembly comprising gypsum board layers on a metal or wood stud frame.

name: Gypsum Board Soffit
description: A dropped or enclosed section of gypsum board that conceals ductwork, piping, or beams.

name: Gypsum Board Bulkhead
description: A horizontal or vertical gypsum board enclosure around mechanical or structural elements projecting from walls or ceilings.

name: Gypsum Board Chase Wall
description: A shallow gypsum board wall built to conceal vertical plumbing pipes, conduits, or ducts.

name: Gypsum Board Furring/Liner System
description: A system of gypsum board attached to furring channels or directly over existing substrates to level or finish a surface.

name: Gypsum Board Shaft Wall Assembly
description: A complete fire-rated shaft enclosure system using gypsum board liner panels and steel studs.

name: Gypsum Board Corner Bead
description: A metal or vinyl edging profile installed at gypsum board external corners to reinforce and finish the edge.

name: Gypsum Board Trim/Accessory
description: Metal or plastic profiles used at gypsum board edges, joints, and terminations including J-bead, L-bead, and control joints.

name: Gypsum Board Joint Tape and Compound
description: Paper or fiberglass tape and setting- or drying-type joint compounds used to finish gypsum board seams and fasteners.

name: Gypsum Board Fasteners (Screws/Nails)
description: Specialized drywall screws or annular-ring nails designed for attaching gypsum board to studs or furring.

name: Gypsum Board Adhesive/Drywall Glue
description: Construction adhesive used to bond gypsum board to studs or existing surfaces, reducing the number of mechanical fasteners needed.

name: Gypsum Board Acoustic Sealant
description: Non-hardening, flexible sealant applied at gypsum board perimeter edges and penetrations to improve sound isolation.

name: Gypsum Board Patching Compound
description: Quick-setting filler material used for small repairs and patching holes in existing gypsum board surfaces.

name: Drywall Installation and Hanging
description: On-site activity of cutting, fitting, and fastening gypsum board panels to the framing or substrate.

name: Drywall Taping and Finishing
description: On-site application of joint tape and compound over gypsum board seams, fasteners, and corners to achieve a smooth surface.

name: Drywall Sanding and Surface Preparation
description: On-site sanding of dried joint compound and preparation of the gypsum board surface for primer and paint application.

name: Drywall Trim/Accessory Installation
description: On-site installation of corner beads, edge trims, and control joints as part of the gypsum board finishing process.

name: Gypsum Board Acoustic Sealant Application
description: On-site application of acoustic sealants around gypsum board perimeters and penetrations to achieve sound-rated assemblies.

name: Cement Mortar
description: A mixture of cement, sand, and water used for bricklaying, plastering, and general masonry work.

name: Lime Mortar
description: A breathable mortar made from lime, sand, and water, used in historic masonry and restoration.

name: Cement-Lime Mortar
description: A composite mortar blending Portland cement and lime for improved workability and adhesion.

name: Masonry Cement Mortar
description: A pre-blended mortar using masonry cement, sand, and water for uniform strength and color.

name: Thin-Set Mortar
description: A polymer-modified adhesive mortar used for bonding tile and stone to substrates in thin layers.

name: Grout
description: A fluid mortar used to fill joints between tiles, masonry units, or voids in reinforced masonry.

name: Fireproof Mortar
description: A refractory mortar formulated to withstand high temperatures for fireplaces, chimneys, and flues.

name: Pointing Mortar
description: A specialized mortar mix designed for repointing exposed masonry joints to match existing color and texture.

name: Bedding Mortar
description: A mortar used as a leveling base for laying masonry units or setting stone flooring slabs.

name: Scratch Coat Mortar
description: A rough base coat applied over lath or masonry to provide a key for subsequent plaster layers.

name: Stucco Mortar
description: A durable exterior finish mortar of cement, lime, sand, and water applied in multiple coats to building facades.

name: Repair Mortar
description: A pre-formulated mortar for patching and restoring deteriorated concrete or masonry surfaces.

name: Render Mortar
description: A smooth coating mortar applied externally to walls for protection and decorative finish.

name: Mortar Bed
description: The continuous layer of mortar onto which masonry units or tiles are laid to ensure uniform load transfer.

name: Mortar Joint
description: The horizontal (bed) or vertical (head) gap between masonry units filled with mortar to bond and seal the assembly.

name: Mortar Mixing
description: On-site combining of cementitious binder, aggregate, water, and additives to produce a workable mortar batch.

name: Pointing
description: On-site finishing of exposed mortar joints by tooling or applying fresh mortar to achieve desired profile and weathertightness.

name: Mortar Application
description: On-site spreading, throwing, or troweling of mortar onto surfaces or between units during masonry construction.

name: Mortar Curing
description: On-site moisture retention and temperature control of freshly applied mortar to ensure proper hydration and strength gain.

name: Construction Adhesive
description: High-strength adhesive used for bonding building materials such as drywall, panels, and trim to substrates.

name: Tile Adhesive/Thinset
description: Cementitious or polymer-modified adhesive mortar used to bond ceramic, porcelain, or stone tiles to floors and walls.

name: Caulk
description: Flexible sealant used for filling gaps and joints around windows, doors, plumbing fixtures, and between dissimilar materials.

name: Expansion Joint Sealant
description: Elastomeric sealant formulated to accommodate movement in expansion and control joints in concrete and masonry.

name: Acoustic Sealant
description: Non-hardening, flexible sealant used to seal gaps in walls and ceilings for sound attenuation and air sealing.

name: Firestop Sealant
description: Intumescent or fire-rated sealant used to seal penetrations in fire-resistance-rated walls and floors.

name: Glazing Sealant
description: Weatherproof sealant used to set and seal glass panes into window and curtain wall frames.

name: Roofing Sealant/Lap Cement
description: Viscous adhesive sealant used to bond and seal overlapping layers of roofing membranes and flashings.

name: Epoxy Adhesive
description: Two-part resin adhesive used for high-strength bonding of concrete anchors, dowels, and structural repairs.

name: Carpet Adhesive
description: Pressure-sensitive or wet-lay adhesive used to bond carpet floor coverings to subfloor surfaces.

name: Wallcovering Adhesive
description: Paste or adhesive formulated for installing wallpaper, vinyl wallcovering, or fabric wall panels.

name: Panel/Drywall Adhesive
description: Construction adhesive specifically formulated for bonding gypsum wallboard or paneling to framing.

name: Sealant Backer Rod
description: Polyethylene or foam rod placed into joints before sealant application to control depth and shape of the sealant bead.

name: Primer/Sealer for Sealants
description: Liquid primer applied to substrate surfaces to improve adhesion and prevent staining from sealant components.

name: Apply Adhesive/Sealant
description: On-site installation activity involving the application of adhesive or sealant to building substrates using caulking guns, trowels, or rollers.

name: Cure/Finish Sealant Joint
description: On-site activity to tool, shape, and allow sealant joints to properly cure for weathertightness and finish quality.

name: Mask and Protect Adjacent Surfaces
description: On-site preparation activity involving taping and masking of surfaces adjacent to sealant joints to ensure clean application.

name: Fully-Adhered Membrane
description: A roofing membrane fully bonded to the substrate using adhesive, providing a seamless weatherproof layer.

name: Mechanically-Fastened Membrane
description: A roofing membrane secured with fasteners and plates along seams, commonly used in single-ply systems.

name: Ballasted Membrane
description: A loosely-laid roofing membrane held in place by a ballast layer of stone, pavers, or gravel.

name: Self-Adhered Membrane
description: A membrane with a factory-applied adhesive backing that bonds to the substrate upon installation without additional adhesives.

name: Torch-Applied Membrane
description: A modified bitumen membrane installed by melting the underside with a propane torch to bond it to the substrate.

name: Protection Board / Cover Board
description: A rigid board installed over the roofing membrane to protect it from physical damage during subsequent trades or occupancy.

name: Membrane Flashing / Flashing Strips
description: Narrow strips of membrane material used to seal transitions, penetrations, and terminations against water ingress.

name: Roof Membrane Adhesive / Bonding Agent
description: Chemical adhesive or solvent used to bond membrane layers or membrane to substrate during installation.

name: Membrane Seam Tape / Seam Sealant
description: Adhesive tape or liquid sealant applied at membrane overlaps to create watertight joints between sheets.

name: Edge Metal / Fascia Flashing
description: Metal termination bars and profiles at roof edges that secure and seal the membrane perimeter.

name: Roof Drain / Drain Flashing Assembly
description: Drain components and their integrated flashing collars that seal the membrane around roof drainage outlets.

name: Pipe Penetration Boot / Pipe Flashing
description: Preformed rubber or membrane boot that seals the membrane around pipe penetrations through the roofing system.

name: Expansion Joint Cover (Roof)
description: A flexible assembly spanning building expansion joints that accommodates movement while maintaining membrane continuity.

name: Membrane Installation (Activity)
description: On-site placement and bonding of roofing membrane sheets or liquid-applied coatings to the prepared substrate.

name: Membrane Seaming / Welding (Activity)
description: Joining adjacent membrane sheets via heat-welding, solvent-welding, or adhesive taping to create a continuous waterproof layer.

name: Membrane Termination / Edge Securing (Activity)
description: Fastening and sealing the membrane at roof edges, parapets, curbs, and penetrations using termination bars and sealants.

name: Membrane Testing (Water/Flood Testing)
description: On-site verification of membrane system watertightness by flooding or conducting electronic leak detection after installation.

name: Acoustic Panel Core Material
description: The sound-absorbing inner layer of an acoustic panel, typically made from fiberglass, mineral wool, foam, or recycled materials.

name: Acoustic Panel Fabric Wrap
description: The decorative outer covering adhered to or stretched over the panel core, available in various colors, textures, and acoustic-transparent weaves.

name: Acoustic Panel Perimeter Frame
description: The rigid border or edging around the panel that provides structural stability and mounting points.

name: Acoustic Panel Mounting Bracket
description: A hardware piece used to attach the acoustic panel to walls, ceilings, or other substrates.

name: Acoustic Panel Suspension Cable
description: A wire or cable system for suspending acoustic panels from ceilings as clouds or baffles.

name: Perforated Acoustic Panel
description: A variant of acoustic panel with a perforated face (often wood, metal, or gypsum) that allows sound to pass through to an absorbent backing.

name: Acoustic Baffle
description: A vertically suspended linear or curved acoustic element hung from ceilings to reduce reverberation in large spaces.

name: Acoustic Cloud Panel
description: A ceiling-suspended horizontal or angled acoustic panel array designed to absorb sound in open-plan areas.

name: Acoustic Ceiling Tile
description: A modular acoustic panel designed to fit into a suspended ceiling grid system for room-wide sound control.

name: Acoustic Wall Panel System
description: An integrated assembly of multiple panels, tracks, and accessories forming a continuous acoustic treatment on a wall surface.

name: Acoustic Panel Installation
description: The on-site process of mounting and securing acoustic panels to walls, ceilings, or support structures.

name: Acoustic Panel Layout and Marking
description: The site activity of measuring and marking panel positions on substrates prior to installation.

name: Bass Trap
description: A specialized thick acoustic panel or corner-mounted device designed to absorb low-frequency sound energy.

name: Acoustic Sound Diffuser Panel
description: A panel with a sculpted or stepped surface that scatters reflected sound rather than absorbing it, improving spatial acoustics.

name: Tile Flooring
description: Individual hard surface units (ceramic, porcelain, stone, or terracotta) installed in a pattern over a substrate with grouted joints.

name: Sheet Flooring
description: Continuous roll-goods such as vinyl, linoleum, or rubber sheet adhered or loose-laid over the subfloor.

name: Plank Flooring
description: Long, narrow floor boards — engineered wood, luxury vinyl, or laminate — joined via click-lock or glue-down systems.

name: Seamless/Resinous Flooring
description: Poured and troweled polymer (epoxy, polyurethane, or MMA) floor toppings that cure into a jointless, monolithic surface.

name: Carpet Flooring
description: Textile floor covering available as broadloom carpet, carpet tiles, or runner mats installed over cushion or direct glue-down.

name: Terrazzo Flooring
description: Composite material of marble/glass chips set in a cementitious or epoxy binder, ground and polished to a smooth finish.

name: Wood Strip Flooring
description: Solid or engineered narrow wood strips nailed, stapled, or glued to the subfloor in a running bond pattern.

name: Floor Underlayment
