description: Intermediate layer placed between the structural subfloor and the visible finish to provide leveling, sound isolation, or moisture protection.

name: Floor Finish Installation
description: On-site process of laying, adhering, fastening, or pouring the final floor surface material over the prepared substrate.

name: Floor Grinding & Polishing
description: On-site mechanical abrasion of concrete or stone floors to achieve a specified smoothness, sheen, or exposed aggregate finish.

name: Floor Sealing & Coating
description: Application of protective sealers, waxes, or clear topcoats to the finished floor surface for durability and stain resistance.

name: Floor Base & Transition Strip
description: Trim elements (wall base, reducer strips, T-moldings) that cover expansion gaps and transition between different floor finishes.

name: Access Floor System
description: Raised modular pedestal-and-panel floor system creating a plenum for cables and air distribution beneath the finished surface.

name: Slip-Resistant Flooring
description: Floor finish with integrally textured surface, grit additives, or specialized profile designed to meet wet/dry slip-resistance codes.

name: Conductive/Antistatic Flooring
description: Specialized floor finish with embedded conductive elements to dissipate static electricity in sensitive environments like data centers or labs.

name: Sport Flooring
description: Engineered floor system (e.g., sprung wood, polyurethane pour-in-place, or rubber sheet) designed for athletic performance and impact absorption.

name: Below-Grade Waterproofing
description: Application of waterproofing membranes and systems to foundation walls, basements, and below-grade structures to prevent groundwater ingress.

name: Above-Grade Waterproofing
description: Installation of weather-resistant barriers and sealants on exterior walls and surfaces above ground level to resist wind-driven rain and moisture.

name: Roof Waterproofing
description: Laying of waterproof membranes, coatings, and flashings on roof decks to prevent water penetration and protect the building envelope.

name: Wet Room Waterproofing
description: Application of liquid-applied or sheet membranes in showers, bathrooms, and other wet areas to create watertight substrates before tiling.

name: Balcony & Terrace Waterproofing
description: Installation of waterproofing systems on exposed exterior decks, balconies, and terraces to protect the structure beneath from standing water.

name: Green Roof Waterproofing
description: Application of root-resistant waterproofing membranes beneath green roof assemblies to prevent water and root damage to the structure.

name: Liquid-Applied Membrane Waterproofing
description: Spraying, rolling, or troweling of liquid polymer or bitumen compounds that cure to form a seamless waterproof barrier.

name: Sheet Membrane Waterproofing
description: Installation of pre-fabricated elastomeric or bituminous sheet membranes adhered or mechanically fastened to surfaces for water protection.

name: Bentonite Clay Waterproofing
description: Placement of sodium bentonite panels or sheets that swell upon contact with water to self-seal joints and cracks in below-grade applications.

name: Cementitious Waterproofing
description: Application of cement-based coatings mixed with waterproofing additives, commonly used on concrete and masonry surfaces in wet areas and tanks.

name: Waterstops
description: Pre-formed strips or profiles of PVC, rubber, or bentonite installed at construction joints in concrete to block water passage.

name: Joint Sealants & Expansion Joints
description: Elastomeric sealants and preformed joint filler materials placed at movement joints to maintain waterproof continuity while accommodating building movement.

name: Drainage Boards & Cavity Drain Membranes
description: Profiled plastic sheets or composite boards installed against waterproofing to create a drained air gap and relieve hydrostatic pressure.

name: Flashing
description: Prefabricated or site-formed metal, rubberized, or self-adhesive strips installed at roof-wall intersections, chimneys, and penetrations to divert water.

name: Dampproofing
description: Application of damp-proof coatings or courses to resist moisture migration through walls and slabs without resisting standing water pressure.

name: Waterproofing Membrane Protection Board
description: Rigid boards or sheets installed over waterproofing membranes to shield them from damage during backfilling or subsequent construction.

name: Wall Formwork
description: Vertical form panel system that shapes and supports poured concrete walls until they gain sufficient strength.

name: Beam Formwork
description: Temporary support and mold assembly used to cast reinforced concrete beams of various spans and depths.

name: Stair Formwork
description: Custom-shaped falsework and form panels used to cast concrete stair flights and landings in place.

name: Foundation Formwork
description: Formwork system constructed to shape and confine concrete footings, strip footings, pad foundations or raft slabs.

name: Table Formwork
description: Large, prefabricated formwork table crane-lifted as a single unit for repetitive slab casting on multi-story buildings.

name: Climbing Formwork
description: Self-raising formwork system that moves upward floor-by-floor using hydraulic or mechanical climbing mechanisms.

name: Tunnel Formwork
description: Room-sized steel form that casts walls and slab simultaneously to produce repetitive cellular units such as hotel rooms or apartments.

name: Flying Formwork
description: Large panel formwork system flown by crane between floors without full dismantling, used for rapid slab construction.

name: Gang Formwork
description: Pre-assembled group of form panels bolted together and handled as a single unit to speed repetitive wall pours.

name: Formwork Shoring & Scaffolding
description: Temporary vertical supports, props, and falsework used to hold formwork in alignment and transfer loads to ground.

name: Formwork Ties & Hardware
description: Tie rods, cones, wing nuts, and waler brackets that hold form panels together against concrete lateral pressure.

name: Form Release Agent Application
description: On-site application of chemical release agent to formwork surfaces to prevent concrete adhesion and ensure clean stripping.

name: Formwork Stripping & Removal
description: On-site dismantling and removal of formwork after concrete has cured to the required strength for self-support.

name: Formwork Cleaning & Refurbishment
description: On-site cleaning, oiling, repairing, and reconditioning of used form panels between pours to maintain quality.

name: Formwork Alignment & Survey
description: On-site setting out, leveling, plumbing, and positional checking of formwork before concrete placement.

name: Insulated Concrete Form (ICF) Installation
description: On-site assembly of interlocking expanded polystyrene form blocks that remain in place as permanent insulation and formwork.

name: Stay-in-Place Formwork Installation
description: On-site installation of permanent formwork elements, typically profiled steel decking or precast concrete planks, left in place after pouring.

name: Formwork Safety Netting & Guardrails
description: Edge protection systems and safety nets installed on formwork perimeters for fall protection during concrete operations.

name: Formwork Striking Time
description: The determination and scheduling of the minimum curing period before formwork can be safely removed based on concrete strength gain and structural loading requirements.

name: Vertical Formwork Removal
description: The on-site process of dismantling and removing column, wall, and other vertical element forms after concrete has achieved sufficient initial set.

name: Horizontal/Slab Formwork Striking
description: The controlled removal of soffit formwork, props, and shoring from concrete slabs and beams, often staged to allow progressive load transfer to the curing slab.

name: Formwork Cleaning and Preparation for Reuse
description: The on-site cleaning, oiling, and repair of struck formwork panels to make them ready for re-erection in subsequent concrete pours.

name: Striking of Slipforms
description: The deactivation and dismantling of continuously moving slipform systems after the concrete structure has been completed to its final elevation.

name: Formwork Release Agent Application
description: The chemical or oil-based compounds applied to formwork faces prior to concreting to facilitate clean separation during striking.

name: Temporary Propping During Striking
description: The reusable steel or aluminum adjustable props and back-propping system used to support slabs during staged formwork removal.

name: Striking Tools and Equipment
description: The on-site hand tools, wedges, pry bars, hammers, and mechanical strikers used to separate formwork from hardened concrete without damaging the structure.

name: Edge Formwork Striking
description: The removal of perimeter formwork, stop-ends, and edge shutters from slab edges, openings, and construction joints.

name: Striking Inspection and Quality Control
description: The on-site inspection of exposed concrete surfaces after formwork removal to check for defects such as honeycombing, surface blemishes, or edge spalling requiring remediation.

name: Rebar & Reinforcement Placement
description: Positioning and tying steel reinforcing bars or mesh within formwork before concrete placement to provide tensile strength.

name: Concrete Mix Design & Batching
description: Proportioning cement, aggregates, water, and admixtures to achieve specified strength, workability, and durability for the pour.

name: Concrete Transport & Delivery
description: Moving fresh concrete from the truck mixer to the placement point via chutes, conveyor belts, buckets, or pump lines.

name: Concrete Pumping
description: Using a mechanical pump to convey liquid concrete through hoses or pipes to elevated or distant pour locations.

name: Concrete Placement & Spreading
description: Depositing fresh concrete into formwork and spreading it evenly to fill all voids around reinforcement.

name: Concrete Compaction & Vibration
description: Using internal or external vibrators to remove entrapped air bubbles from fresh concrete, ensuring dense consolidation.

name: Concrete Screeding & Leveling
description: Striking off excess concrete and bringing the surface to the required grade using a straightedge or power screed.

name: Concrete Troweling & Finishing
description: Smoothing and compacting the concrete surface with hand or power trowels to achieve the specified finish texture.

name: Concrete Jointing
description: Creating control, construction, or expansion joints by saw-cutting, tooling, or placing joint strips to control cracking.

name: Formwork Stripping & Surface Repair
description: Removing formwork after concrete has cured sufficiently and patching any surface defects such as honeycombing or bug holes.

name: Ready-Mix Concrete
description: Factory-batched concrete delivered in a plastic state to the site, the primary bulk material placed during concrete pouring.

name: Concrete Admixtures
description: Chemical additives such as plasticizers, retarders, accelerators, or air-entrainers blended into concrete to modify its fresh or hardened properties.

name: Concrete Anchor Bolts & Embeds
description: Steel anchor rods, plates, or inserts cast into concrete to provide connection points for structural steel, equipment, or other building elements.

name: Pour Stop & Bulkhead
description: Temporary or permanent barriers installed within formwork to define the edge of a concrete placement lift or pour sequence.

name: Concrete Testing & Quality Control
description: Sampling fresh concrete for slump, air content, and temperature tests and casting cylinders for compressive strength verification.

name: Curing Compound
description: A liquid membrane-forming compound applied to freshly placed concrete surfaces to retard moisture loss during hydration.

name: Wet Curing
description: A method of concrete curing involving continuous or frequent application of water via ponding, spraying, or saturated coverings.

name: Steam Curing
description: An accelerated concrete curing method using controlled steam application to promote early strength gain in precast or in-situ elements.

name: Curing Blanket
description: An insulating or moisture-retaining blanket placed over fresh concrete to maintain temperature and humidity during the curing period.

name: Curing Membrane
description: A continuous impermeable film, typically liquid-applied or sheet-based, that seals moisture in freshly placed concrete.

name: Internal Curing
description: A technique using pre-wetted lightweight aggregate or superabsorbent polymers within the concrete mix to provide internal water reservoirs for hydration.

name: Curing Period Monitoring
description: The on-site inspection and measurement of temperature, humidity, and time conditions to verify compliance with curing specifications.

name: Moisture Retaining Cover
description: A sheet material such as polyethylene, burlap, or synthetic fabric placed over concrete to reduce evaporation during curing.

name: Curing Temperature Control
description: The on-site regulation of concrete temperature through heating or cooling methods to ensure proper hydration rate and avoid thermal cracking.

name: Concrete Slab Finishing
description: On-site finishing of concrete floor slabs including power troweling, surface hardeners, and curing compounds.

name: Concrete Wall Finishing
description: On-site finishing of cast-in-place concrete walls including patching, grinding, and surface preparation for coatings.

name: Concrete Surface Sealing
description: Application of liquid sealers, densifiers, or waterproofing membranes to finished concrete surfaces.

name: Concrete Staining & Dyeing
description: On-site application of acid stains, water-based stains, or reactive dyes to color concrete surfaces.

name: Concrete Polishing
description: Mechanical grinding, honing, and polishing of concrete floor surfaces to achieve specified gloss and aggregate exposure.

name: Concrete Texture & Broom Finish
description: Creation of slip-resistant or decorative texture on concrete surfaces using brooms, stamps, or rollers.

name: Troweled Concrete Topping
description: Application and finishing of thin cementitious topping layers over base concrete for leveling or decorative effect.

name: Concrete Joint Finishing
description: Forming, tooling, and sealing of construction joints, control joints, and isolation joints in concrete.

name: Exposed Aggregate Finish
description: Revealing decorative aggregate on concrete surfaces through surface retarders or washing techniques.

name: Concrete Formliner Finish
description: Installation of formliners to cast architectural patterns, textures, or graphics into concrete surfaces.

name: Concrete Repair & Patching
description: On-site repair of concrete surface defects including spalls, honeycombing, and cracks prior to final finish.

name: Curing Application
description: On-site application of wet curing, membrane-forming curing compounds, or insulating blankets to concrete.

name: Concrete Blast Cleaning
description: Abrasive blast cleaning of concrete surfaces to remove laitance and prepare for coatings or sealers.

name: Glazing Panel
description: A single factory-fabricated unit of glass or other transparent material installed within a frame, forming the basic infill element of a glazed opening.

name: Glazing Frame
description: The structural perimeter (e.g., sash, curtain wall mullion, or storefront section) that supports and seals the glazing panel in place.

name: Glazing Gasket
description: A pre-formed elastomeric seal compressed between the glazing panel and frame to provide weather-tightness and accommodate thermal movement.

name: Glazing Spacer Bar
description: A hollow or solid profile separating two or more glass panes in an insulated glazing unit, often containing desiccant to prevent internal condensation.

name: Insulated Glazing Unit (IGU)
description: A sealed assembly of two or more glazing panels separated by spacer bars and gas-filled cavities to improve thermal and acoustic performance.

name: Laminated Glazing
description: A glazing panel composed of two or more glass plies bonded with an interlayer (e.g., PVB) to enhance safety, security, and sound insulation.

name: Tempered Glazing
description: A heat-treated glass panel with increased mechanical strength and, upon breakage, fragments into small granular pieces for safety.

name: Low-E Coated Glazing
description: A glazing panel with a microscopically thin metallic oxide coating that reflects long-wave infrared radiation to reduce heat loss while transmitting visible light.

name: Tinted Glazing
description: A glazing panel incorporating colorants in the glass body or a surface coating to reduce solar heat gain and glare.

name: Reflective Glazing
description: A glazing panel with a metallic or dielectric reflective coating applied to one surface to control solar radiation and provide privacy.

name: Self-Cleaning Glazing
description: A glazing panel with a photocatalytic or hydrophilic coating that breaks down organic dirt and allows rain to wash it away.

name: Electrochromic Glazing
description: A smart glazing panel whose tint or transparency can be electrically switched to dynamically control solar gain and daylight.

name: Thermochromic Glazing
description: A smart glazing panel whose light transmission changes passively in response to temperature to reduce solar heat gain in warm conditions.

name: Fire-Rated Glazing
description: A glazing assembly tested to withstand fire exposure for a rated duration, using special glass and framing to maintain integrity and limit heat transfer.

name: Bullet-Resistant Glazing
description: A multilayered glazing assembly designed to stop projectiles and forced entry, typically combining glass and polycarbonate laminates.

name: Decorative Glazing
description: A glazing panel with surface treatments such as etching, fritting, acid-frosting, or embedded patterns for privacy and aesthetic effect.

name: Spandrel Glazing
description: An opaque or back-paneled glazing unit installed in curtain wall spandrel zones to conceal floor slabs, mechanical equipment, or structural elements.

name: Curtain Wall Glazing System
description: A non-load-bearing aluminum-framed facade system that supports and seals a continuous array of glazing panels across the building exterior.

name: Storefront Glazing System
description: A ground-floor or low-rise aluminum-framed glazing system designed for retail and commercial entrances with thermal breaks and integral doors.

name: Window Glazing System
description: A complete framed opening assembly (operable or fixed) installed into a structural rough opening, including sash, hinges, hardware, and glazing infill.

name: Skylight Glazing System
description: A sloped or flat roof-mounted glazing assembly, often with a structural curb, condensation gutter, and diffusing or shading attachments.

name: Sloped Glazing System
description: An inclined structural glazing assembly used in atria, canopies, or roof lights that must resist rainwater run-off, snow load, and solar gain.

name: Structural Glazing System
description: A facade system where glazing panels are structurally bonded to a support frame using silicone adhesive, creating a smooth external glass surface without exposed caps.

name: Point-Supported Glazing System
description: A structural glazing system where panels are supported at discrete points by stainless steel spider fittings and tension cables or mullions.

name: Glazing Installation Activity
description: The on-site process of placing and securing glazing panels into frames, including setting blocks, shims, and temporary bracing.

name: Glazing Gasketing Activity
description: The on-site installation of pre-formed gaskets into frame channels before or after the glazing panel is placed.

name: Glazing Sealant Application Activity
description: The on-site application of wet sealant at glazing perimeter joints, including tooling and curing, to complete the weather seal.

name: Glazing Panel Handling & Lifting Activity
description: The on-site receipt, uncrating, vertical lifting, and positioning of large or heavy glazing panels using vacuum lifters, cranes, or suction cups.

name: Glazing Quality Control & Testing Activity
description: The on-site inspection and performance testing of installed glazing (e.g., water spray test, air-leakage test, thermal imaging) to verify specified performance.

name: Paint Coat
description: The liquid coating material applied to surfaces, consisting of pigments, binders, solvents, and additives.

name: Primer Coat
description: An initial preparatory coating applied to improve adhesion of subsequent paint layers and seal the substrate.

name: Paint System
description: The complete layered assembly of primer, intermediate, and finish coats specified for a given substrate and performance requirement.

name: Paint Roller Application
description: The on-site application of paint using a roller tool to cover large flat surface areas efficiently.

name: Paint Brush Application
description: The on-site application of paint using a brush for cutting in edges, corners, and detailed or narrow areas.

name: Spray Painting Application
description: The on-site application of paint using spray equipment to achieve a uniform finish on complex or large surfaces.

name: Surface Preparation
description: The on-site preparation work including cleaning, sanding, filling, and masking prior to paint application.

name: Protective Coating
description: A specialized paint formulation applied to protect surfaces from corrosion, moisture, fire, or chemical exposure.

name: Decorative Finish Coat
description: The final visible paint layer that provides color, sheen, texture, and aesthetic appearance to the surface.

name: Varnish
description: A transparent or semi-transparent coating applied over surfaces to provide a protective glossy finish while revealing the substrate.

name: Wall Painting
description: The on-site activity of applying paint to interior or exterior vertical wall surfaces.

name: Ceiling Painting
description: The on-site activity of applying paint to overhead ceiling surfaces.

name: Trim & Millwork Painting
description: The on-site activity of painting architectural trim, baseboards, door frames, window frames, and other millwork elements.

name: Paint Inspection & Touch-Up
description: The final on-site quality inspection and remedial touching up of painted surfaces before handover.

name: System Startup and Initialization
description: The first-time power-up and initialization of building systems including verifying power supplies, control panel readiness, and system status indicators.

name: Functional Performance Testing
description: Verification that each building system or component operates according to its design intent, sequence of operations, and functional specifications under normal conditions.

name: Integrated Systems Testing
description: Testing the interaction and interoperability between multiple building systems such as HVAC, lighting, fire alarm, and BMS to confirm coordinated operation.

name: Control System Calibration
description: Adjustment and calibration of sensors, actuators, controllers, and setpoints across building automation and control systems to achieve specified accuracy.

name: Air and Water Balancing
description: Measurement and adjustment of airflow rates, water flow rates, and pressure differentials in HVAC distribution systems to meet design specifications.

name: Sequence of Operations Verification
description: Step-by-step verification that programmed control sequences execute correctly under various modes such as occupied, unoccupied, morning warm-up, and night setback.

name: Alarm and Notification Testing
description: Testing of all alarm conditions, warning signals, and notification devices including visual, audible, and remote alerts for fire, security, and system faults.

name: Safety and Life Safety System Testing
description: Verification of fire alarm, sprinkler, smoke control, emergency lighting, and egress systems to confirm code-compliant operation in emergency scenarios.

name: Electrical System Commissioning
description: Testing of switchgear, distribution panels, transformers, uninterruptible power supplies, emergency generators, and transfer switches under load and fault conditions.

name: Plumbing and Piping System Testing
description: Pressure testing, leak testing, and flow verification of domestic water, sanitary drainage, stormwater, and gas piping systems throughout the building.

name: HVAC System Commissioning
description: Comprehensive testing of heating, ventilation, and air conditioning equipment including chillers, boilers, air handlers, VAV boxes, and terminal units.

name: Lighting and Daylighting Commissioning
description: Verification of lighting control strategies, occupancy sensors, daylight harvesting, dimming, and scheduled lighting scenes across all zones.

name: Building Enclosure Commissioning
description: Testing of the building envelope including air barrier continuity, water penetration resistance, thermal performance, and fenestration seal integrity.

name: Verification Documentation and Reports
description: Preparation and submission of commissioning records, test reports, certificates of performance, and as-built documentation for all commissioned systems.

name: Seasonal Performance Testing
description: Deferred testing performed during both peak heating and peak cooling seasons to validate system performance under extreme outdoor conditions.

name: Training and Handover
description: Instruction of building owner and facility management staff on the operation, maintenance, and troubleshooting of all commissioned systems and controls.

name: Retro-Commissioning
description: Systematic re-testing and re-optimization of existing building systems to restore or improve performance relative to current operational requirements.

name: Witness and Hold Point Inspections
description: Scheduled on-site inspections at critical milestones where commissioning authority must witness and approve specific tests before work proceeds.

name: Factory Witness Testing
description: Off-site verification of major equipment performance at the manufacturer's facility before delivery and installation on the construction site.

name: Trend Logging and Data Analysis
description: Continuous monitoring, data logging, and analytical review of system performance trends over an extended period to confirm stable and efficient operation.

name: Steel Reinforcement Bars (Rebar)
description: Steel bars of various diameters and grades used as the primary tensile reinforcement in concrete structures.

name: Welded Wire Fabric (WWF)
description: Prefabricated steel mesh sheets used for reinforcing slabs, walls, and pavements.

name: Rebar Supports/Chairs
description: Plastic or metal devices used to support and maintain correct cover and spacing of reinforcement bars during concrete placement.

name: Tying Wire
description: Annealed steel wire used to manually tie intersecting rebars together before concrete pour.

name: Rebar Couplers/Mechanical Splices
description: Mechanical devices used to join two reinforcing bars end-to-end in lieu of lapped splices.

name: Reinforcement Spacers
description: Preformed components ensuring consistent spacing between rebar layers and between rebar and formwork.

name: Starter Bars/Dowel Bars
description: Pre-placed projecting reinforcement bars left protruding from a concrete pour for connecting to subsequent pours.

name: Shear Reinforcement (Stirrups/Links)
description: Closed-loop or open-shaped steel bars placed transversely in beams and columns to resist shear forces.

name: Tensioning Tendons/Strands
description: High-strength steel strands or bars used in post-tensioned or pre-tensioned concrete systems.

name: Rebar Bending/Drawing Schedule
description: On-site preparation and interpretation of bending schedules and shape codes for fabricating reinforcement to design specifications.

name: Fixing Column Reinforcement Cage
description: Assembling and tying vertical reinforcement bars with transverse links into a rigid cage within column formwork.

name: Fixing Beam Reinforcement
description: Placing and tying longitudinal bars and stirrups within beam formwork prior to concrete pouring.

name: Fixing Slab Reinforcement
description: Laying and tying bottom and top reinforcement mats in slab formwork, including edge reinforcement and openings.

name: Fixing Wall Reinforcement
description: Erecting vertical and horizontal rebars with ties in wall formwork to form a reinforced wall panel.

name: Fixing Foundation Reinforcement
description: Placing and securing rebar mats, starter bars, and dowels in foundation footings, rafts, and pile caps.

name: Post-Tensioning Stressing/Anchoring
description: On-site tensioning of prestressing strands or bars against the hardened concrete using hydraulic jacks and permanent anchorages.

name: Reinforcement Cover Block Installation
description: Placing concrete or plastic cover blocks between rebar and formwork to ensure the specified concrete cover depth.

name: Tying and Lapping Rebar
description: Manually tying intersecting rebars with wire and overlapping bars at splice locations per structural drawings.

name: Corrosion Protection/Coating Application
description: Applying epoxy coating, galvanizing, or other protective treatments to reinforcement bars on-site before embedment.

name: Reinforcement Inspection/Quality Check
description: Checking rebar size, spacing, cover depth, and tying integrity before concrete pour is approved.

name: Brick types
description: Varieties of clay or concrete masonry units including common, facing, engineering, and calcium silicate bricks used in wall construction.

name: Mortar types
description: Cement-lime, cement, lime, or thin-joint mortars that bond masonry units and accommodate movement.

name: Bond patterns
description: Arrangements of bricks such as running, Flemish, English, and stretcher bonds that determine wall appearance and structural behavior.

name: Reinforced masonry
description: Masonry walls incorporating vertical or horizontal steel reinforcement grouted into cores or cavities for seismic or load-bearing capacity.

name: Cavity wall construction
description: Two wythes of masonry separated by an airspace, with wall ties and insulation, forming a weather-resistant external wall assembly.

name: Masonry veneer
description: A single non-load-bearing wythe of brick attached to a structural backing, used as a decorative or weather-resistant cladding.

name: Stone masonry
description: The on-site laying of natural or reconstituted stone units for walls, cladding, or architectural features using mortar or dry-stack methods.

name: Masonry lintels and arches
description: Precast concrete, steel, or brick-arch elements spanning openings in masonry walls to support loads above doors and windows.

name: Movement joints
description: Controlled gaps with sealant or filler installed in masonry to accommodate thermal and moisture-induced expansion and contraction.

name: Scaffolding and access
description: Erection and dismantling of temporary support platforms and hoists required for safe bricklaying at height on building sites.

name: Masonry cleaning and pointing
description: Removal of mortar smears and stains from finished brickwork, and renewal of weathered or defective mortar joints.

name: Damp-proof courses
description: Horizontal or vertical sheets of impermeable material built into masonry to prevent rising or penetrating dampness.

name: Masonry chimneys and flues
description: Vertical brick or block enclosures housing flue liners for venting combustion products from fireplaces, boilers, or stoves.

name: Retaining walls
description: Masonry walls designed to resist lateral soil pressure, often constructed with battered faces, weep holes, and drainage backfill.

name: Brick pavers and paving
description: Installation of brick or clay pavers on prepared base courses for pedestrian or light vehicular surfaces outdoors.

name: Masonry inspection and testing
description: On-site sampling and testing of mortar cubes, brick compressive strength, and bond integrity to verify compliance with specifications.

name: Plaster Base Layer
description: The initial scratch or bonding coat applied directly to the substrate (masonry or lath) to provide adhesion for subsequent plaster coats.

name: Plaster Finish Coat
description: The final smooth or textured layer of plaster that forms the visible surface, which may be left plain, painted, or decorated.

name: Plaster Render (External)
description: A cement, lime, or polymer-based plaster applied to exterior building façades for weather protection and decorative finish.

name: Gypsum Plaster
description: A fast-setting plaster composed primarily of calcium sulfate hemihydrate, commonly used for interior wall and ceiling finishes.

name: Lime Plaster
description: A breathable plaster made from lime putty and sand, traditionally used on historic or solid masonry walls.

name: Cement Plaster
description: A durable, moisture-resistant plaster made from Portland cement, sand, and water, often used in wet areas and exteriors.

name: Clay Plaster
description: A natural, low-embodied-energy plaster made from clay, sand, and fiber, offering hygroscopic moisture regulation.

name: Acoustic Plaster
description: A specialized plaster containing sound-absorbent aggregates or fibers to reduce reverberation in interior spaces.

name: Decorative Plaster Molding
description: Cast or hand-applied ornamental plaster shapes such as cornices, ceiling roses, coves, and panel moldings fixed to walls or ceilings.

name: Plaster Key (on Lath)
description: The portion of wet plaster that squeezes through gaps in metal or wood lath and hardens to mechanically lock the plaster in place.

name: Metal Lath
description: A galvanized steel mesh or expanded metal sheet fixed to substrates as a reinforcement base for plaster application.

name: Plaster Bead / Trim
description: Perforated metal or PVC profiles (corner beads, stop beads, angle beads) embedded at plaster edges to form clean transitions and protect vulnerable corners.

name: Plaster Reinforcement Mesh
description: Alkali-resistant fiberglass or wire mesh embedded within plaster coats to control cracking and improve tensile strength.

name: Plasterwork Substrate Preparation
description: The on-site activity of cleaning, dampening, scratching, or applying bonding agents to the wall surface prior to plastering.

name: Scratch Coat Application
description: The on-site application of a first plaster coat that is cross-scratched to provide a mechanical key for subsequent coats.

name: Brown Coat Application
description: The on-site application of a second plaster coat used to build up thickness and level the surface before the finish coat.

name: Float and Set (Finish Plastering)
description: The on-site activity of applying the final plaster coat and troweling it to a smooth, dense surface finish.

name: Plaster Spray Application
description: The on-site mechanized spraying of wet plaster onto surfaces using a plaster spray machine for high-speed coverage.

name: Plaster Repair / Patching
description: The on-site activity of cutting out damaged plaster, applying bonding agents, and filling with new plaster to match existing surfaces.

name: Plaster Curing and Drying Management
description: The on-site controlled drying process (ventilation, heating, humidity control) to prevent cracking and ensure proper plaster strength development.

name: Plastering Over Insulation Board
description: The on-site application of a continuous plaster layer over rigid insulation boards fixed to walls as part of an internal or external insulation system.

name: Venetian Plaster Application
description: The on-site multi-coat application of polished lime-based plaster troweled to a high-gloss, marble-like finish.

name: Sgraffito Plasterwork
description: The on-site decorative technique of scratching through successive colored plaster layers to reveal patterns or images.

name: Stucco Application
description: The on-site application of exterior cement or polymer-based plaster (stucco) in multiple coats, often with a textured finish.

name: Plaster Skimming
description: The on-site application of a thin, smooth final plaster layer over existing plasterboard or old plaster to produce a fresh surface.

name: Tile Substrate Preparation
description: On-site preparation of the substrate surface including cleaning, leveling, priming, and moisture testing to ensure proper tile adhesion.

name: Thin-Set Mortar Application
description: On-site mixing and spreading of thin-set mortar or adhesive onto the prepared substrate for bonding tiles.

name: Tile Layout and Cutting
description: On-site planning of tile layout patterns and field cutting of tiles to fit edges, corners, and penetrations.

name: Tile Setting and Placement
description: On-site placement and positioning of tiles into the mortar bed with proper alignment, spacing, and leveling.

name: Grout Application
description: On-site filling of tile joints with grout, followed by cleaning and sealing of the grout lines.

name: Tile Expansion Joint Installation
description: On-site installation of expansion joints and sealants within the tile field to accommodate thermal and structural movement.

name: Tile Base and Transition Installation
description: On-site installation of tile baseboards, cove bases, and transition strips where tile meets other floor or wall finishes.

name: Tile Backer Board Installation
description: On-site installation of cementitious or waterproof tile backer board substrate for wet-area tile installations.

name: Waterproof Membrane Application for Tile
description: On-site application of liquid or sheet waterproofing membrane over backer board in shower, bath, and wet areas prior to tiling.

name: Ceramic and Porcelain Tile
description: Clay-based tiles fired at high temperatures, available glazed or unglazed, used for wall and floor installations.

name: Stone Tile
description: Natural stone tiles such as marble, granite, travertine, slate, and limestone used in building finish applications.

name: Glass and Mosaic Tile
description: Small-format glass, metal, or ceramic mosaic tiles mounted on mesh sheets for decorative wall and floor applications.

name: Quarry Tile and Paver Tile
description: Dense, through-body floor tiles and outdoor-rated paver tiles used in heavy-traffic and exterior applications.

name: Tile Trim and Edge Profiles
description: Metal or plastic profile strips installed at tile edges, corners, and terminations to provide a finished appearance and edge protection.

name: Tile Spacers and Leveling Systems
description: Plastic spacing devices and clip-and-wedge leveling systems used on-site to ensure consistent joint width and flat tile surfaces.

name: Tile Crack Isolation Membrane
description: Sheet or liquid-applied membrane installed beneath tile to prevent substrate cracks from telegraphing through the tile surface.

name: Heated Floor System Integration for Tile
description: On-site installation of in-floor radiant heating cables or mats embedded in the mortar bed beneath tile flooring.

name: Tile Sealer and Grout Sealer Application
description: On-site application of penetrating or surface sealers to protect porous tile and grout from staining and moisture ingress.

name: Air Handling Unit (AHU) Ductwork Connection
description: Ductwork sections that connect air handling units to the main distribution duct runs.

name: Supply Ductwork
description: Duct runs that deliver conditioned air from the air handling equipment to supply diffusers in occupied spaces.

name: Return Ductwork
description: Duct runs that convey air from return grilles back to the air handling unit or exhaust system.

name: Exhaust Ductwork
description: Duct runs that remove contaminated or stale air from spaces and discharge it to the outdoors.

name: Fresh Air Intake Ductwork
description: Duct sections that bring outdoor ventilation air into the mechanical system.

name: Rectangular Sheet Metal Duct
description: Prefabricated rectangular galvanized steel duct sections used for main distribution runs in commercial HVAC systems.

name: Spiral Round Duct
description: Factory-formed spiral-seam round metal duct used for low-pressure air distribution.

name: Flexible Duct
description: Helically-wound wire-reinforced flexible duct used for final branch connections from rigid duct to diffusers or terminals.

name: Duct Liner
description: Fibrous glass or foam lining applied to the interior of sheet metal ducts for sound attenuation and thermal insulation.

name: Ductwork Hangers & Supports
description: Metal straps, rods, trapeze assemblies, and seismic bracing that suspend and secure duct runs to the building structure.

name: Volume Control Damper
description: Manually adjustable blade damper installed within ductwork to regulate airflow to specific zones or branches.

name: Motorized Fire Damper
description: Fire-rated damper that automatically closes upon detection of heat to prevent fire spread through duct openings in fire-rated walls.

name: Smoke Damper
description: Damper that closes upon smoke detection to control the movement of smoke through ducts and air transfer openings.

name: Backdraft Damper
description: Gravity-operated or spring-loaded damper that permits airflow in one direction only and prevents reverse flow.

name: Duct-Mounted Access Door
description: Hinged or latched panel installed in duct walls to provide access for cleaning, inspection, and balancing.

name: Duct Takeoff Fitting
description: Sheet metal fitting that branches a smaller duct run from a larger main duct, including conical, conical-tapered, and 45-degree entry types.

name: Duct Elbow
description: Directional change fitting in ductwork available in various radii and with or without turning vanes.

name: Duct Transition & Reducer
description: Fitting that changes duct cross-sectional shape or size to connect different duct sections.

name: Duct Silencer / Sound Attenuator
description: Prefabricated duct section containing baffles or absorptive media to reduce airborne noise transmitted through ductwork.

name: Duct Sealing (Mastic/Tape)
description: On-site application of mastic, foil tape, or gaskets to seal duct joints and seams against air leakage.

name: Ductwork Pressure Testing
description: On-site testing of installed ductwork sections by pressurizing the system and measuring leakage rates to verify compliance with specifications.

name: Ductwork Installation Coordination
description: Layout and routing of ductwork on site in coordination with structural beams, plumbing, electrical conduits, and fire protection systems.

name: Diffuser & Grille Installation
description: On-site mounting of supply diffusers, return grilles, and exhaust registers at duct termination points in ceilings or walls.

name: Duct-Mounted Reheat Coil
description: Hot water or electric heating coil installed inside ductwork to provide zone-level temperature control.

name: Duct-Mounted Humidifier
description: Steam or evaporative humidifier installed within ductwork to add moisture to supply air.

name: VAV Box Duct Connection
description: Inlet and outlet duct connections to variable air volume terminal units, including the upstream duct and downstream distribution duct.

name: Plenum Box
description: Sheet metal or lined box connecting a duct branch to a diffuser, used to reduce air velocity and attenuate noise.

name: Kitchen Exhaust Duct
description: Grease-tight, non-combustible ductwork specifically designed for commercial kitchen hood exhaust systems.

name: Laboratory Exhaust Duct
description: Corrosion-resistant ductwork (often stainless steel or polypropylene) for fume hood exhaust in laboratory environments.

name: Pipework Routing
description: The on-site installation and laying of pipes along designated pathways within the building structure.

name: Pipework Supports and Hangers
description: Brackets, clamps, hangers, and anchors that secure pipework to building structure.

name: Pipework Insulation
description: Application of thermal or acoustic insulation material around pipes to prevent heat loss/gain or reduce noise.

name: Pipework Jointing and Connection
description: On-site joining of pipe sections and connection to fittings, valves, and equipment using welding, threading, solvent welding, or compression methods.

name: Pipework Testing and Commissioning
description: Pressure testing, leak testing, flushing, and balancing of installed pipework systems to verify performance.

name: Pipework Valves and Fittings
description: Valves, elbows, tees, reducers, flanges, and other fittings that control flow and connect pipe segments.

name: Pipework Penetrations and Firestopping
description: Creation of openings through building elements and subsequent fire-rated sealing around pipes passing through walls, floors, and ceilings.

name: Cold Water Pipework
description: Pipework system distributing potable cold water from mains supply or storage to fixtures and equipment.

name: Hot Water Pipework
description: Pipework system distributing heated water from water heaters or boilers to taps, showers, and other hot water outlets.

name: Heating Pipework
description: Pipework system circulating hot water or steam for space heating via radiators, underfloor loops, or fan coil units.

name: Sanitary Drainage Pipework
description: Gravity pipework system conveying wastewater and sewage from fixtures to building drains or sewers.

name: Stormwater Drainage Pipework
description: Pipework system collecting and conveying rainwater from roofs, gutters, and surface drains to disposal or storage.

name: Vented and Overflow Pipework
description: Pipework system providing venting to drainage stacks and overflow protection for tanks and cisterns.

name: Gas Pipework
description: Pipework system distributing natural gas or LPG from meter to appliances such as boilers, cookers, and heaters.

name: Fire Suppression Pipework
description: Pipework system supplying water to sprinklers, hose reels, hydrants, and other fire-fighting equipment.

name: Refrigerant Pipework
description: Copper or steel pipework connecting outdoor condensing units to indoor evaporator units in split HVAC and refrigeration systems.

name: Pipework Identification and Labeling
description: Application of color-coded bands, labels, and flow-direction arrows to pipes for system identification per standards.

name: Pipework Corrosion Protection
description: Application of protective coatings, wraps, or sacrificial anodes to buried or exposed pipework to prevent corrosion.

name: Cable Trays and Ladder Racks
description: Continuous rigid support structures mounted along ceilings or walls to route and organize electrical cabling in accessible pathways.

name: Conduit Systems (EMT/IMC/RMC/PVC)
description: Metal or plastic tubing that encloses and protects individual electrical wires, routed through walls, slabs, and ceilings.

name: Cable Trunking and Raceways
description: Enclosed rectangular channels with removable covers, installed on wall or floor surfaces for distributing cabling in finished areas.

name: Underfloor Duct and Cellular Floor Systems
description: Pre-formed ducts or cellular steel floor decks that distribute power and data cabling within the floor slab for flexible outlet placement.

name: Cable Basket and Mesh Systems
description: Wire mesh troughs for supporting low-voltage data, communication, and small power cables in ceiling voids and service corridors.

name: Cable Glands and Entry Fittings
description: Sealing and anchoring fittings at cable entry points into enclosures, panels, equipment, or through building penetrations.

name: Cable Ties, Clips, and Fasteners
description: Securing devices including nylon ties, metal clips, and adhesive mounts used to bundle and anchor cables to support structures.

name: Cable Markers and Identification Labels
description: Numbered rings, wrap-around labels, or heat-shrink tags applied to individual cables for circuit identification during commissioning and maintenance.

name: Firestopping and Cable Transit Seals
description: Intumescent wraps, putty pads, and sealant systems that restore fire-rated barriers where cables pass through walls or floors.

name: Cable Pulling and Installation Activity
description: On-site work of pulling, feeding, and routing conductors through installed conduit, tray, or raceway systems before termination.

name: Cable Termination and Connection Activity
description: Stripping, crimping, soldering, or lug-connecting cable ends to panels, devices, outlets, and distribution boards.

name: Cable Testing and Commissioning Activity
description: On-site verification of continuity, insulation resistance, polarity, and loop impedance after cable installation is complete.

name: Cable Dressing and Management Activity
description: Neatly arranging, bundling, and securing cables within panels, trays, and enclosures to ensure airflow, labeling visibility, and serviceability.

name: Cable Pathway Firestop Installation Activity
description: Installing fire-rated seals and wraps at every cable penetration through fire-resistance-rated building elements.

name: Wire (Conductors) per AWG Size
description: Individual insulated copper or aluminum conductors in standardized gauge sizes used for power distribution within the building.

name: Armored (BX/AC) and Metal-Clad Cable
description: Factory-assembled cable with a spiral metal armor providing mechanical protection, used for branch circuits in exposed or concealed locations.

name: Non-Metallic (NM/Romex) Cable
description: Factory-assembled sheathed cable with multiple insulated conductors, commonly used for residential and light commercial branch wiring.

name: Low-Voltage and Data Cabling (Cat 6/6A/Coax/Fiber)
description: Communication-grade cables for data, voice, video, and building automation signals, installed parallel to but separate from power cabling.

name: Mineral-Insulated (MI) Cable
description: Fire-resistant copper-sheathed cable with magnesium oxide insulation, specified for fire-pump feeders and emergency circuits in high-risk areas.

name: Service Entrance and Feeder Cabling
description: Large-gauge cables bringing utility power from the service point to the main distribution panel within the building.

name: Fire Sprinkler Piping
description: The network of pipes (typically steel, copper, or CPVC) that delivers water from the supply to sprinkler heads throughout the building.

name: Sprinkler Control Valve
description: A valve (e.g., gate valve, butterfly valve) used to isolate sections of the sprinkler system for maintenance or after activation.

name: Fire Sprinkler Pump
description: A pump that boosts water pressure to ensure adequate flow and pressure at sprinkler heads when the system demands it.

name: Sprinkler Water Supply Connection
description: The point where the sprinkler system connects to the building's water main, a dedicated fire water tank, or a fire hydrant.

name: Sprinkler System Riser
description: The vertical pipe assembly that distributes water from the supply to the horizontal branch piping on each floor.

name: Sprinkler Flow Switch
description: A monitoring device that detects water flow in the piping and sends an alarm signal to the fire alarm system.

name: Sprinkler Tamper Switch
description: A supervisory switch attached to control valves that triggers an alarm if a valve is partially closed or tampered with.

name: Sprinkler Drain Valve
description: A valve located at low points of the piping system to allow drainage for testing, maintenance, or freeze protection.

name: Sprinkler Pipe Hanger and Support
description: Structural supports, clamps, and hangers that secure sprinkler piping to the building's structural elements.

name: Sprinkler Escutcheon
description: A decorative or protective plate that covers the gap between a sprinkler head and the finished ceiling or wall surface.

name: Sprinkler Head Guard
description: A wire cage or protective shield installed around sprinkler heads in areas prone to mechanical impact.

name: Fire Sprinkler System Type
description: The classification of the sprinkler arrangement—wet pipe, dry pipe, pre-action, or deluge—dictated by the building's fire risk and ambient conditions.

name: Sprinkler System Room
description: A dedicated mechanical or fire protection room housing the sprinkler riser, pump, control valves, and monitoring equipment.

name: Sprinkler Pipe Insulation
description: Thermal insulation applied to sprinkler piping in unheated areas to prevent freezing within dry or wet pipe systems.

name: Sprinkler Installation and Testing
description: On-site installation, alignment, pressure testing, and commissioning of sprinkler piping, heads, and associated components.

name: Gypsum Board Panels
description: Standard drywall sheets made of gypsum plaster sandwiched between paper facings, available in various thicknesses for wall and ceiling assemblies.

name: Metal Stud Framing
description: Light-gauge galvanized steel studs and tracks that form the structural backing to which drywall panels are fastened.

name: Joint Compound (Mud)
description: A gypsum-based paste applied over tape and fastener heads to create smooth, seamless wall surfaces.

name: Drywall Tape
description: Paper or fiberglass mesh tape embedded in joint compound to reinforce seams between adjacent drywall panels.

name: Corner Beads
description: Metal, vinyl, or paper-faced trim installed at external corners to protect edges and provide a clean finished line.

name: Drywall Fasteners (Screws/Nails)
description: Specialized corrosion-resistant screws or ring-shank nails used to attach gypsum panels to studs or joists.

name: Drywall Cutting and Fitting
description: Measuring, scoring, snapping, and cutting panels to size, including cutouts for outlets, windows, and doors.

name: Panel Hanging and Fastening
description: Lifting and attaching gypsum boards to the framing in a staggered pattern, driving fasteners at specified spacing.

name: Taping and Bedding
description: Applying embedded tape over joints and the first coat of joint compound to fill and reinforce seams.

name: Mudding and Finishing
description: Applying successive coats of joint compound (fill, taping, finish coats) with progressive sanding to achieve the desired finish level.

name: Sanding and Surface Preparation
description: Smoothing dried joint compound with sandpaper or sanding screens, dust removal, and priming before paint or texture.

name: Water-Resistant (Greenboard) Drywall
description: Moisture-resistant gypsum panel with a green-colored paper facing, used in bathrooms, kitchens, and other high-humidity areas.

name: Fire-Rated (Type X) Drywall
description: Gypsum board with glass-fiber reinforcement and denser core, providing increased fire-resistance ratings for rated assemblies.

name: Mold-Resistant Drywall
description: Gypsum panel with treated paper or fiberglass facers and non-organic core additives that inhibit mold and mildew growth.

name: Sound-Insulating (Acoustic) Drywall
description: Denser, multi-layer gypsum panels or sound-damping boards designed to improve sound transmission class (STC) in party walls.

name: Flexible/Arched Drywall
description: Thinner, fiberglass-mat-faced gypsum panels that can be bent to form curved walls and radius ceilings.

name: Shaftliner Drywall
description: Non-structural, fire-resistant gypsum board used as a liner in elevator shafts, stairwells, and mechanical chases.

name: Exterior Gypsum Sheathing
description: Weather-resistant gypsum board with water-repellent facers used as a substrate beneath exterior cladding systems.

name: Ceiling Drywall Installation
description: Overhead installation of gypsum panels on ceiling joists or furring channels, requiring temporary bracing and specialized lifting equipment.

name: Drywall Texture Application
description: Sprayed, rolled, or hand-applied surface texturing (e.g., knockdown, orange peel, skip trowel) over finished drywall prior to painting.

name: Fire-Caulking and Penetration Sealing
description: Sealing gaps around pipes, ducts, and cables through drywall assemblies with firestop sealants to maintain fire-rated integrity.

name: Trim and Reveal Installation
description: Installing L-bead, J-bead, or reveal profiles to create clean edges around openings, expansion joints, and junctions with other materials.

name: Metal Furring and Resilient Channels
description: Hat-shaped channels or resilient sound-isolating clips and channels that decouple drywall from structure to reduce sound transmission.

name: Access Panels and Hatches
description: Pre-assembled metal or plastic framed doors installed flush in drywall ceilings and walls to allow maintenance access to building services.

name: Drywall Joint Compound Application
description: The process of applying joint compound (mud) over drywall seams, fasteners, and corners to create a smooth, uniform surface for finishing.

name: Joint Tape Embedding
description: The activity of embedding paper or mesh joint tape into the first coat of joint compound to reinforce drywall seams and prevent cracking.

name: Corner Bead Installation
description: Installing metal, plastic, or paper-faced corner beads at external drywall corners to provide a straight, durable edge for compound finishing.

name: Flattening and Skimming
description: Applying successive thin coats of joint compound over taped seams, gradually widening the application to feather the edges and achieve a flat finish.

name: Sanding and Smoothing
description: Abrading dried joint compound with sandpaper or mesh screens to eliminate ridges, tool marks, and imperfections prior to priming.

name: Internal Corner Finishing
description: Applying compound and tape to inside (concave) drywall corners, typically using pre-formed paper-faced metal corner strips or hand-folding techniques.

name: Fastener Spotting
description: Applying small dabs of joint compound over drywall screw or nail heads to conceal them and prevent rust bleed-through on finished surfaces.

name: Pre-Finished Drywall Patching
description: Filling and taping cutouts, damage repairs, or penetrations in gypsum board to restore a continuous finish surface.

name: Texture Application
description: Applying spray-on, knockdown, skip-trowel, or roller-applied texture finishes over joint-compounded surfaces for aesthetic or acoustic purposes.

name: Drywall Primer Application
description: Rolling or spraying a drywall-specific primer over the finished taped and jointed surface to seal the compound and prepare for paint.

name: Reflective / Radiant Barrier Insulation
description: Material with a reflective surface (typically aluminum foil) installed to reduce radiant heat transfer across air spaces.

name: Insulated Sheathing
description: Structural or non-structural board product combining insulation with a facing or substrate, installed on the exterior of wall framing.

name: Insulated Metal Panel
description: Factory-assembled sandwich panel with a foam insulation core between two metal faces, used for building enclosures and roofs.

name: Structural Insulated Panel (SIP)
description: Composite building panel consisting of an insulating foam core bonded between two structural facing layers (typically OSB) for walls, roofs, and floors.

name: Insulation Vapor Retarder / Air Barrier
description: Sheet membrane or facing material (kraft paper, foil, polyethylene, or smart membrane) integrated with or applied over insulation to control moisture diffusion.

name: Insulation Fastening & Accessories
description: Hardware and supports including insulation hangers, pins, washers, tape, mesh, and adhesives used to secure insulation in place.

name: Blown-In Attic Insulation Installation
description: On-site process of pneumatically conveying loose-fill insulation material into attic spaces to a specified depth and density.

name: Spray-Applied Insulation Installation
description: On-site application of two-component spray polyurethane foam or spray-applied cellulose using specialized equipment.

name: Cavity Wall Insulation Installation
description: Installation of insulation material within the sealed cavity of masonry cavity walls, often via injection or partial-fill batts.

name: Exterior Insulation and Finish System (EIFS)
description: Multi-layer exterior wall cladding system combining rigid insulation board with a reinforced base coat and textured finish.

name: Below-Grade / Foundation Insulation
description: Installation of rigid insulation board on the exterior or interior of foundation walls and under slabs to control heat loss to the ground.

name: Cementitious Screed
description: A traditional sand-cement mortar screed applied wet and trowelled smooth to form a level, durable base for floor finishes.

name: Anhydrite/Calcium Sulfate Screed
description: A self-levelling, flowable screed based on calcium sulfate binder, offering faster drying and reduced shrinkage compared to cementitious screed.

name: Bonded Screed
description: A thin screed layer applied directly onto a prepared concrete base with a bonding agent to ensure monolithic adhesion.

name: Unbonded Screed
description: A screed laid over a separating membrane or slip layer on top of insulation or a substrate, not bonded to the structural slab.

name: Floating Screed
description: A screed placed over a layer of thermal or acoustic insulation, isolated from the structural slab and walls to reduce sound transmission.

name: Heated Floor Screed
description: A screed incorporating embedded underfloor heating pipes or cables, typically anhydrite or cement-based, designed to encase and distribute heat evenly.

name: Lightweight Screed
description: A screed using lightweight aggregates such as expanded clay, perlite, or foam beads to reduce dead load on the structure.

name: Fast-Drying Screed
description: A specialized screed formulated with accelerators or low-water-content binders to achieve rapid drying and early traffic loading.

name: Polymer-Modified Screed
description: A screed enhanced with polymer additives to improve flexural strength, adhesion, and resistance to cracking.

name: Self-Levelling Underlayment
description: A high-flow, pumpable screed compound that levels itself by gravity, used to smooth irregularities before final floor finishes.

name: Screed Reinforcement Mesh
description: Steel or synthetic fibre mesh embedded within the screed to control cracking and increase tensile strength.

name: Expansion/Contraction Joint Installation
description: The installation of pre-formed joint profiles or formed saw-cuts in the screed to accommodate thermal and moisture movement.

name: Screed Surface Hardener & Dust-Proofer Application
description: The application of liquid or powder surface treatments to densify the screed surface and prevent dusting.

name: Screed Curing
description: The controlled process of retaining moisture in freshly laid screed to ensure proper hydration and strength development.

name: Screed Moisture Testing
description: On-site measurement of residual moisture content in the screed to verify readiness for floor finish installation.

name: Liquid Waterproof Membrane Under Screed
description: A brush- or roller-applied liquid membrane applied over the substrate before screeding, providing waterproofing in wet-room applications.

name: Roof Deck
description: The structural base layer of the roof, typically consisting of steel decking, precast concrete planks, or wood sheathing that supports all overlying roofing materials.

name: Cover Board
description: A protective layer installed over insulation to provide a uniform surface for the membrane and protect insulation from foot traffic and membrane puncture.

name: Air Barrier
description: A continuous membrane or coating installed within the roof assembly to control air leakage into or out of the building envelope.

name: Roof Membrane
description: The primary waterproofing layer of the roof system, which may be built-up asphalt, modified bitumen, PVC, TPO, EPDM, or liquid-applied.

name: Roof Covering / Ballast
description: The exposed surface layer such as gravel ballast, pavers, green roof growing medium, or reflective coating that protects the membrane and provides finished surface properties.

name: Roof Edge Flashing / Trim
description: Metal or preformed flashing installed along roof perimeters, including drip edges, gravel stops, and coping caps that secure and seal membrane edges.

name: Penetration Flashing
description: Curbs, flashing boots, pitch pans, and sealant assemblies around roof penetrations such as vents, pipes, skylights, and HVAC units to maintain watertight integrity.

name: Expansion Joint Assembly
description: Premanufactured or built-in-place joint covers and seals spanning structural roof movement joints to accommodate thermal expansion and contraction while remaining watertight.

name: Roof Curb
description: A raised, framed and flashed support structure on the roof deck used to mount rooftop equipment such as fans, exhausts, skylights, and mechanical units.

name: Roof Walkway Pads
description: Raised, non-penetrating protective walkway pads or runners installed on the membrane surface to allow maintenance access without damaging the roofing system.

name: Green Roof Assembly
description: A vegetated roof system including waterproofing, root barrier, drainage layer, filter fabric, growing medium, and plants for stormwater management and thermal benefits.

name: Skylight / Roof Window
description: A factory-assembled, glazed roof opening unit including frame, glazing, and flashed curb that provides natural daylight and ventilation through the roof plane.

name: Roof Hatch
description: A hinged, insulated, weatherstripped access door assembly with curb flashing providing rooftop access from the interior via a ladder or stairs.

name: Photovoltaic Roof Integration
description: Building-integrated photovoltaic panels or solar shingles mounted on or serving as the roofing surface to generate electrical power on-site.

name: Roof Insulation Fastening
description: The installation of mechanical fasteners, plates, and adhesive used to secure insulation boards and cover boards to the roof deck against wind uplift forces.

name: Membrane Seaming & Welding
description: The on-site heat-welding, solvent-welding, or adhesive seaming of membrane sheets at overlaps to form a continuous watertight roof covering.

name: Membrane Termination & Edge Securing
description: The installation of termination bars, batten strips, sealant beads, and clamping devices at roof edges, curbs, and penetrations to mechanically secure and seal the membrane.

name: Roof Flashing Installation
description: The cutting, bending, soldering, and fastening of sheet metal flashings (lead, copper, aluminum) at valleys, hips, ridges, and wall-to-roof intersections.

name: Roof Drain Installation
description: The installation of drain bodies, strainers, under-deck clamping rings, and connection to storm piping to provide positive roof drainage.

name: Roof Insulation Placement
description: The cutting, fitting, and laying of rigid insulation boards or application of spray foam in multiple layers with staggered joints to minimize thermal bridging.

name: Window Frame Installation
description: On-site installation of window frames including fixing, leveling, and anchoring to the rough opening.

name: Window Sill Installation
description: Installation of interior and exterior window sills, including flashing and sealing.

name: Window Casing/Trim Installation
description: Installation of decorative and protective trim around window frames on interior and exterior.

name: Window Weatherstripping
description: Application of weather seals around window openings to prevent air and water infiltration.

name: Window Hardware Installation
description: Installation of window operating hardware such as hinges, handles, locks, and cranks.

name: Door Frame Installation
description: Installation of door frames including leveling, squaring, and anchoring to the wall opening.

name: Door Leaf Hanging
description: Hanging of door slabs onto frames, including hinge alignment and adjustment for proper operation.

name: Door Casing/Architrave Installation
description: Installation of trim around door openings to conceal gaps and provide finished appearance.

name: Door Weatherstripping & Threshold Installation
description: Installation of weather seals at door perimeter and threshold at bottom to prevent air and water infiltration.

name: Window Frame (Component)
description: The structural perimeter framing of a window that supports the glazing and attaches to the wall.

name: Window Glazing / Glass Panel
description: The glass or transparent panel within a window frame, including single, double, or triple glazing units.

name: Window Casing / Trim
description: Molding or trim pieces that surround the window frame on the interior and exterior for aesthetic finish.

name: Weatherstripping (Window)
description: Flexible sealant strips applied around window openings to prevent air and moisture penetration.

name: Window Sealant / Caulking
description: Applied sealant compound used at window perimeter joints to ensure water and air tightness.

name: Door Leaf / Door Slab
description: The moving panel or slab of a door that swings, slides, or folds to open and close the opening.

name: Door Casing / Architrave
description: Decorative molding trim installed around a door opening to cover the gap between frame and wall.

name: Weatherstripping (Door)
description: Flexible sealing strips applied around door perimeters and threshold to block air and water infiltration.

name: Door Sealant / Caulking
description: Sealant compound applied at door frame to wall joints for weatherproofing and air sealing.

name: Window Assembly
description: The complete pre-assembled or site-assembled window unit including frame, glazing, and integrated components.

name: Door Assembly
description: The complete door unit including frame, leaf, and integrated hardware as a functional system.

name: Glazing Bead / Stop
description: Trim strips that retain the glass panel within the window frame, removable for glazing replacement.

name: Window Screen Installation
description: Installation of insect screens onto window frames, including screen frame and mesh attachment.

name: Window Screen
description: A framed mesh panel installed over an open window to prevent insect entry while allowing airflow.

name: Window Operating Hardware Adjustment & Testing
description: Adjustment and functional testing of all window operating mechanisms to ensure smooth open/close operation.

name: Door Operating Hardware Adjustment & Testing
description: Adjustment and functional testing of door hinges, closers, and latches for proper swing and latching.

name: Safety Glass / Tempered Glass
description: Glass that has been heat-treated or laminated for increased strength and safety where required by code.

name: Window Flashing Installation
description: Installation of waterproof flashing membrane around window openings integrated with the weather barrier.

name: Window Flashing
description: Waterproof membrane or sheet metal installed around window openings to direct water away from the opening.

name: Door Flashing Installation
description: Installation of waterproof flashing at door openings to prevent moisture ingress at the interface.

name: Door Flashing
description: Waterproof membrane or metal flashing installed at door thresholds and heads for moisture protection.

name: Door Kick Plate Installation
description: Installation of protective metal plates on the bottom of door leaves to prevent damage from foot traffic.

name: Kick Plate
description: A protective metal plate mounted on the lower portion of a door leaf to resist scuffs and impacts.

name: Door Viewing Port / Vision Panel Installation
description: Installation of small glazed openings or peephole viewers in doors for visibility through the door.

name: Vision Panel / Door Lite
description: A small glass panel or glazed opening within a door leaf allowing visibility through the door.

name: Automatic Door Operator Installation
description: Installation of motorized door opening mechanisms including sensors, actuators, and control wiring.

name: Sliding Door Track & Hardware Installation
description: Installation of track rails, rollers, and guides for sliding door operation.

name: Sliding Door Track & Hardware
description: The rail system, rollers, and guide components that enable a door to slide open and closed.

name: Folding Door System Installation
description: Installation of multi-panel folding door assemblies including tracks, hinges, and stacking hardware.

name: Folding Door System
description: A door assembly with multiple hinged panels that fold together when opened, often used for wide openings.

name: Bay/Bow Window Assembly Installation
description: On-site assembly and installation of bay or bow window units that project outward from the wall.

name: Bay/Bow Window Assembly
description: A multi-panel window assembly that projects outward from the building facade, creating interior shelf space.

name: Window Opening Control Device Installation
description: Installation of restrictors or limit devices that control how far a window can open for safety.

name: Window Opening Restrictor
description: A safety device that limits the maximum opening distance of a window to prevent falls.

name: Acoustic Seal Installation (Doors/Windows)
description: Installation of specialized acoustic gaskets and seals around door and window perimeters for sound attenuation.

name: Acoustic Seal / Gasket
description: Specialized sealing material around doors and windows that reduces sound transmission through gaps.

name: Fire-Rated Door Installation
description: Installation of fire-rated door assemblies including required fire-rated frames, hardware, and seals.

name: Fire-Rated Door Assembly
description: A door and frame assembly tested and rated to resist fire spread for a specified duration.

name: Fire-Rated Glazing Installation
description: Installation of fire-resistant glass panels in windows or door vision panels where fire rating is required.

name: Intumescent Seal Installation
description: Installation of fire-reactive seals around door perimeters that expand when heated to block smoke and fire.

name: Intumescent Seal
description: A fire-activated seal that expands under heat to close gaps around doors and prevent smoke/fire spread.

name: Door Stop Installation
description: Installation of floor-mounted or wall-mounted stops to prevent doors from swinging too far and damaging walls.

name: Lift Car
description: The enclosed cabin that transports passengers or goods vertically within the building.

name: Lift Shaft
description: The vertical enclosed passageway that houses and guides the lift car as it travels between floors.

name: Lift Machine Room
description: The dedicated room housing the lift hoisting machinery, controller cabinet, and electrical supply equipment.

name: Lift Pit
description: The recessed space at the bottom of the lift shaft containing buffers, compensating chains, and pit access ladder.

name: Lift Guide Rails
description: Vertical steel rails mounted in the shaft that guide and stabilize the lift car and counterweight during travel.

name: Lift Counterweight
description: A weighted assembly that moves opposite the lift car to balance the load and reduce motor power requirements.

name: Lift Hoisting Ropes or Belts
description: Steel cables or flat belts that connect the lift car and counterweight to the drive sheave for vertical movement.

name: Lift Traction Machine
description: The electric motor and gearbox or gearless drive assembly that rotates the sheave to move the hoisting ropes.

name: Lift Controller
description: The electronic control panel that processes landing calls and manages car movement, door operation, and safety circuits.

name: Lift Landing Doors
description: Power-operated sliding doors installed at each floor landing that open and close automatically when the car arrives.

name: Lift Car Doors
description: The sliding door mounted on the lift car itself that opens and closes in sync with the landing doors.

name: Lift Buffers
description: Energy-absorbing devices installed in the lift pit to arrest an over-traveling car or counterweight in an emergency.

name: Lift Safety Gear
description: Mechanical braking devices mounted on the car that engage the guide rails if the lift exceeds its rated speed.

name: Lift Overhead Beam
description: Structural steel beam at the top of the shaft that supports the lift machine and pulley assemblies.

name: Lift Traveling Cable
description: Flexible electrical cable that runs between the lift car and the shaft to supply power and control signals.

name: Lift Call Buttons and Indicators
description: User interface panels at each landing and inside the car for floor selection, door open/close, and floor position indication.

name: Hydraulic Lift Power Unit
description: The pump, motor, valve block, and oil reservoir that pressurize hydraulic fluid for a hydraulic lift system.

name: Hydraulic Lift Ram and Cylinder
description: The piston-and-cylinder assembly that extends to push the car upward in a hydraulic lift configuration.

name: MRL (Machine-Room-Less) Lift System
description: A compact lift configuration where the machine and controller are housed inside the shaft itself, eliminating a separate machine room.

name: Scenic / Panoramic Lift
description: A lift variant with glass walls or a transparent shaft designed to provide views during travel, often with exposed structural framing.

name: Goods / Freight Lift
description: A heavy-duty lift variant with reinforced car, larger doors, and higher load capacity for transporting goods and equipment.

name: Lift Shaft Construction
description: On-site construction of the reinforced concrete or masonry shaft enclosure including formwork, pouring, and blockwork.

name: Lift Guide Rail Installation
description: On-site mounting, aligning, and fixing of vertical guide rails within the shaft to manufacturer tolerances.

name: Lift Machine Installation
description: On-site positioning, bolting, and alignment of the traction machine, motor, and brake assembly on the overhead beam or machine room floor.

name: Lift Car Assembly and Installation
description: On-site assembly and fitting of the car platform, car frame, wall panels, ceiling, and interior finishes inside the shaft.

name: Lift Counterweight Assembly
description: On-site stacking and securing of counterweight blocks and fitting the counterweight frame within its guide rails.

name: Lift Hoisting Rope Rigging
description: On-site threading, tensioning, and terminating of steel cables or belts over the drive sheave and between car and counterweight.

name: Lift Landing Door Installation
