description: On-site lifting, positioning, plumbing, and temporary bracing of a prefabricated box column onto its base plate or foundation.

name: Box Column Concreting
description: Pouring, vibrating, and curing concrete inside the formwork of a cast-in-place box column to achieve the specified strength.

name: Box Column Welding
description: Field welding of box column splices, base plates, diaphragms, or beam-to-column connections on site during steel frame erection.

name: Box Column Survey and Alignment
description: Setting out, checking plumb, and adjusting the position of box columns during installation to ensure vertical alignment within tolerances.

name: Ring Beam
description: A continuous perimeter beam that encircles a building at a roof or floor level to distribute lateral loads and tie structural elements together.

name: Wall Starter Beam
description: A perimeter beam cast at the base of a wall to distribute the wall load onto the foundation and provide a connection interface for vertical reinforcement.

name: Parapet Beam
description: A beam running along the top of a perimeter wall or roof edge that supports the parapet coping and resists wind uplift forces.

name: Perimeter Foundation Beam
description: A reinforced concrete beam at the building perimeter that distributes wall loads to the footings and ties the foundation system together.

name: Bond Beam
description: A horizontal reinforced concrete or masonry beam within a perimeter wall that ties the wall together and distributes lateral loads.

name: Perimeter Beam Installation
description: On-site placement, alignment, and securing of perimeter beams including formwork setup, reinforcement placement, and concrete pouring or steel erection.

name: Perimeter Beam Formwork
description: Construction and fixing of temporary molds at the building perimeter to shape and support concrete perimeter beams during curing.

name: Perimeter Beam Reinforcement
description: Cutting, bending, tying, and placing of steel rebar cages within perimeter beam formwork prior to concrete pour.

name: Perimeter Beam Concrete Pouring
description: On-site pouring, vibrating, and finishing of concrete into perimeter beam formwork to achieve specified strength and surface quality.

name: Perimeter Beam-to-Column Connection
description: The junction detail and connection hardware between a perimeter beam and its supporting column, including shear tabs, bolts, or welded plates.

name: Perimeter Beam Fireproofing
description: Application of spray-applied fire-resistive material or intumescent coating to perimeter beams to achieve required fire resistance rating.

name: Vapor Barrier / Vapor Retarder
description: A sheet or coating material that resists moisture diffusion through the wall assembly, typically installed on the warm side of insulation.

name: Weather-Resistive Barrier (WRB)
description: A water-shedding layer applied behind exterior cladding to protect the sheathing and interior from liquid moisture intrusion.

name: Self-Adhered Membrane (Peel-and-Stick)
description: A rubberized asphalt sheet membrane with adhesive backing used for flashings and below-grade waterproofing.

name: Fluid-Applied Membrane
description: A liquid coating that cures to form a seamless elastomeric waterproof or air barrier layer on wall surfaces.

name: Drainage Membrane / Mat
description: A dimpled plastic sheet or mat that creates an air gap behind cladding to allow drainage and drying of the wall assembly.

name: House Wrap
description: A spun-bond polyolefin or similar synthetic sheet used as a weather-resistive barrier that allows vapor escape while blocking liquid water.

name: Building Paper (Asphalt-Impregnated Felt)
description: A traditional, permeable sheet material made from organic fibers saturated with asphalt, used as a secondary weather barrier.

name: Below-Grade Waterproofing Membrane
description: A heavy-duty membrane (sheet or fluid) applied to foundation walls to resist hydrostatic pressure and groundwater ingress.

name: Spray-Applied Vapor Retarder
description: A vapor-retarding coating sprayed directly onto insulation or substrate to control moisture migration in wall cavities.

name: Polyethylene Sheet Vapor Barrier
description: A simple clear polyethylene film installed on the warm side of wall insulation to block moisture vapor diffusion.

name: Membrane Flashing Components
description: Pre-formed or field-cut strips of membrane material used at wall openings, transitions, and penetrations to direct water outward.

name: Membrane Tape and Seam Sealant
description: Specialized adhesive tapes and sealants used to bond membrane laps and seal penetrations for continuous air and water tightness.

name: Install Weather-Resistive Barrier
description: On-site installation of WRB sheets or fluid-applied coatings over sheathing, lapped and sealed per manufacturer specifications.

name: Install Air and Vapor Barrier
description: On-site application of vapor retarder or air barrier materials with continuity maintained at all penetrations and joints.

name: Install Below-Grade Waterproofing
description: On-site application of sheet or fluid waterproofing membranes to foundation walls, including protection board and drainage board.

name: Apply Fluid-Applied Membrane
description: On-site rolling, spraying, or troweling of liquid membrane material to specified dry film thickness over prepared substrates.

name: Vault Structural Frame
description: The load-bearing ribs, joists, or arching framework that defines the vault's geometry and transfers loads to supporting walls or columns.

name: Vault Soffit / Intrados
description: The finished underside surface of the vault, which may be plastered, tiled, or left exposed as a ceiling finish.

name: Vault Extrados / Backing
description: The upper/outer surface of the vault structure, often leveled with fill or screed to support a floor finish above.

name: Vault Fill / Levelling Layer
description: Lightweight aggregate or concrete fill placed over the vault extrados to create a level base for the floor finish.

name: Vault Reinforcing
description: Steel rebar, mesh, or fiber reinforcement embedded within concrete or masonry vault construction to resist tensile forces.

name: Vault Web / Panel
description: The thin shell or panel spanning between vault ribs, forming the primary curved surface of the vault.

name: Vault Springing Point / Haunch
description: The base or lower curved portion of the vault where it meets its supporting wall, pier, or beam.

name: Vault Keystone / Crown
description: The topmost central wedge or ridge of an arched vault, often accentuated as a structural and visual focal point.

name: Vault Tie Rod / Lateral Restraint
description: Steel rods or cables installed at springing level to resist outward thrust and maintain vault stability.

name: Groin / Intersection Rib
description: The diagonal or transverse edge formed where two vault surfaces intersect in a groin or cross vault configuration.

name: Vault Formwork / Centering
description: Temporary falsework and molds used to support the vault during construction until the structure becomes self-supporting.

name: Vault Skylight / Oculus
description: A glazed opening or dormer integrated into the vault surface to admit natural light.

name: Barrel Vault
description: A continuous semi-cylindrical arched ceiling structure extending in one direction, forming a tunnel-like space.

name: Groin Vault / Cross Vault
description: A vault formed by the perpendicular intersection of two barrel vaults of equal span, transferring loads to corner piers.

name: Rib Vault
description: A vault with a framework of diagonal, transverse, and longitudinal ribs carrying the infill panels or webs.

name: Fan Vault
description: A vault composed of repeated concave half-cone ribs radiating from a single point, typical of late Gothic architecture.

name: Dome / Sail Vault
description: A vault shaped as a hemisphere or spherical cap, often with an oculus, spanning a circular or polygonal space.

name: Segment / Surbased Vault
description: A vault with a shallower curve than a semicircle, having its center below the springing line.

name: Guastavino / Tile Vault
description: A thin-shell vault constructed from layered terra-cotta tiles and fast-setting mortar using traditional Catalan technique.

name: Jack Vault / Flat Vault
description: A nearly flat or very shallow arched vault used for bridging openings with minimal headroom.

name: Vault Waterproofing Membrane
description: A liquid- or sheet-applied waterproof layer installed above the vault extrados to protect the structure from moisture.

name: Vault Acoustic Treatment
description: Sound-absorbing panels, baffles, or spray coatings applied to the vault soffit to control reverberation.

name: Vault Insulation Layer
description: Thermal insulation board or spray foam placed over or under the vault to meet energy performance requirements.

name: Vault Mosaic / Decorative Finish
description: Ornamental tilework, fresco, or decorative plaster applied to the vault intrados as an architectural finish.

name: Vault Construction - Formwork Assembly
description: Erecting temporary centering and forms that define the vault's shape and support it during casting or masonry laying.

name: Vault Construction - Rib Placement
description: Installing the primary load-bearing ribs as the first structural step before filling vault webs or panels.

name: Vault Construction - Concrete Casting
description: Placing, vibrating, and curing reinforced concrete to form a monolithic vault shell.

name: Vault Construction - Masonry Laying
description: Laying brick, stone, or terra-cotta tile units in a curved bed pattern to build up the vault surface.

name: Vault Construction - Tie Rod Installation
description: Fixing steel tie rods or cables across the vault springing points to resist lateral thrust.

name: Vault Construction - Waterproofing Application
description: Applying membrane or liquid waterproofing to the vault extrados after the structure has cured.

name: Vault Construction - Insulation & Finish Layup
description: Installing thermal insulation and floor/roof finishes over the vault backing as the final topping sequence.

name: Vault Construction - Decorative Finishing
description: Applying plaster, paint, mosaic, or other ornamental treatments to the vault intrados.

name: Cloister Vault / Domical Vault
description: A vault formed by the intersection of four or more barrel vaults at equal angles, resembling a dome on a square base.

name: Vault Drainage / Weep System
description: Drainage channels or weep holes embedded in the vault construction to manage trapped moisture within the assembly.

name: Vault Geometry Types
description: Classification of vault forms including barrel vaults, groin vaults, ribbed vaults, fan vaults, and domical vaults that define the roof's structural and spatial geometry.

name: Vault Ribbing
description: Structural ribs (transverse, diagonal, tierceron, lierne) that form the skeletal framework supporting the vault webs.

name: Vault Web Panels
description: The thin infill panels or masonry courses between the structural ribs that form the vault's surface.

name: Vault Springing Points
description: The structural supports or corbels at the base of each vault where the arch curve begins to rise from the wall or column.

name: Vault Haunch
description: The lower, steeper portion of the vault surface between the springing point and the crown.

name: Vault Crown
description: The topmost horizontal ridge or apex line of the vault where opposing curved surfaces meet.

name: Vault Voussoirs
description: The wedge-shaped stone, brick, or precast concrete units arranged in arched courses that form the vault's curved structure.

name: Vault Centering / Formwork
description: Temporary supporting framework or falsework used during construction to shape and support the vault until it becomes self-supporting.

name: Vault Lateral Buttressing
description: Structural elements including flying buttresses, wall buttresses, and transverse arches that resist the outward thrust generated by the vault.

name: Vault Infill / Backing
description: Lightweight fill material (rubble, concrete, or insulating layers) placed over the vault extrados to create a flat roof deck or drainage slope.

name: Vault Soffit Finish
description: The applied plaster, render, paint, or decorative coating on the underside (intrados) of the vault surface.

name: Vault Penetrations & Openings
description: Purpose-built openings through the vault surface for rooflights, skylights, chimneys, ventilation flues, or access hatches.

name: Vault Edge / Wall Connections
description: The junction detailing and flashing at the interface where the vault meets perimeter walls, gable walls, or adjacent roof structures.

name: Vault Drainage Elements
description: Concealed gutters, valley channels, and drainage outlets integrated at vault valleys or intersections to manage rainwater runoff.

name: Vault Thermal Insulation Layer
description: Insulation material placed above or within the vault construction (over extrados or between ribs) to meet thermal performance requirements.

name: Cross Vault Intersection
description: The spatial junction where two vaults intersect at right angles, creating groins or ridges that require special structural and drainage detailing.

name: Vault Erection & Assembly Activity
description: On-site construction process of building the centering/falsework, laying voussoirs or pouring concrete, and curing the vault structure.

name: Vault Waterproofing Installation Activity
description: On-site application of waterproofing membranes, flashings, and drainage components over the completed vault extrados.

name: Vault Insulation & Backfill Activity
description: On-site placement of thermal insulation and lightweight fill materials over the vault extrados to achieve required U-values and drainage slopes.

name: Operable Window
description: A window assembly designed to open and close, typically hinged or sliding, providing ventilation and natural light.

name: Skylight / Rooflight
description: A window installed on the roof slope or roof deck to admit natural light from above.

name: Glass Curtain Wall
description: A non-loadbearing exterior cladding system composed of framed glass panels spanning multiple floors.

name: French Door
description: A pair of hinged glazed doors opening outward or inward from the centre.

name: Pivot Door
description: A door that rotates on a vertical pivot axis rather than on conventional hinges.

name: Folding Door (Bi-fold)
description: A door with hinged panels that fold back against one another when opened.

name: Acoustic Door
description: A door with enhanced sound insulation properties for noise-sensitive spaces.

name: Door Frame & Lining
description: The structural surrounding frame that supports and anchors a door leaf within an opening.

name: Window Frame & Sash
description: The perimeter framing and movable sash that hold the glazing within a window assembly.

name: Glazing / Glass Panel
description: The transparent or translucent glass component used in doors and windows including single, double, or triple glazing.

name: Door Hardware (Hinges, Handles, Locks)
description: The operating and security fittings attached to a door including hinges, handles, locks, and latches.

name: Window Hardware (Catch, Stay, Hinges)
description: The operating fittings attached to a window including friction stays, catches, handles, and hinges.

name: Window Sill & Surround
description: The horizontal ledge and perimeter trim forming the finished edge of a window opening.

name: Lintel over Opening
description: A horizontal structural beam spanning the top of a door or window opening to support the wall above.

name: Window Shading / Sunscreen
description: A fixed external louver or shade device integrated with the window to control solar gain.

name: Window Installation Activity
description: On-site placement, levelling, and securing of window units into prepared rough openings.

name: Door Installation Activity
description: On-site hanging, alignment, and fitting of door leaves into frames including hardware installation.

name: Weather Sealing Activity
description: On-site application of weatherstripping, gaskets, and sealant around installed doors and windows.

name: Low Sill Structure
description: The horizontal load-bearing base element forming the bottom of the low sill assembly, typically concrete, masonry, or steel.

name: Low Sill Framing
description: The timber or metal stud framework built below the window opening to support the sill and transfer loads.

name: Low Sill Insulation
description: Thermal insulation material placed within or beneath the low sill to prevent heat loss and condensation.

name: Low Sill Waterproofing Membrane
description: A flexible sheet or liquid-applied barrier installed on the low sill to prevent moisture ingress.

name: Low Sill Flashing
description: A thin metal or plastic sheet installed at the sill-to-wall junction to shed water away from the assembly.

name: Low Sill Cladding / Finish
description: The exterior facing material (e.g. brick, stone, render, metal panel) applied to the low sill area.

name: Low Sill Backer Rod & Sealant
description: Compressible rod and flexible sealant installed at joints and transitions to maintain airtightness and weather resistance.

name: Low Sill Cill / Sill Board
description: The top horizontal cap or board of the low sill, forming the finished internal window ledge or external cill.

name: Low Sill Drip Edge / Groove
description: A projecting edge or groove on the underside of the external sill that prevents water from running back onto the wall.

name: Low Sill Weep Holes
description: Small openings through the low sill or surrounding masonry that allow trapped moisture to drain out.

name: Low Sill Installation
description: On-site assembly, setting, and fixing of the low sill components into the building opening.

name: Low Sill Waterproofing Application
description: On-site installation of waterproofing membranes, flashings, and sealants to the low sill area.

name: Low Sill Insulation Placement
description: On-site fitting of thermal insulation within the low sill cavity to meet thermal performance requirements.

name: Low Sill – Window Interface
description: The junction detail between the low sill assembly and the window frame above, including sub-sills and adapters.

name: Low Sill – Wall Interface
description: The connection detail where the low sill meets the adjacent wall construction, including cavity trays and closers.

name: Window Reveal Lining
description: The internal vertical side surface or board that lines the depth of a window opening between the glazing and the inner wall face.

name: Door Reveal Lining
description: The internal vertical side surface or board that lines the depth of a door opening between the door frame and the inner wall face.

name: Deep Reveal Sill
description: The horizontal bottom surface of a deep reveal, typically finished with a sill board or stone to shed moisture and support the window unit.

name: Reveal Soffit/Lintel Finish
description: The horizontal top surface of a reveal below the lintel or above the opening, finished to match the surrounding interior.

name: Reveal Insulation
description: Thermal insulation installed within the depth of a deep reveal to reduce thermal bridging at window and door openings.

name: Reveal Thermal Break
description: A low-conductivity material strip integrated into the reveal construction to interrupt heat flow through the building envelope at the opening perimeter.

name: Reveal Backing Rod & Sealant
description: Compressible backing rod and elastomeric sealant applied at the gap between the window/door frame and the reveal to provide airtightness and weather sealing.

name: Reveal Plaster/Plasterboard Finish
description: Gypsum plaster or plasterboard applied over the reveal substrate to create a smooth interior surface ready for painting or decoration.

name: Reveal Angle Bead
description: A perforated metal or plastic corner bead fixed at the internal and external corners of a reveal to reinforce plaster edges and maintain straight arrises.

name: Deep Reveal Installation
description: On-site construction activity comprising the framing, insulating, lining, and finishing of deep reveals around window and door openings.

name: Reveal Sealant Application
description: On-site installation of backing rod and sealant at the perimeter gap between the opening frame and the reveal lining to achieve airtightness.

name: Low Doorway Frame
description: The structural frame surrounding a low doorway opening, including head, jambs, and sill.

name: Low Door Leaf
description: The door panel that is shorter than standard height to fit within a low doorway opening.

name: Low Doorway Header/Lintel
description: The horizontal structural element above a low doorway that supports the wall above the reduced-height opening.

name: Clearance Height Marker
description: Visual indicator or signage affixed near a low doorway to denote the reduced headroom clearance.

name: Low Doorway Threshold
description: The bottom strip or transition piece at the base of a low doorway opening.

name: Low Doorway Arch
description: An arched top configuration for a low doorway, reducing effective height while maintaining a curved opening.

name: Low Doorway Weatherstripping
description: Sealing material installed around the perimeter of a low doorway to prevent air and moisture infiltration.

name: Low Doorway Frame Anchors
description: Metal brackets or fasteners that secure the low doorway frame to the surrounding wall construction.

name: Low Doorway Installation
description: On-site installation process of setting, leveling, and securing a low doorway frame and door leaf into a prepared rough opening.

name: Low Doorway Head Protection Pad
description: A cushioned or padded surface applied to the header area of a low doorway to mitigate head impact injuries.

name: Low Doorway in Partition Wall
description: A low-height passage opening through an interior non-load-bearing partition wall.

name: Low Doorway in Loadbearing Wall
description: A reduced-height opening formed through a structural loadbearing wall, requiring a reinforced lintel.

name: Low Doorway in Historic Building
description: A low doorway retained or reinstated in an older building due to original construction constraints or preservation requirements.

name: Low Access Hatch Doorway
description: A very low doorway providing access to confined spaces such as attics, crawlspaces, or mechanical chases.

name: Concrete Edge Formwork
description: Temporary or permanent formwork shaped to produce a thickened, finished edge on a concrete slab.

name: Edge Tapering Detail
description: A gradual reduction in slab thickness toward the free edge, often used in parking structures to shed water.

name: Thickened Slab Edge Insulation
description: Rigid insulation applied to the exterior face of a thickened slab edge to reduce thermal bridging.

name: Load-Bearing Edge Profile
description: A shaped metal or precast concrete profile attached to the slab edge to distribute concentrated loads from cladding or curtain walls.

name: Drip Edge / Drip Channel
description: A groove or projection formed in the thickened edge to direct water runoff away from the slab underside.

name: Edge Reinforcement Cage
description: A cluster of longitudinal and transverse rebar placed within the thickened edge zone to resist tensile and shear forces.

name: Post-Tensioning Edge Anchor
description: A stressing anchor pocket and hardware embedded in the thickened edge for post-tensioned slab tendons.

name: Slab Edge Formwork Installation
description: On-site assembly and bracing of edge formwork to create the thickened slab perimeter profile before concrete placement.

name: Edge Reinforcement Placement
description: Installation of rebar cages and shear stirrups within the thickened edge zone prior to concreting.

name: Thickened Edge Concrete Pour
description: Placing and vibrating concrete in the edge formwork to achieve the designed thickened section monolithically with the slab.

name: Edge Insulation Installation
description: Application of rigid insulation boards and waterproofing membrane to the exposed thickened edge after pour and curing.

name: Slab Edge Waterproofing Application
description: Sealing the top and face of the thickened edge with liquid-applied or sheet waterproofing to prevent moisture ingress.

name: Thermal Break Assembly
description: A proprietary load-bearing insulation block placed within the thickened edge to structurally separate interior and exterior slab portions.

name: Precast Concrete Edge Beam
description: A factory-cast beam that is lifted and installed at the slab perimeter, acting as the thickened edge.

name: Steel Edge Angle
description: An L-shaped steel section anchored to the slab edge to serve as a continuous support for brick veneer or stone cladding.

name: Composite Deck Edge Closure
description: A metal closure angle or plate that seals the edge of a composite steel deck slab where the concrete fill is thickened.

name: Column Enclosure/Cladding
description: The fire-rated or finish layer applied around a structural column for protection or appearance.

name: Column Base
description: The bottom resting element of a column that transfers load to the floor or foundation.

name: Column-to-Beam Connection
description: The joint assembly that transfers shear and moment forces between a column and an intersecting beam.

name: Column-to-Slab Connection
description: The interface detail where a column meets a floor slab, including any drop panels or shear reinforcement.

name: Column Reinforcement Installation
description: On-site placement and tying of steel rebar cages within column formwork prior to concreting.

name: Column Cladding Installation
description: On-site attachment of architectural finishes or fire-rated encasement around a column.

name: Column Plumbness Surveying
description: On-site measurement and verification that columns are installed vertically within tolerance.

name: Embedded Column Base Plate
description: A steel plate anchored into the foundation that provides a bolted connection for the column above.

name: Column Void/Shaft
description: The enclosed vertical space or chase within or beside a column that may house building services or ducts.

name: Column Grid Line
description: The two-dimensional layout reference system defining column positions across a floor plate.

name: Pedestal Column
description: A short, stout column used to elevate an element above a roof or floor level, often for equipment supports.

name: Bolted Column Connection
description: A column connection that uses bolts and nuts to join steel column sections to each other or to base plates and beams for structural continuity.

name: Welded Column Connection
description: A column connection where steel column elements are joined by fusion welding at the splice or at the beam-to-column interface.

name: Column Base Plate Connection
description: A steel plate welded to the bottom of a column and anchored to the foundation with holding-down bolts to transfer loads.

name: Beam-to-Column Moment Connection
description: A rigid connection between a beam and a column designed to transfer bending moments in addition to shear forces.

name: Beam-to-Column Shear Connection
description: A simple connection that transfers vertical shear forces from a beam to a column with minimal rotational restraint.

name: Column Cap/Head Connection
description: The top termination connection of a column, typically receiving a beam or beam assembly at the uppermost level.

name: Column Anchor Bolt Assembly
description: The set of threaded rods, nuts, and washers embedded in the foundation to fix the column base plate in position.

name: Column Connection Stiffener Plate
description: A steel plate welded at the column connection region to reinforce the web or flange against localized buckling or high stresses.

name: Column Connection Gusset Plate
description: A triangular or shaped steel plate used at a column connection to transfer forces between bracing members and the column.

name: Grouting of Column Base
description: The on-site placement of non-shrink grout between the column base plate and the foundation to ensure full bearing and load transfer.

name: Bolting-Up of Column Connection
description: The on-site tightening of high-strength bolts at a column connection to achieve the required pre-tension and clamp force.

name: Welding of Column Connection
description: The on-site fusion welding of column splice or beam-to-column joints in accordance with approved welding procedure specifications.

name: Column Connection Installation and Alignment
description: The on-site positioning, plumbing, and temporary bracing of a column at the connection point before permanent fastening.

name: Column Connection Non-Destructive Testing
description: The on-site inspection of completed column connections using ultrasonic, magnetic particle, or radiographic methods to verify weld or bolt integrity.

name: Column Haunch Connection
description: A reinforced connection region where a tapered or haunched beam end joins a column to increase moment capacity at the joint.

name: Column Connection Shear Tab
description: A steel plate welded to the column web to provide a bolted shear-only connection for the beam web.

name: Column Connection End Plate
description: A steel plate welded to the end of a beam or column that is then bolted to the adjacent column flange or web at the joint.

name: Concrete Column Dowel Connection
description: Vertical reinforcing bars projecting from a concrete foundation or lower column to lap with the reinforcement of the column above.

name: Precast Concrete Column Socket Connection
description: A connection where a precast column is inserted into a pre-formed socket in a foundation or beam and grouted in place.

name: Column Connection Fire Protection Wrap
description: A fire-resistive coating, board, or spray-applied material applied specifically at the column connection region to maintain structural fire rating.

name: Column Connection Inspection and Testing
description: The on-site verification of column connection tightness, weld quality, and alignment against specification tolerances.

name: Retrofitting/Strengthening of Column Connection
description: The on-site addition of steel plates, stiffeners, or FRP wraps to an existing column connection to increase its load capacity.

name: Stair Vault Enclosing Walls
description: Structural or non-structural walls that enclose and define the stair vault space, separating it from adjacent spaces.

name: Stair Vault Floor Slab
description: The structural floor slab at the base of the stair vault that supports the stair flight and landing.

name: Stair Vault Ceiling/Soffit
description: The underside of the floor or roof above forming the top boundary of the stair vault space.

name: Guardrail/Balustrade
description: A protective barrier system installed along the open side(s) of the stair vault to prevent falls.

name: Stair Vault Lighting
description: Fixed luminaires and emergency lighting installed within the stair vault for safe illumination.

name: Stair Vault Fire Protection System
description: Fire-rated construction elements such as fire doors, smoke vents, and sprinkler heads serving the enclosed stair vault.

name: Stair Vault Ventilation
description: Natural or mechanical ventilation openings, smoke extraction shafts, or pressurization ducts serving the stair vault.

name: Stair Vault Door
description: Fire-rated access doors providing entry to and egress from the stair vault at each floor level.

name: Stair Vault Floor Finish
description: The wear-resistant surface material applied to stair treads, risers, and landings such as terrazzo, rubber, or tile.

name: Stair Vault Wall Finish
description: The interior wall surface treatment within the stair vault, typically paint, tile, or impact-resistant paneling.

name: Stair Vault Signage
description: Fixed floor-level identification, directional, and emergency egress signs mounted within the stair vault.

name: Stair Vault Construction
description: On-site assembly and installation of stair flights, landings, handrails, and enclosing walls within the stair vault space.

name: Stair Vault Fireproofing Installation
description: Application of fire-resistive coatings or encasement to structural elements within the stair vault.

name: Stair Vault Finishing
description: Installation of floor, wall, and ceiling finishes, lighting, signage, and hardware within the completed stair vault.

name: Duct
description: The primary hollow conduit used within duct space for conveying air in HVAC systems.

name: Duct Hanger/Support
description: Structural brackets, rods, or trapeze assemblies that suspend and secure ducts from the building structure.

name: Duct Sealant
description: Mastic, tape, or gasket material used to seal joints and seams in ductwork to prevent air leakage.

name: Duct Damper
description: A manually or motorized blade within the duct used to regulate or block airflow.

name: Duct Access Door
description: A hinged or removable panel providing entry into the ductwork for inspection and cleaning.

name: Flexible Duct Connector
description: A short flexible section joining rigid duct to diffusers or terminal units to isolate vibration.

name: Duct Turning Vane
description: A set of curved guide vanes installed inside duct elbows to reduce turbulence and pressure loss.

name: Duct Space Installation
description: On-site assembly, hanging, and joining of duct sections within the building's reserved duct zone.

name: Duct Insulation Installation
description: On-site wrapping, adhering, or cladding of insulation material around installed ductwork.

name: Duct Leakage Testing
description: On-site pressurization testing of the assembled duct system to verify airtightness within allowable limits.

name: Radiant Floor Heating
description: A heating system embedded in the floor slab or screed that circulates warm fluid or uses electric cables to radiate heat upward into the occupied space.

name: Radiant Ceiling Panels
description: Metal or gypsum panels suspended from or embedded in the ceiling that carry hot water pipes or electric elements to radiate heat downward.

name: Radiant Wall Panels
description: Wall-mounted panels containing hot water tubing or electric heating elements that radiate heat into the room from vertical surfaces.

name: Hydronic Tubing (PEX/Copper)
description: Flexible cross-linked polyethylene or rigid copper pipes that circulate heated water through radiant heating loops embedded in floors, walls, or ceilings.

name: Electric Radiant Cables
description: Resistance heating cables installed beneath finished flooring or within ceiling/ wall assemblies to produce radiant heat when energized.

name: Radiant Manifold
description: A distribution hub with valves and flow meters that splits a main supply line into multiple individual radiant heating loops.

name: Heat Source (Boiler/Heat Pump)
description: The central heating plant — a boiler, heat pump, or district heating connection — that supplies hot water to the radiant distribution system.

name: Embedded Insulation (Under-Slab/Perimeter)
description: Rigid foam or other insulation placed beneath or around radiant slabs and piping to reduce downward and edge heat loss.

name: Radiant Ceiling Hydronic Module
description: A factory-assembled panel containing serpentine tubing, insulation, and a metal face that is installed as a ceiling-mounted radiant emitter.

name: Floor Coverings for Radiant Systems
description: Tile, stone, engineered wood, or thin carpet specifically selected and installed with appropriate thermal conductance to allow effective radiant heat transfer.

name: Installation of Underfloor Radiant Tubing
description: On-site laying and fastening of hydronic tubing to insulation boards or reinforcement mesh before the concrete slab or screed is poured.

name: Commissioning of Radiant Heating Loops
description: Pressure testing, flow balancing, and temperature calibration of each radiant loop to ensure even heat distribution across all zones.

name: Embedding Radiant Cables in Screed
description: Placing and securing electric radiant cables on a subfloor substrate and covering them with a sand-cement screed to the finished floor level.

name: Installation of Ceiling Radiant Panels
description: Suspending or flush-mounting pre-assembled radiant panels to the ceiling structure and connecting them to the hydronic or electrical supply.

name: Radiant Zone Thermostat
description: A room or zone temperature controller that modulates flow valves or electrical relays to maintain the setpoint for a radiant heating zone.

name: Radiant Heating Control Valve
description: An actuated valve on the manifold or branch line that regulates hot water flow to individual loops or zones based on thermostat demand.

name: Dormer Frame
description: The structural framework (rafters, studs, joists) forming the walls and roof of the dormer projection from the main roof slope.

name: Dormer Siding
description: The exterior cladding material (e.g., shingles, siding panels, stucco) applied to the vertical walls of the dormer.

name: Dormer Roof Deck
description: The sheathing or decking material covering the dormer's roof framing to support the roofing membrane.

name: Dormer Roof Covering
description: The waterproof roofing material (shingles, slate, metal, etc.) installed on the dormer's roof surface.

name: Dormer Flashing
description: Metal or membrane flashings installed at the dormer-to-main-roof junction and along dormer edges to prevent water intrusion.

name: Dormer Window Unit
description: The pre-assembled or site-built window installed within the dormer's front wall opening to provide light and ventilation.

name: Dormer Window Trim
description: Architectural trim, casings, and sill details surrounding the dormer window on the interior and exterior.

name: Dormer Soffit & Fascia
description: The underside and edge trim components of the dormer's roof overhang, including ventilation if present.

name: Dormer Interior Wall Finish
description: The gypsum board, paneling, or plaster applied to the interior surfaces of the dormer walls and ceiling.

name: Dormer Insulation
description: Thermal insulation installed within the dormer's wall and roof cavities to meet energy code requirements.

name: Dormer Gutter & Downspout
description: Rainwater collection components specifically serving the dormer roof, diverting water to the main roof drainage system.

name: Dormer Ice & Water Shield
description: A self-adhering waterproof underlayment applied at the dormer's eaves and valleys for ice dam protection.

name: Dormer Exterior Trim
description: Decorative corner boards, friezes, and other architectural trim elements applied to the exterior of the dormer.

name: Dormer Construction Activity
description: On-site assembly, framing, sheathing, and finishing of the dormer structure integrated into the main roof system.

name: Dormer Window Installation Activity
description: On-site setting, leveling, fastening, and sealing of the window unit into the dormer's prepared rough opening.

name: Gable-Front Dormer
description: A dormer with a gabled roof, creating a triangular roof profile above a vertical window wall.

name: Shed Dormer
description: A dormer with a single-slope (shed) roof pitched in the same direction as the main roof but at a shallower angle.

name: Hip Dormer
description: A dormer with a hipped roof where three sloping roof planes meet, eliminating the vertical gable end.

name: Flat-Roof Dormer
description: A dormer with a nearly flat or low-slope roof, often used in modern or contemporary designs.

name: Dormer Valley
description: The internal angle or depressed channel formed at the intersection of the dormer roof and the main roof slope.

name: Roof Cap Membrane
description: The waterproof membrane layer specifically installed as the topmost covering of a roof cap assembly to prevent moisture intrusion.

name: Roof Cap Flashing
description: Sheet metal or preformed flashing pieces that seal the edges and transitions of the roof cap against water penetration.

name: Roof Cap Insulation
description: Thermal insulation layer integrated within the roof cap assembly to reduce heat transfer through the roof termination.

name: Roof Cap Substrate/Deck
description: The structural base or sheathing panel onto which the roof cap membrane and finishes are applied.

name: Roof Cap Coping
description: A preformed metal or stone cover piece that caps the top of a parapet wall, serving as the uppermost weather barrier.

name: Roof Cap Gravel Stop
description: A metal edge detail installed at the perimeter of a roof cap to retain ballast or gravel and provide a clean termination.

name: Precast Concrete Roof Cap
description: A prefabricated concrete unit used as a durable, fire-resistant roof cap atop parapet or masonry walls.

name: Metal Roof Cap
description: A formed sheet metal (copper, aluminum, or steel) roof cap installed as a lightweight, corrosion-resistant capping detail.

name: Stone Roof Cap
description: A natural or cast stone slab used as a decorative and durable roof cap element on masonry parapets.

name: Roof Cap Sealant Joints
description: Elastomeric sealant beads and backer rods installed at joints between roof cap segments to maintain weathertightness.

name: Roof Cap Fasteners & Clips
description: Concealed clips, screws, or anchors that secure the roof cap components to the supporting wall or deck.

name: Install Roof Cap Flashing
description: On-site installation of metal flashing around roof cap edges, transitions, and penetrations to ensure watertight sealing.

name: Install Roof Cap Coping
description: On-site placement and fastening of coping units onto the parapet or roof cap assembly.

name: Apply Roof Cap Membrane
description: On-site laying or adhering of the waterproof membrane over the prepared roof cap substrate.

name: Install Roof Cap Insulation
description: On-site placement and securing of rigid insulation boards within the roof cap build-up.

name: Seal Roof Cap Joints
description: On-site application of sealant and backer rod at joints between roof cap segments to achieve weathertight continuity.

name: Floor Base Layer / Screed
description: A cementitious or bonded layer applied over the structural slab to achieve required falls, levelness, and substrate for finishes.

name: Vapor Barrier / Damp-proof Membrane
description: A polyethylene or bituminous sheet installed beneath or within the floor assembly to prevent moisture migration from the ground or slab.

name: Floor Drain / Trench Drain
description: Plumbing fixture set flush into the floor surface to collect and convey water to waste piping in wet areas.

name: Expansion / Control Joint
description: Pre-formed gap or filler installed in the floor slab to accommodate thermal or structural movement and prevent cracking.

name: Access Floor Panel
description: Removable raised floor panel supported on pedestals, creating a plenum space for cabling and air distribution in data centers or offices.

name: Raised Access Floor System
description: Complete raised floor assembly of pedestals, stringers, and panels providing a structural elevated walking surface with an interstitial plenum.

name: Radiant Floor Heating / Cooling System
description: Embedded tubing or electric mats within the floor assembly that circulate fluid or current to condition the space thermally.

name: Structural Floor Slab
description: The primary horizontal structural member (reinforced concrete, composite steel-deck, or timber) that supports floor loads and spans between beams or walls.

name: Stair Tread / Landing Surface
description: The horizontal walking surface of a stair step or intermediate landing, finished with anti-slip material or nosing.

name: Floor Socket / Floor Box
description: Electrical or data outlet receptacle mounted flush in the floor surface to provide power and connectivity at occupied points.

name: Floor Grating / Grate
description: Metal or FRP open-grid panel set into the floor for drainage, ventilation, or industrial slip-resistant walkways.

name: Floor Mat / Entrance Mat
description: Recessed or surface-mounted scraper/wiper mat installed at building entrances to remove dirt and moisture from footwear.

name: Slip-resistant Floor Coating
description: A textured aggregate or epoxy coating applied to the floor finish to increase friction and reduce slip hazards in wet areas.

name: Floor Tiling Installation
description: The on-site process of laying, cutting, grouting, and curing ceramic, stone, or vinyl tiles onto the prepared substrate.

name: Screed Pouring & Leveling
description: The wet-trade operation of mixing, pouring, spreading, and floating cementitious screed to achieve specified floor flatness and falls.

name: Floor Polishing / Grinding
description: On-site mechanical grinding and polishing of concrete or stone floor surfaces to achieve a specified gloss and smoothness.

name: Self-leveling Compound Application
description: Pumping and spreading of a free-flowing polymer-modified cementitious compound to create a perfectly flat substrate for flooring.

name: Underfloor Heating Loop Installation
description: The fixing, routing, and pressure-testing of hydronic tubing or electric mats within the floor build-up prior to screeding.

name: Floor Grating Installation
description: Cutting, framing, and securing metal or FRP grating panels into the supporting structure with appropriate bearing bars and fasteners.

name: Resilient Flooring Welding (Vinyl/Linoleum)
description: Heat-welding or cold-welding of seams between sheet vinyl or linoleum to create a monolithic, hygiene-compliant floor surface.

name: Lapped Wall Cladding
description: The overlapping weather-resistant boards or planks (e.g., timber shiplap, fiber-cement planks) fixed to the external face of the wall.

name: Lapped Wall Underlay/Substrate
description: The breather membrane, sheathing board, or building paper installed behind the lapped cladding to provide drainage and air-tightness.

name: Lapped Wall Battens/Counter-Battens
description: The vertical or horizontal timber or metal strips that create a ventilated cavity and provide a fixing surface for the lapped cladding boards.

name: Lapped Wall Flashing
description: The sheet-metal or flexible flashings installed at openings, corners, and penetrations to shed water and seal the lapped cladding system.

name: Lapped Wall Trim & Corner Boards
description: The external corner profiles, starter strips, and trim pieces used to finish the edges and transitions of the lapped wall assembly.

name: Lapped Wall Ventilation Cavity
description: The drained and ventilated air gap between the lapped cladding and the substrate, allowing moisture to escape and preventing trapped condensation.

name: Lapped Wall Fasteners & Fixings
description: The corrosion-resistant nails, screws, or clips that secure each lapped board to the battens or substrate.

name: Lapped Wall Insulation Layer
description: The continuous thermal insulation installed within or behind the cavity to improve the thermal performance of the lapped wall assembly.

name: Lapped Wall Installation
description: The on-site process of installing battens, laying boards with the correct lap overlap, and fitting flashings to create a weathertight lapped wall.

name: Lapped Wall Air Seal
description: The gaskets, tapes, or sealants applied at board joints and penetrations to prevent uncontrolled air leakage through the lapped assembly.

name: Interior Partition Wall
description: A non-load-bearing wall assembly that divides interior space, typically comprising framing, insulation, and finishes.

name: Interior Wall Framing
description: The structural skeleton of an interior wall, usually metal or wood studs, tracks, and blocking.

name: Wall Insulation Layer
description: Thermal or acoustic insulation material placed within the wall cavity to improve energy and sound performance.

name: Vapor Barrier / Air Barrier
description: A continuous membrane or coating applied to the wall assembly to control moisture and air infiltration.

name: Gypsum Board / Drywall
description: Factory-made panels of gypsum plaster sandwiched between paper facers, used as the primary interior wall surface.

name: Interior Wall Sheathing
description: Panel material (plywood, OSB, or cement board) applied to wall framing as a substrate for finishes or bracing.

name: Wall Finish / Plaster
description: A wet-applied or troweled surface coating (gypsum plaster, veneer plaster, or stucco) that provides the final decorative and protective layer.

name: Interior Wall Cladding
description: Decorative paneling or boarding (wood, MDF, PVC, metal, or glass) applied over the wall base for aesthetic finish.

name: Wall Tile / Ceramic Wall Finish
description: Ceramic, porcelain, or stone tiles adhered to wall surfaces in wet areas for water resistance and cleanability.

name: Interior Wall Paint / Coating
description: Liquid-applied pigmented coating that provides color, durability, and washability to interior wall surfaces.

name: Wall Corner Bead / Trim
description: Perforated metal or plastic profiles installed at drywall corners and edges to reinforce and create clean transitions.

name: Interior Wall Expansion Joint
description: A pre-formed gap and cover assembly that accommodates building movement while maintaining fire and acoustic ratings.

name: Hidden Services Chase Wall
description: A shallow void or bulkhead within or against the wall assembly that conceals mechanical, electrical, or plumbing services.

name: Interior Wall Construction
description: On-site assembly and erection of interior wall framing, sheathing, insulation, and lining boards.

name: Wall Finish Application
description: On-site installation of wall finishes including drywall finishing, plastering, tiling, painting, or cladding application.

name: Hopper Window
description: A window with a bottom-hinged sash that tilts inward, often used in basements for controlled ventilation.

name: Sliding Window (Horizontal)
description: A window with one or more sashes that slide horizontally along tracks to create an opening.

name: Projection Window
description: A window that projects outward from the building facade, such as a bay or bow window with operable casement sections.

name: Pivot Window
description: A window with a central hinge axis allowing the sash to rotate horizontally or vertically for a wide opening.

name: Jalousie / Louvre Window
description: A window composed of multiple parallel glass slats that crank open simultaneously like a venetian blind.

name: Folding / Bi-Fold Window
description: A window with multiple panels that fold back onto themselves, creating a large uninterrupted opening to the outdoors.

name: Tilt-and-Turn Window
description: A window with dual-action hardware that can either tilt inward from the top or swing fully inward from the side.

name: Window Frame Assembly
description: The structural perimeter framing (head, jamb, sill) that supports the operable sash and glazing units.

name: Operable Glazing Panel (Sash)
description: The movable framed panel containing glass that opens and closes within the window frame.

name: Window Hinge and Hardware Set
description: The collection of hinges, friction stays, handles, and locking mechanisms required for the window's opening action.

name: Window Operator / Crank Mechanism
description: A geared mechanical device, typically with a crank handle, used to push casement or awning windows open.

name: Window Balance System
description: A spring-loaded or weight-based mechanism that counterbalances sliding sashes in hung or sliding windows.

name: Wide-Open Window Limit Stop
description: A safety or control device that restricts how far the window can open, or locks it in a fully open position.

name: Window Opening Area
description: The architectural aperture or rough opening in the wall assembly into which the operable window unit is installed.

name: Window Installation / Set-in-Place
description: The on-site activity of placing, leveling, shimming, and anchoring the window unit into the structural opening.

name: Window Flashing and Sealing
description: The installation of waterproof membrane flashings and sealants around the window perimeter to ensure weathertightness.

name: Operable Window Commissioning and Adjustment
description: The final on-site adjustment of hinges, friction stays, and locking hardware to ensure smooth operation and proper closure.

name: Door Leaf (Solid Core with Glass Panel)
description: The main operable panel of the door combining a solid core (hollow or solid timber/metal) with one or more glazed apertures.

name: Glass Panel/Glazing Insert
description: The transparent or translucent glass pane fitted into the door leaf, which may be single, double, laminated, tempered, or wired glass.

name: Door Frame (with Glazing Rebates)
description: The fixed surround that supports the door leaf and contains rebates or stops to accommodate both the door and any sidelight glazing.

name: Sidelight Glazing Panel
description: A fixed vertical glazed panel mounted beside the door frame to allow additional light transmission alongside the solid door.

name: Glazing Bead/Stop
description: The trim or molding that secures the glass panel within the door leaf or frame, removable for glass replacement.

name: Transom Panel with Glass
description: A horizontal glazed panel positioned above the door opening to provide borrowed light while maintaining a solid door below.

name: Door Closer (Concealed or Surface-Mounted)
description: A mechanical device installed on the door leaf or frame that automatically closes the door after opening.

name: Hinges (Butt or Continuous/Piano)
description: The pivoting hardware connecting the solid door leaf to the frame, sized to support the combined weight of the solid core and glass.

name: Lock/Latch Set with Key Cylinder
description: The latching and locking mechanism installed in the solid portion of the door leaf to secure the door.

name: Door Handle/Pull (Back-to-Back)
description: The operating hardware mounted on both faces of the solid door leaf, typically in the solid lower or mid-rail area.

name: Kick Plate (Metal or Plastic)
description: A protective plate applied to the lower portion of the door leaf's solid area to resist scuffing and impact.

name: Glazing Gasket/Seal
description: A compressible rubber or silicone strip that weather-seals the perimeter of the glass panel within the door leaf or frame.

name: Intumescent Glazing Channel
description: A fire-rated frame channel containing intumescent material that expands under heat to contain the glass during a fire.

name: Install Solid Door with Glass Assembly
description: On-site positioning and fixing of the pre-assembled door leaf, frame, and glazing into the prepared opening.

name: Install Glazing Panel into Door Leaf
description: Setting the glass panel into the door leaf's glazing pocket and securing it with beads, gaskets, or structural silicone.

name: Install Door Hardware (Hinges/Locks/Closers)
description: Fitting and adjusting hinges, locks, latches, door closers, and pulls onto the solid door leaf and frame.

name: Light Shelf
description: A horizontal or angled reflective surface mounted above eye level on a window or façade that redirects daylight deeper into a space.

name: Light Tube / Solar Tube
description: A tubular skylight system that channels sunlight from a roof dome through a reflective tube into interior spaces.

name: Diffusing Glazing
description: Glass or polycarbonate panel with a fritted, etched, or frosted surface that scatters incoming light to reduce glare and shadows.

name: Light-Directing Louvers
description: Adjustable or fixed horizontal blades integrated into a window assembly that reflect or refract sunlight onto the ceiling plane.

name: Prismatic Skylight
description: A skylight fitted with prismatic lenses that break and redirect direct sunlight into diffuse ambient light across a room.

name: Reflective Ceiling Panel
description: A ceiling tile or panel with a high-reflectance finish designed to distribute incoming daylight evenly throughout the space.

name: Light Well / Atrium
description: A vertical shaft or open courtyard within a building that channels daylight downward to lower floors through interior windows.

name: Lightshelf Bracket & Support Assembly
description: Structural brackets and mounting hardware that secure a light shelf to the building façade or window mullion.

name: Install Light Shelf
description: On-site mounting, leveling, and fastening of light shelves to the building structure or curtain wall system.

name: Install Light Tube System
description: On-site assembly and installation of tubular daylighting devices including roof flashing, reflective tube sections, and ceiling diffuser.

name: Install Diffusing Glazing
description: On-site fitting and sealing of diffusing glass panels into window frames or curtain wall systems.

name: Install Prismatic Skylight
description: On-site mounting, flashing, and sealing of prismatic skylight units onto roof curbs.

name: Light-Redirecting Film
description: A micro-structured adhesive film applied to existing glazing that refracts incoming sunlight toward the ceiling while maintaining view.

name: Window pane with small-divided lights
description: A single glass pane within a window that is subdivided into smaller lites or panes by muntins or grilles, characteristic of traditional small-pane windows.

name: Muntin/grille bar
description: The vertical or horizontal bar that subdivides a window into smaller individual panes, whether structural or decorative.

name: True divided light (TDL) sash
description: A window sash assembly where individual panes of glass are separated by integral muntins, typical of historic small-pane windows.

name: Simulated divided light (SDL) sash
description: A window sash assembly with a single large pane of glass and applied or adhered muntins that mimic the appearance of small panes.

name: Small-pane interior transom window
description: A small-pane window unit located above a door or another window, typically subdivided into multiple lites.

name: Small-pane casement window assembly
description: A hinged window assembly subdivided into multiple small panes, common in historic and cottage-style architecture.

name: Small-pane double-hung window assembly
description: A vertically sliding window assembly with both sashes subdivided into multiple small panes.

name: Small-pane fixed window assembly
description: A non-operable window unit subdivided into multiple small panes, often used as a decorative or transom element.

name: Small-pane window sash
description: The movable or fixed frame that holds the multiple small panes of glass within a small-pane window assembly.

name: Cam lock/keeper for small-pane sash
description: A hardware component used to secure the small-pane window sash in a closed position.

name: Small-pane window frame
description: The outer structural frame that surrounds and supports the small-pane window sash assembly.

name: Small-pane window glazing putty/bead
description: The sealant or trim bead that holds each individual small pane of glass in place within the sash.

name: Lead came strip
description: H-shaped lead strips used to join individual small panes of glass in leaded-glass or stained-glass small-pane windows.

name: Small-pane storm window
description: An exterior secondary window applied over a small-pane primary window to improve thermal performance while preserving the subdivided appearance.

name: Small-pane window installation
description: The on-site installation of a small-pane window assembly into the rough opening of a building's wall.

name: Small-pane glazing installation
description: The on-site process of setting individual small panes of glass into the sash and securing them with putty or glazing beads.

name: Small-pane window weatherstripping application
description: The on-site application of weatherstripping around small-pane window sashes to reduce air infiltration.

name: Small-pane window hardware installation
description: The on-site installation of locks, hinges, lifts, and other hardware on small-pane window assemblies.

name: Small-pane window restoration/reglazing
description: The on-site repair or replacement of individual small panes and glazing compounds in an existing small-pane window.

name: Mullion for small-pane window grouping
description: A vertical or horizontal structural member that separates adjacent small-pane window units within a window assembly.

name: Trim Board
description: The dimensional lumber or engineered wood strip that forms the actual physical trim piece, typically 1/2-inch thick by various widths.

name: Trim Fasteners
description: Nails, screws, or adhesive used to secure half-inch trim to the substrate.

name: Coped Joint
description: The shaped intersection where two pieces of half-inch trim meet at an inside corner.

name: Mitered Corner
description: The 45-degree angled joint where two pieces of half-inch trim meet at an outside corner.

name: Trim Backing/Substrate
description: The wall surface or framing member behind the trim that provides a nailing surface and support.

name: Crown Molding (Half-inch variant)
description: A decorative profiled half-inch trim installed at the junction between walls and ceiling.

name: Baseboard Trim (Half-inch)
description: Half-inch thick base molding installed at the junction between the finished floor and wall to cover the gap.

name: Casing Trim (Half-inch)
description: Half-inch thick decorative molding installed around door and window openings to cover the gap between frame and wall.

name: Chair Rail (Half-inch)
description: A half-inch thick horizontal molding installed midway up a wall as a protective and decorative band.

name: Picture Rail (Half-inch)
description: A half-inch thick horizontal molding with a rounded upper edge designed for hanging picture hooks.

name: Shoe Molding (Half-inch)
description: A small half-inch thick quarter-round or similar molding at the base of baseboard covering the floor expansion gap.

name: Corner Guard (Half-inch)
description: Half-inch thick protective molding installed at exterior wall corners to prevent damage.

name: Trim Installation
description: The on-site process of measuring, cutting, fitting, fastening, and finishing half-inch trim pieces to the building substrate.

name: Trim Priming and Painting
description: On-site surface preparation and application of primer and paint to half-inch trim after installation.

name: Trim Caulking
description: Application of sealant at gaps and joints between half-inch trim and adjacent surfaces for a finished appearance.

name: Scarf Joint
description: A diagonal overlapping joint used to connect two pieces of half-inch trim end-to-end along a long wall run.

name: Stadium Bench Seating
description: Continuous bench seating installed in sports venues or arenas, typically made of plastic, metal, or wood on fixed risers.

name: Individual Fixed Seat
description: Single anchored seat unit (non-folding) bolted to the floor or structure in waiting areas, lobbies, or transit spaces.

name: Bleacher System
description: Retractable or fixed tiered platform system with integrated seat boards for gymnasiums, multi-purpose halls, or outdoor fields.

name: Theater Box Seat
description: Individual compartmentalized seating area within a balcony or mezzanine level of a performance venue.

name: Seat Row Spacing Tread
description: The stepped floor tread onto which seat rows are mounted in raked seating layouts, forming part of the structural seating platform.

name: Seat Numbering & Wayfinding Plate
description: Fixed signage plate or engraved marker affixed to seating to indicate row and seat numbers for orientation and ticketing.

name: Armrest / Cup Holder Unit
description: Integrated armrest component, often with a built-in cup holder, mounted between adjacent seats in fixed seating rows.

name: Fold-down Seat Mechanism
description: Hinged seat pan and backrest assembly with a gravity-return or spring-return mechanism for self-stowing in narrow aisles.

name: VIP / Premium Seat Section
description: Designated zone within a venue featuring upgraded seats with extra legroom, wider width, or enhanced cushioning.

name: Accessible / Wheelchair Companion Seat
description: Fixed seat adjacent to a designated wheelchair space, with removable armrest to allow lateral transfer for accessibility compliance.

name: Seat Installation Activity
description: On-site positioning, leveling, and mechanical fastening of seat units to pre-installed floor anchors or riser brackets.

name: Riser & Tier Construction Activity
description: On-site forming, pouring, or assembling of stepped concrete or steel riser platforms that support rows of fixed seats.

name: Seat Anchor Point Setting Activity
description: Installation of threaded inserts, expansion anchors, or embedded plates in the floor slab at precise grid positions before seat mounting.

name: Bench Frame
description: The load-bearing structural assembly (typically metal brackets, wood beams, or concrete base) that supports the bench seat and provides anchorage to the building floor or wall.

name: Bench Seat
description: The horizontal sitting surface of the bench, typically made of wood, metal, stone, or composite planks fixed to the frame.

name: Bench Backrest
description: The vertical or angled panel attached to the frame that provides back support for seated users.

name: Bench Armrest(s)
description: Optional side supports attached to the bench frame that define seating boundaries and provide arm support.

name: Bench Leg/Base Anchors
description: Metal brackets, bolts, or embed plates that secure the bench to the building's floor slab or wall structure.

name: Freestanding Entry Bench
description: A fixed but non-structural bench unit placed in the entry zone, anchored to prevent movement but not built into the wall structure.

name: Mudroom Storage Bench
description: A combined bench-and-storage unit at the entry, fitted with cubbies, hooks, or drawers beneath or beside the seat.

name: Entry Vestibule Bench Zone
description: The designated area within the front entry lobby or vestibule where the bench is located, including required clearance and circulation space.

name: Bench Structural Support Wall
description: The building wall section that carries lateral or gravity loads from a cantilevered or wall-mounted bench system.

name: Bench-Floor Interface Trim
description: The transition molding, filler strips, or sealant at the junction between the bench base and the finished flooring material.

name: Bench Top Finish
description: The applied surface coating, stain, sealant, or upholstery layer on the bench seat and backrest.

name: Install Bench Anchorage
description: On-site installation of mechanical anchors, expansion bolts, or embed plates into the floor slab or wall to secure the bench.

name: Assemble Bench Frame On-Site
description: On-site assembly of the bench frame components including connection of brackets, cross-beams, and supports.

name: Install Bench Seat and Backrest
description: On-site fixing of the finished seat planks and backrest panels to the assembled bench frame.

name: Seal Bench-to-Building Joints
description: Application of caulking, gaskets, or trim at the interface between the bench assembly and adjacent building surfaces.

name: Fire-Rated Bench Assembly
description: A bench system constructed with fire-rated materials and sealants to maintain compartmentation integrity at exit enclosures.

name: Accessible Bench Clearance Zone
description: The designated accessible route and knee/ toe clearance area required adjacent to the bench under ADA or local accessibility codes.

name: Sitting Wall Bench
description: A built-in bench integrated into the sitting wall structure for seating.

name: Sitting Wall Cushion
description: A removable or fixed cushion pad placed on the sitting wall for comfort.

name: Sitting Wall Backrest
description: A vertical support element attached to the sitting wall providing lumbar support.

name: Sitting Wall Armrest
description: A horizontal support element attached to the sitting wall for arm support.

name: Sitting Wall Planter
description: A planting trough integrated into or adjacent to the sitting wall for greenery.

name: Sitting Wall Cladding
description: The finish surface material applied to the sitting wall for durability and aesthetics.

name: Sitting Wall Substructure
description: The concealed framing or support structure that carries the loads of the sitting wall.

name: Sitting Wall Foundation
description: The base footing or ground support system beneath the sitting wall.

name: Sitting Wall Lighting
description: Integrated light fixtures mounted within or along the sitting wall for illumination.

name: Sitting Wall Storage Niche
description: A recessed compartment built into the sitting wall for storing small items.

name: Sitting Wall Electrical Outlet
description: An integrated power receptacle installed in the sitting wall for device charging.

name: Sitting Wall Installation
description: On-site assembly and fixing of sitting wall components into position.

name: Sitting Wall Surface Finishing
description: On-site application of paint, sealant, or coating to the sitting wall surface.

name: Sitting Wall Cushion Installation
description: On-site placement and securing of cushion pads onto the sitting wall bench.

name: Sitting Wall Planter Planting
description: On-site filling and planting of integrated planter beds within the sitting wall.

name: Sitting Wall Lighting Wiring
description: On-site electrical connection and testing of integrated lighting in the sitting wall.

name: Retaining Sitting Wall
description: A sitting wall designed to also retain soil or earth on one side.

name: Freestanding Sitting Wall
description: A self-supporting sitting wall not attached to a building or other structure.

name: Curved Sitting Wall
description: A sitting wall with a curved or rounded plan layout for organic seating arrangements.

name: Terraced Sitting Wall
description: A stepped or tiered sitting wall configuration providing multiple levels of seating.

name: Heated Sitting Wall
description: A sitting wall incorporating embedded heating elements for warmth in outdoor spaces.

name: Canvas Membrane
description: The primary tensile fabric sheet forming the waterproof and UV-protective outer layer of the roof.

name: Steel Cable Network
description: The grid of tensioned steel cables that support and shape the canvas membrane.

name: Mast or Compression Strut
description: Vertical or inclined structural posts that push upward against the cable network to create the roof's curvature.

name: Edge Catenary Cable
description: Perimeter cable that anchors the free edges of the canvas membrane and transfers forces to the supporting structure.

name: Foundation Anchors (for masts)
description: Concrete or steel footings and ground anchors that restrain the tensile forces from masts and cables.

name: Perimeter Ridge or Compression Ring
description: A stiff boundary beam or compression ring at the roof perimeter that resists inward forces from the cable network.

name: Tensioning Turnbuckles and Plates
description: Adjustable hardware elements connecting cables to anchors/masts used to tension the membrane.

name: Rainwater Gutters and Downpipes
description: Collection channels and vertical pipes fitted at roof edges to drain water off the fabric surface.

name: Membrane Installation and Stretching
description: On-site unrolling, positioning, and tensioning of the canvas fabric over the cable network.

name: Cable Rigging and Tensioning
description: On-site assembly and pre-tensioning of the cable network to the specified forces before and after membrane attachment.

name: Mast Erection and Plumb Adjustment
description: Hoisting of compression masts into position, bolting to foundations, and vertical alignment.

name: Planter Box
description: A prefabricated or built-in container structure that holds soil and drainage material for raised flower planting.

name: Planter Wall
description: A retaining or freestanding wall system that encloses and supports the raised flower bed on one or more sides.

name: Drainage Layer
description: A layer of gravel, crushed stone, or proprietary drainage mat placed beneath the soil to prevent waterlogging within the raised planter.

name: Geotextile Filter Fabric
description: A permeable textile membrane placed between the drainage layer and soil to prevent fine particles from clogging the drainage system.

name: Growing Medium (Soil)
description: Engineered soil mix specifically formulated for raised planting beds to provide adequate nutrients, aeration, and drainage.

name: Irrigation System (Raised Planter)
description: A fixed drip or soaker-hose irrigation network installed within the planter to deliver water directly to the plant root zone.

name: Planter Cap/Finish Trim
description: A capping or trim piece fixed to the top edge of the planter wall to provide a finished appearance and seating surface.

name: Raised Planter Installation
description: On-site assembly, placement, and securing of planter boxes or poured-in-place planter walls at the designated building location.

name: Drainage & Waterproofing Installation
description: Installation of the drainage layer, filter fabric, and any waterproofing membrane within the planter enclosure before adding growing medium.

name: Climbing Plant Support Structure
description: Fixed framework (trellis, wires, cables, or mesh) attached to the building facade or freestanding that guides and supports climbing plant growth.

name: Green Facade Mounting System
description: Brackets, rails, and anchors that secure the support structure to the building envelope while maintaining an air gap for ventilation and moisture control.

name: Irrigation System for Green Wall
description: Built-in drip or micro-spray irrigation lines, emitters, and controllers integrated into the facade or planter to water climbing plants.

name: Planting Container/Planter
description: Fixed trough, raised bed, or modular planter box at the base of the facade housing the root zone of climbing plants, including drainage and growing medium.

name: Drainage and Waterproofing Layer
description: Waterproof membrane and drainage mat behind or beneath the planting system to protect the building fabric from moisture and root ingress.

name: Root Barrier
description: Physical membrane installed between planters and building structure to prevent root penetration into foundations or wall assemblies.

name: Growing Medium / Substrate
description: Engineered soil or lightweight mineral wool substrate in planters or modular panels that provides anchorage and nutrients for climbing plants.

name: Climbing Plant Installation
description: On-site planting, training, and initial fastening of climbing plants onto the support structure at the building facade.

name: Green Wall Support Assembly
description: On-site installation and fixing of trellis panels, cables, brackets, and mounting rails to the exterior wall structure.

name: Irrigation System Installation for Green Facade
description: On-site laying, connection, and testing of irrigation lines, drippers, and controllers within the climbing plant zone.

name: Planter Box Installation
description: On-site positioning, securing, and waterproofing of fixed planters or modular troughs at the base of the facade.

name: Stone/Paver Units
description: Individual paving stones or pavers that are laid with intentional gaps between them to form a permeable or decorative surface.

name: Joint/Gap Filler Material
description: Material such as gravel, crushed stone, sand, or fines placed in the gaps between paving stones to stabilize them and allow drainage.

name: Base/Subbase Layer
description: Compacted aggregate layer beneath the pavers that provides structural support and drainage for the paving system.

name: Edge Restraint
description: Rigid border element such as a concrete curb, metal edging, or timber restraint that contains the paving and prevents lateral movement.

name: Geotextile Fabric
description: Permeable fabric membrane placed between the subgrade and base layer to prevent soil migration and maintain drainage performance.

name: Bedding Sand Layer
description: A thin leveling course of sand or fine aggregate upon which the paving stones are bedded.

name: Stormwater Drainage Inlet
description: A grated or slotted drain component incorporated into the paving surface to collect and route excess surface water.

name: Permeable Interlocking Concrete Pavement System
description: The complete permeable paving assembly comprising pavers, gaps, base layers, and drainage designed to infiltrate stormwater on-site.

name: Paver Installation Activity
description: On-site laying and alignment of individual paving stones with specified gap widths in the prepared bedding layer.

name: Joint Filling Activity
description: On-site sweeping or placement of gravel, sand, or aggregate into the gaps between installed pavers and compacting it.

name: Base Compaction Activity
description: Mechanical compaction of the base and subbase aggregate layers to achieve required density before paver installation.

name: Edge Restraint Installation Activity
description: On-site installation and fixing of edge restraints along the perimeter of the paving area to contain the pavers.

name: Paver Pattern Layout Activity
description: On-site layout and marking of the desired paver pattern and joint alignment prior to permanent installation.

name: Soft Tile Flooring
description: Resilient floor covering made from materials like vinyl, linoleum, or rubber, installed in sheets or tiles.

name: Ceramic Wall Tile
description: Glazed or unglazed clay tiles used as a durable, water-resistant wall finish.

name: Porcelain Floor Tile
description: Dense, low-porosity ceramic tile suitable for high-traffic floor areas.

name: Mosaic Tile
description: Small tiles arranged in sheets to create decorative patterns on walls or floors.

name: Quarry Tile
description: Unglazed, extruded clay tile with high slip resistance, commonly used in commercial kitchens and utility areas.

name: Tile Backer Board
description: Cementitious or gypsum-based rigid panel installed beneath tile as a stable, moisture-resistant substrate.

name: Tile Underlayment Membrane
description: Waterproofing or crack-isolation sheet or liquid membrane placed beneath tile to protect the substrate.

name: Brick Pavers
description: Thin clay bricks laid on a sand or mortar bed for exterior pedestrian paving or interior flooring.

name: Brick Mortar Joint
description: The bed and head joints of mortar that bond individual bricks together into a masonry assembly.

name: Tile Installation Activity
description: On-site process of setting tiles in adhesive, cutting to fit, and finishing joints with grout.

name: Brick Laying Activity
